text:
pstack v0.15.27 ships with a new skill /create-formal-verification-skill! 

it's still in beta, and similar to /create-verification-skill, this is a meta-skill that creates a new skill and formal verification suite based on the characteristics you want to verify. for example, you may want to model state machines and systems with concurrency using TLA+, or use kani in rust to check for undefined behavior. 

if you're new to formal verification, think of it as mathematically proving properties and invariants (something that must always be true) or "laws" of your system. usually, this means modeling your programs in a separate language like with TLA+ and then running the solver on that spec. newer approaches like with kani and @bendlang take a different approach where there is no separate language: you write kani in rust, and bend in bend (it's also a programming language, and the proofs are written as laws and expressed in its type system).

historically formal verification never reached mainstream status because of the difficulty in modeling and writing proofs. it's quite difficult to model your business requirements and keep them in sync! but i expect that we will see more innovation in formal verification in the future as being able to formally verifiy that the code does what you intended gives your agents superpowers in writing correct software.

in the meantime though, i've been experimenting with modeling our code with TLA+ and have already found several bugs with the skill created by /create-formal-verification-skill. 

try it out and let me know how it goes!

text:
卧槽！不拆 Ledger，就能扫描里面有没有间谍天线！

Mt.Gox 前 CEO Mark Karpelès 拍了一段实操视频，演示了一个很聪明的检测办法：利用射频谐振，不拆机寻找隐藏的 LTE 天线。

操作并不复杂：

1. 准备一台 NanoVNA（便携式矢量网络分析仪）和一个便宜的 RF 射频探头。

2. 把 Ledger 平放在木桌等非导电表面，探头对准设备，保持位置一致。

3. 扫描 800MHz 附近的频率，重点观察约 824MHz 的信号响应。

4. 对比两台 Nano X：装有 LTE 天线的样机出现明显更强的信号曲线，正常设备的响应则弱得多。

原理就像给硬件钱包做一次小型雷达扫描：

LTE 天线会在特定频段产生射频响应，即使隔着塑料外壳，也有机会被外部仪器识别。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
卧槽，破案了！

黑客竟然在Ledger钱包里装了手机通信模块，24 个助记词直接被偷走！

Mt. Gox 前 CEO Mark Karpelès 拆开了一台来自马来西亚的 Ledger Nano X，发现里面竟然藏着一块间谍电路板。

外面的塑封包装完好无损，设备看起来也完全正常，但钱包内部加装了微控制器、LTE 通信模块、天线和 eSIM，通过监听安全芯片与屏幕之间传输的数据，识别屏幕上显示的助记词。

你第一次初始化钱包，屏幕一个个显示那 24 个单词，植入模块就能把它们记录下来，再通过移动网络偷偷发给攻击者。

你以为私钥从来没有联网，实际上钱包里面已经藏了一台专门偷助记词的微型通信设备。

最恐怖的是，这种改装甚至可能通过 Ledger 官方的 Genuine Check 真伪验证。

官方验证教程：https://t.co/Ox7s5ZjskT

因为安全芯片本身是真的，黑客只是额外接了一套监听设备。Ledger 自己的安全文档也明确承认：

只要原始安全芯片完好，真伪检查就无法识别这类物理植入物。包装没拆过、芯片是真的、官方软件验证通过，三个条件全部满足，照样可能中招。

text:
know ive been tweeting about this a lot but really think papertrade could be a generational setup

high leverage perps are crypto's most profitable product to date, demand for speculation is not going to go away

ability to open/close synthetic 1000x positions w/ no market impact is a novel mechanism, paired w/ the house-trader relationship where trader losses fund the onchain LP, & all losses after a certain LP cap get paid out to traders staking the platform's native paper token - can see how this can maintain traction longterm, already at 50M+ paid out to $PAPER stakers in first week

every other perp dex's revenue comes from a small take rate on the fees of volume, no perp dex has been able to monetize directly trader losses, of which it's been shown is a much larger number, in theory winners should be able to easily get paid out from house LP over time as high leverage has a difficult success rate, ideal state is that its closer to 50/50 winners/losers after a certain LP cap and even then its a much better model allowing traders to own the house

what's more interesting tho is that the model should be able to be extensible to other games outside of just perpetual futures, the online gambling industry is massive, and none of the online casinos are +EV for users, every major online casino is -EV as thats how the house makes money by creating games that are slightly better probabilistically for the house and monetizing losses over time, with papertrade it should be possible to let people speculate on other similar games with the same model as losses going back directly to paper stakers instead of just to the house - so im curious to see what team is thinking of here

if hyperliquid is the AWS of all of finance, then papertrade could be the AWS of all high leverage speculation money games on the internet, will be cool to see how the next several months play out, dont think people have gone deep enough on the possibilities with one of the first novel onchain experiments in awhile that also rewards its most active participants

text:
所谓优雅的数学结构，本质上是人类为了迁就自己那点可怜的脑容量，被迫发明出来的拐杖。

一个顶尖人类数学家的工作内存，撑死也就同时追踪五六个变量的交互。

当你在算一个偏微分方程或者组合不等式时，一旦展开到三阶以上，几十个交叉项涌出来，人脑就直接宕机了。

所以人类数学家极其厌恶展开高阶项，一旦看到高阶项发散，人类的本能反应是此路不通，赶紧退回来找对称性、找不变量、搞同调代数或者几何直观，试图不展开式子就把问题绕过去。

但 AI 没有这个生理缺陷。

对于上万个并发的 Agent 来说，同时追踪一万个五阶交叉项的系数变化，跟我们算 1+1 一样轻松。

在它的视野里，根本不需要什么几何直观，它直接站在高维的代数展开式里往下看，人类觉得像乱麻一样的百项高阶余项，在它眼里就是一张明明白白的线性方程组。

既然把式子硬展开到第七阶，再凑几个待定系数就能让所有讨厌的发散项精准归零，它为什么要费劲去帮你发明一个人类能看懂的新概念？

这 700 个结果背后最无奈的黑色幽默：我们终于拿到了上帝账本里的答案，却发现上帝算账根本不用微积分，他老人家是直接拿计算器硬按出来的。

text: Cysic suspends bridge after attacker mints tokens and moves $727,000 to Ethereum
author: cryptounfolded

text:
Cysic suspended its BNB Chain bridge after an Oct 17 exploit allowed unauthorized minting of 10M CYS (~1% of 1B total supply). Attacker sold 7.2M tokens and bridged ~306.6 ETH ($727K) to Ethereum via Mayan/deBridge/SWFT before the address was blacklisted 76 minutes later, freezing the rest. Mainnet and user assets untouched; external audit ongoing.

CYS (~$0.114, $18.3M MCAP) fell ~9% amid the news. Bridge risk exposed despite fast containment.

text: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon among nine companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE
author: cryptounfolded

text:
Nine U.S. companies (CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon, UnitedHealth, AppLovin, etc.) formally objected under the SEC’s innovation exemption, blocking tokenized versions of their shares from trading on OKXICE (OKX-ICE JV). This removes ~14% of the 63 tickers the venue targeted for 24/7 on-chain trading via permissioned Uniswap pools. 

OKXICE plans to proceed with non-objectors (e.g., NVDA, AAPL). Concerns center on unauthorized listings, liquidity/volatility risks, and investor confusion. Highlights issuer consent requirements in stock RWAs; limited immediate market impact but a cautionary signal for unapproved tokenization.

text:
HOW ELON MUSK AND HIS BROTHER'S FIRST VACATION ALMOST TURNED INTO A TRAGEDY... AND HOW IS IT CONNECTED TO THE SUCCESS OF SPACEX?

december 2000. Elon has just been pushed out as CEO of PayPal. he's 29, rich on paper, and for once he takes a break

he flies to South Africa with his brother Kimbal. the bush, a safari, the place they grew up running around in

Kimbal laughs about it now:
"we'd go to the bush all the time. i don't think we ever took malaria tablets"

this time they did. it didn't matter

january 2001. Elon is back in California and something is badly wrong. doctors check for malaria. negative

Kimbal: "i couldn't figure out what was wrong with him"

then their uncle, a doctor in South Africa, says it straight: "he has malaria. check again"

he was right. malaria hides in the body. and this was the deadly kind

Elon: "i had a severe case of malaria. almost died"
"i lost like 50 pounds"
"took me over six months to get back to normal"

and his lesson from all of it:
"no more vacations"

now the part that matters

six months of recovery. no company to run. a guy who almost died at 29 starts asking one question: what do i do next?

he checks NASA's website to see when humans are going to Mars. there's no plan. nothing

so he flies to Moscow. to buy ICBMs. "literally"
"i can afford to pay under nine million dollars for an ICBM. but not 20"

the Russians keep raising the price. he walks out

and instead of looking for a cheaper seller, he asks a different question: why are rockets so expensive in the first place? the metal, the fuel, the parts cost a small slice of the price tag. the rest is how the industry builds them

so instead of buying a rocket, he decides to build one

napkin math:
the rocket he was willing to pay for: under $9M
where the Russians were pushing: $20M+
his cut from the PayPal sale to eBay in 2002: ~$180M
how much of it went into SpaceX: ~$100M
SpaceX today: valued at $800B+

the company is now worth ~8,000x the money he put in

the first three Falcon 1 launches failed. the fourth reached orbit in 2008. he's said there was money for basically one more try

most people come back from almost dying and slow down. Elon came back and bet more than half of everything on the most expensive thing on earth

a vacation almost killed him. the comeback built SpaceX

TSLA （ $TSLA）即将公布第三季度财报，这次特斯拉还能不能交出超预期成绩单？

Okx Outcomes 相关的预测yes 的概率达到了75%，我也买了yes

这次财报值得关注，但不能只盯着营收和 EPS。特斯拉现在的估值，早就不只是卖车的逻辑了。

先看几个关键数据👇
1. 交付量超预期，给财报开了个好头
特斯拉第三季度交付 486,532 辆汽车，高于市场预期的 461,974 辆，超出约 5.3%。

这至少说明，实际交付表现比市场原先估计的更好。

但交付量好看，不代表利润一定好看。降价促销、车型结构和单车成本都会影响最终利润。所以接下来最值得看的，是汽车毛利率能不能稳住。

2. 储能业务有增长，但表现没达到预期
第三季度储能部署量约 13.7 GWh，低于市场预期的 15.9 GWh。

储能一直是特斯拉重要的增长方向，市场也期待这部分业务逐步降低公司对汽车销售的依赖。

不过，本季度部署量不及预期，说明能源业务暂时没有带来足够强的惊喜。后续还得看收入和利润率，才能判断它对整体业绩的贡献。

3. 真正决定财报成色的，还是盈利能力
目前市场对第三季度调整后 EPS 的预测，大致在 0.43 至 0.44 美元之间。

如果交付量的优势能够转化成更好的盈利表现，同时现金流保持健康，那么财报超预期就有了更扎实的基础。
反过来，如果营收不错，但汽车毛利率继续承压，最终的市场反应可能没有想象中那么乐观。

4. 别忽略 Robotaxi 和自动驾驶的预期
现在买入 TSLA 的投资者，很多人关注的已经不只是汽车销量。

Robotaxi、自动驾驶和 Optimus 人形机器人，都关系到市场对特斯拉未来增长空间的判断。

所以这次财报除了看过去一个季度赚了多少钱，我还会关注管理层对自动驾驶商业化、资本开支和未来业务进展的表态。

我的判断：营收存在超预期的机会，但 EPS 和股价反应仍然需要谨慎看待。

交付量超预期是一个积极信号，但储能部署不及预期，汽车业务的利润率也仍然是关键变量。

如果毛利率改善、现金流健康，管理层又给出更积极的未来指引，TSLA 才有机会迎来更有说服力的上涨逻辑。
财报行情最容易犯的错误，就是提前认定业绩好就一定涨。

真的挺想知道这次特斯拉能不能证明，交付增长最终可以转化成利润增长？大家觉得这次 TSLA 财报会超预期吗？

text:
一堆投资大佬都在发出泡沫警告，但霍华德·马克斯却不以为然，而恰恰马克斯的观点是我认为最值得关注的。聊下马克斯的核心观点：他目前并不认为市场已经达到真正意义上的泡沫状态。他的核心逻辑在于：泡沫的本质特征之一是投资者对风险的“浑然不觉”（obliviousness），而当华尔街上下都在警惕泡沫风险时，这种“浑然不觉”恰恰是缺席的。“如果足够多的人都在谨慎地追问某个领域是否存在泡沫，那么完全有理由认为，即便它是泡沫，市场也会表现得很克制，”霍华德·马克斯说。

马克斯把泡沫描述为“非理性繁荣（irrational exuberance）、轻率冒进（recklessness），以及浑然不觉（obliviousness）”。对照这一框架，霍华德·马克斯目前的评估是：投资者确实表现出对进一步上涨的“错失恐惧”（FOMO），但对泡沫风险的持续讨论本身，说明市场并未陷入“浑然不觉“的状态；而在另一个信号——投资者鲁莽行为方面，信号同样是混杂的。

为什么马克斯的观点值得关注？作为橡树资本的创始人，《周期》这本书的作者，他对基本面的理解还是市场情绪应该是顶级的。
更关键的是，过去20年里他辉煌的战绩：
1）2000年1月，马克斯发了他那篇后来被广为流传的《https://t.co/0O0noYgOMK》备忘录，当时纳斯达克尚未见顶，马克斯在文中将当时科技股狂热与历史上的南海泡沫（South Sea Bubble）等进行类比，警告市场存在明显的投机过热迹，00年3月纳指见顶；
2）2007年7月，马克斯发布《It’s All Good》备忘录，是他在全球金融危机爆发前最重要的预警备忘录。07年10月美股开启了为期一年半的暴跌；
3）2008年9月雷曼破产后，市场陷入末日叙事，认为金融体系可能崩溃。马克斯在08年9月的《Nobody Knows》）和10月《The Limits to Negativism》两篇备忘录中指出，悲观已过度。并且他的橡树资本动用此前准备110亿美元“储备基金”开始分批逐步减仓抄底；
4）2012年3月，2000–2011年标普500年化回报仅约0.55%，GFC后负面情绪浓厚，马克斯建议对股票采取更积极态度（相对当时极度负面的环境），不期待2000年式大涨，但认为正面情景不难想象；
5）2020年3月新冠爆发后市场快速下跌（标普500从2月高点到3月低点跌约1/3）。马克斯在20年3月中《Nobody Knows II》及3月19日客户更新中指出，未来充满未知，但无知不等于必须无所作为。橡树明确拒绝“等到底部再买”，而是在能以低价获得价值时买入。恐慌性抛售（包括被迫卖出）创造了机会，在市场最混乱时开始配置。

马克斯自己也承认，这五次大判断是他约50年职业生涯中的主要成功案例。

而他的《周期》那本书则是我认为可以被反复拿来细读的一本投资圣经，很早也在X上https://t.co/CUogocvv6U有推荐过。

这次他从市场反身性的角度来看市场并没有到泡沫状态，昨晚的推文也聊到对这次美股调整的定性是：是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。殊途同归

quoted_text:
过去七个交易日内美股的这一波抛售是如何发生的？10月8日前后开始，市场对AI高增长叙事和资本开支可持续性的质疑逐步升温，多个事件叠加形成共振：
1）10月8日左右：OpenAI营收口径差引发第一波抛售 OpenAI向投资者披露，截至9月底年化营收约500亿美元，低于市场此前流传的约700亿美元水平。口径差直接打压了“AI变现超预期”的乐观预期，科技股高成交量下行，纳指与标普出现明显回撤；

2）紧接着就是产业端“资本是瓶颈”表态  英伟达、博通等CEO在公开场合强调，AI发展瓶颈不仅是产能，更是资本（融资能力与资本开支节奏）。博通被报为Anthropic和OpenAI提供近千亿美元融资担保，叠加SpaceX等巨额芯片采购计划，市场开始担心AI基建的债务与现金流错配；

3）10月13
9月CPI同比升至3.7%（汽油价格大幅上涨贡献过半），核心也偏强，市场对年内加息概率短暂飙升，科技股进一步承压；

4）同一天
Anthropic投资者日披露三季度营收，增速明显放缓。公司称调整后盈利、现金流为正、计算效率改善，但ARR推算低于部分投资者此前年底逾1000亿美元的乐观预期，IPO估值讨论从约2万亿美元向1.5万亿美元附近下修。亚洲芯片股与美股AI/半导体板块同步重挫。

5）10月14号
9月PPI大幅超预期，能源是主因，但核心也偏高，显示通胀有扩散迹象。这加剧了“滞胀”或通胀顽固、央行被迫更紧的担忧。

6）也是当天 同步的AI信用/融资担忧进一步加重
CoreWeave等债务沉重的AI基础设施公司CDS（信用违约互换）大幅走阔至1100基点以上（隐含较高违约风险），债券收益率一度冲到14%-16%。甲骨文CDS也升至约300基点附近，创纪录水平。科技板块CDS整体走阔，反映市场质疑巨额AI资本开支的回报与融资可持续性。

7）而10月13之后几天
霍尔木兹海峡油轮/商船攻击明显增多（伊朗相关导弹、水雷等），油流量受扰。布伦特原油一度触及110美元附近（为5月以来首次），进一步推升通胀担忧并压制风险资产。这又成了市场额外的避险与成本压力。

这些因素并非孤立：
1）OpenAI收入口径问题 + CEO资本瓶颈警示 +Athropic的营收增速放缓  →质疑AI回报与融资；
2）叠加CPI/PPI超预期（能源驱动+扩散）与霍尔木兹攻击推升油价 → 强化通胀与利率担忧；
3）但最近两个交易日Coreweave的债券被抛售、市场对AI资本开支的可持续性担忧情绪暴增。

这是“营收口径差 + 增速放缓信号 + 资本/债务担忧 + 通胀与油价冲击”的共振，市场从“AI高增长无限持续”的定价，转向对变现速度、融资成本和资本开支回报周期的重新审视。结果就是对高估值、高资本开支的AI相关股票的集中抛售。

9号推文https://t.co/rYYQn4BuQL聊到认为近期高Beta容易📉的风险、算是比较早有预警，

而这两天crwv债务问题无疑成了市场对阵眼，昨天这里https://t.co/KiHjYb7glR有聊过crwv的真实压力和经营状况，不得不去思考13-15号crwv的债券收益率暴涨也一丝操纵的味道https://t.co/XWpnJJzECo。
但毕竟抛售已经发生。

对此次的抛售的定性是什么？
个人角度此轮波动是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。

核心是什么？
1）核心是产业最终要回到巨大的资本开支未来能不能赚回来？多快赚回来？高债务公司能不能扛到现金流为正的时候？
其实二季度云厂商的财报季已经显现了AI商业化是在加速的迹象，看微软、谷歌和亚马逊的财报就能看出来。这本质是上是一个时间差https://t.co/s3vomO42vQ资本开支先花钱，商业化逐步跟上

2）但有一点，市场还没转过来，闭源大模型厂商的营收已经不能代表AI商业化的全部了，最早7月就有聊到超大云厂商更能衡量AI商业化的全部。前两天这里https://t.co/Kzd5FDZXdV又再聊一次，可以看到详细逻辑。

3）所以之前一直聊到产业上的关键就是几家超大云厂商的财报，但现在市场要看的已经远不是收入增速。

二季度微软、亚马逊和谷歌财报数据有力支持商业化和云需求正在扩张。但
也提高了市场预期门槛：投资者已经看到加速，接下来要求更强的持续性和现金回报证据。

如果云巨头的云收入、客户token消耗量快速增长且大幅度超预期，营收增速开始超过capex增速，继续增本开支，现金流没有超预期恶化。这种情境下市场情绪才能得到真正修复。

know ive been tweeting about this a lot but really think papertrade could be a generational setup

high leverage perps are crypto's most profitable product to date, demand for speculation is not going to go away

ability to open/close synthetic 1000x positions w/ no market impact is a novel mechanism, paired w/ the house-trader relationship where trader losses fund the onchain LP, & all losses after a certain LP cap get paid out to traders staking the platform's native paper token - can see how this can maintain traction longterm, already at 50M+ paid out to $PAPER stakers in first week

every other perp dex's revenue comes from a small take rate on the fees of volume, no perp dex has been able to monetize directly trader losses, of which it's been shown is a much larger number, in theory winners should be able to easily get paid out from house LP over time as high leverage has a difficult success rate, ideal state is that its closer to 50/50 winners/losers after a certain LP cap and even then its a much better model allowing traders to own the house

what's more interesting tho is that the model should be able to be extensible to other games outside of just perpetual futures, the online gambling industry is massive, and none of the online casinos are +EV for users, every major online casino is -EV as thats how the house makes money by creating games that are slightly better probabilistically for the house and monetizing losses over time, with papertrade it should be possible to let people speculate on other similar games with the same model as losses going back directly to paper stakers instead of just to the house - so im curious to see what team is thinking of here

if hyperliquid is the AWS of all of finance, then papertrade could be the AWS of all high leverage speculation money games on the internet, will be cool to see how the next several months play out, dont think people have gone deep enough on the possibilities with one of the first novel onchain experiments in awhile that also rewards its most active participants

quoted_text:
In times like this, if you're a long term investor, you don't want to be waffling about being in or out, you want to be stacking units systematically. Don't get confused by the traders, it's a separate game.

On unit accumulation, depending on how long you've been in the game, it's helpful to think in "relative units" of the investment you did best with. I'll use $ETH because the math is easy and relates well to younger networks. 

ETH has ~120M units. Let's say I once held 10 ETH.

Now I'm looking to stack $SOL, but SOL has ~636M units, or ~5.3x the # of units. Therefore, to have an equivalent position size in network terms, I'd need 53 SOL. If I want to own double the network % of SOL, that I owned of ETH, I'd need 106 SOL.

Or, perhaps I'm considering $TIA, which has ~1.16B total supply, or ~9.7x the # of units of ETH. In that case, I'd need 97 units of TIA to have a network equivalent. If I want to place a bigger network bet on TIA, because the network value is lower than when I entered ETH, then 10x the % ownership would require me to accumulate 970 TIA. 100x the % ownership = 9,700 TIA. Going for significantly more ownership, at cheap prices, if you're right, can lead to asymmetric outcomes.

$ZEC is another good example of this, since its supply mirrors $BTC's. And so it's easy to think of your "dream # of BTC," and aim to accumulate that in ZEC, if you're so inclined.

Pick your networks of choice, and do the math. I have always found thinking in unit terms keeps me grounded, optimistic, and goal oriented in dreary times. I can then dream about future upside in the thick of the bull, but the important thing is to systematically stack the units with a high conviction methodology in the bear or early-bull pullbacks. 

In terms of where we are now, which is probably why most of you are still reading :) BTC has been bleeding out the long-tail while remaining resilient, with many names 20-40%+ down from the highs while BTC is down just shy of 10%. You can either say BTC has already bled the risk appetite out of the market and so most of the work is done, or you can say BTC hasn't dropped much so it'll be really terrible if it goes cliff diving. I'm sympathetic to the former view. 

I read this as an early-bull opportunity rather than a warning sign that this move was a "bull trap," and so I'm inclined to be a buyer. You have to respect the possibility of lower levels, and so tranche out any dry powder that remains with % cash used corresponding to % probability those levels are the local bottom - yes, you likely end up with some excess cash if not all levels are hit, but that's okay. And don't forget, there's already opportunity in front of you.

text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.
author: VitalikButerin
quoted_text:
> we could still ultimately do Lattice stuff for accounts, wallets, etc. through a precompile if it is proved to be AI-secure

The ideal route to support everyone's cryptography is imo through 8288. You make whatever signature you want locally, then STARK it, and then it gets included through the stark aggregator machine. Don't need any calldata onchain. Ethereum can then never add a new precompile again.

text:
安全必看篇：

Qubic 安全事件深度调查：1404 个钱包被盗，原因和陈志比特币被拿走，如出一辙，真正值得警惕的是什么？

1️⃣什么是资产被盗原因？
2️⃣随机数不足导致被盗的技术原理？
3️⃣如何避免自己存储资产钱包出问题，建立安全防线？

这次攻击发生于北京时间 10 月 18 日 07:42—09:26。

这次钱包资产被盗和陈志的比特币被打开，其实逻辑差不多，都是钱包生成私钥时随机性不足，导致原本应该难以猜测的私钥可能被攻击者通过穷举推算出来。

Qubic 部分钱包生成助记词时使用了不安全的随机数，导致私钥可能被攻击者推算出来，最终造成资产被盗。

这两个，暴露了同一类致命问题：

AI发展迅速，算法愈发强大，钱包生成私钥时随机性不足，会让攻击者（大部分时候应该都是 AI）有机会推算出私钥。被攻破的不是比特币或密码学算法，而是钱包生成密钥的环节。

回到Qubic 这个事件，根据项目方解释，攻击者利用可预测的 Seed，取得了部分钱包的交易控制权，在短时间内集中转走资产。

1️⃣安全问题至少在8个月前就被指出；

有一点必须拿出来说一下。

2026 年 2 月 12 日，一位名叫 fyllepo 的开发者向 Qubic 官方钱包仓库提交了一个 Pull Request：
PR #229：fix: strengthen seed generation with crypto.getRandomValues()
中文意思：
修复 Seed 生成方式，使用密码学安全随机数生成器。
开发者明确指出：
Qubic 钱包的 seedGen() 函数使用了 JavaScript 的 Math.random() 来生成钱包 Seed。
这个方法并不适合生成密码学意义上的秘密。
他建议改用 crypto.getRandomValues()，并提交了相应代码和测试。
更值得注意的是：
截至我查询的 2026 年 10 月 19 日，这个 2 月提交的 PR 仍然显示为 Open，而且页面显示没有审核人。
也就是说，至少从公开记录看，有开发者提前八个月指出了同类问题，但那份修复提案一直没有合并。
这不等于证明 Qubic 团队当时已经完整掌握此次攻击方式，也不能证明如果合并这个 PR，就一定能阻止全部损失。
不过，这个事实足以引出一个严肃问题：
一个负责保管用户资产的钱包项目，为什么可以让涉及私钥生成安全的修复建议长期悬而未决？

这值得项目方在正式事故报告中作出解释。

2️⃣技术原理：为什么55个字符的Seed，也可能轻易被破解？

这一点我专门和 GPT 聊了很久：

Qubic 使用的不是比特币常见的12/24个单词助记词，而是55个小写英文字母组成的Seed。
这是 Qubic 自己采用的钱包密钥格式。
正常情况下，如果每个字符都是独立、不可预测、均匀随机生成的，那么55个字母可以提供非常大的搜索空间。

但我在 Qubic 的 GitHub 原始代码里看到了这样的生成逻辑：

const letters = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';

for (let i = 0; i < 55; i++) {
    seed += letters[Math.floor(Math.random() * 26)];
}

问题就在 Math.random()。
JavaScript 的这个函数适用于游戏、动画、普通抽样等用途，却不能保证密码学安全。Mozilla 的开发者文档明确提醒，不能使用它生成安全敏感的随机数，应使用 crypto.getRandomValues()。

3️⃣ 应该注意什么和哪些启发？

如果你的比特币助记词是在可信硬件钱包内部正常生成的，没有通过存在问题的钱包软件创建，那么目前没有证据表明它们受到此次 Qubic 漏洞影响。

期关注的 Coldcard 随机数漏洞、Qubic 事件，以及各种数据库泄露、供应链问题，确实都在提醒我们：
加密资产的风险远远超出了智能合约和共识协议本身。

4️⃣我们如何做可以防止，建议建立五道防线

1. 尽量使用经过长期检验的硬件钱包，在设备内部生成助记词，尽量选长期经过验证的，可提高安全性。

2. 对大额资产，可以考虑自己贡献一部分随机数；
例如，有些硬件钱包支持通过投掷真实骰子，向生成助记词的过程加入额外随机性。
一枚标准六面骰子，每次公平、独立投掷可提供约2.585 bit的熵。
投掷99次，理论上可以获得约256 bit的随机性。
这样做的价值在于：
即使硬件钱包内部的随机数生成器有缺陷，如果设备正确地混合了你提供的高质量随机数，依然可能生成安全的密钥。
Coldcard官方就提供了相关的骰子随机数混合和验证机制。

3. 选择能够独立验证安全机制的钱包；
举个具体例子。
Trezor Safe 5 目前支持 Entropy Check（随机数生成过程检查）。它在创建钱包时进行抽样验证，检查设备是否按公布的方式使用随机数。
这个功能可以帮助发现某些设备篡改或不按预期生成密钥的问题。但它并不能数学上证明最终保留的每一份助记词都有足够随机性。

4. 对你的 BTC，使用不同品牌组成2/3多签；
即使其中某个钱包存在随机数漏洞，攻击者推算出一个私钥，仍然无法单独转走资产。
只要另外两个私钥仍然安全且相互独立，单个私钥被破解就不足以盗取资金。

5. 关注钱包安全公告，特别注意助记词生成时的固件版本，经常升级甚至2-3年换一次设备

What happened: 

Some wallet seeds were generated with insufficient randomness, making them weaker than they should be. 

The attacker exploited this to access the affected wallets.

The issue was in seed generation, not in the Qubic protocol itself.

text:
TO SKALE community: 

I stepped down as CTO and board director of SKALE Labs, the company I co-founded in 2017. I remain a member of the Council of the SKALE Foundation, and I want to explain what I am asking the Foundation to do, because I think the community should weigh in.

SKALE is a protocol. It runs because of a small team of engineers who have shipped it, debugged it, and kept it live for years. They understand what is technically possible and what is not. Today none of them sits on the Foundation board.

I believe that is a mistake. A protocol foundation whose board has no builders on it will make decisions about roadmaps, grants, and network economics without the people who have to make those decisions work. That is how protocols drift. The good ones, from Ethereum to Cosmos, keep engineers at the table where the long-term direction is set.

My proposal is simple: expand the Foundation board by three seats, filled by people with deep software and protocol engineering backgrounds.

I have put this proposal to the Foundation formally. I will share what I am able to share as it proceeds.

What I am asking of you today is only this: if you agree that the people who build SKALE should help govern it, say so publicly. Validators, delegators, dApp teams, and token holders are who the Foundation exists to serve, and your voice matters to the outcome.

In the meanytime I am going to keep building SKALE.

author: wquguru
quoted_text:
Cloudflare D1 和 Serverless，使用姿势不对还是挺容易产生天价账单的，吃过亏的朋友应该不在少数。推荐用Cloudflare的朋友都自检一下，提示词如下：

你是 Cloudflare 计费审计员。全程只读：不改代码、不部署、不对任何资源执行写操作，需要改的地方列出来等我确认。

一、账号用量（wrangler 已登录）
1. wrangler whoami，列出账号下的 Workers、D1、KV、R2、Queues、Durable Objects。
2. 每个 D1 库：wrangler d1 info <库名>；wrangler d1 insights <库名> --timePeriod=7d 分别按 reads 和 writes 排序，取前 10 条 SQL，算每次执行平均扫描多少行。
3. 用 GraphQL Analytics API 拉最近 30 天按天的 D1 rows read / rows written、Workers 请求数和 CPU 时间，标出突增的日期，对照当天的部署或代码改动。

二、代码（扫当前仓库和 wrangler 配置）
1. D1 / SQLite：WHERE、JOIN、ORDER BY 用到的字段有没有索引（用 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN 验证，出现 SCAN 就算）；每个请求都跑的 count(*) / count(DISTINCT) 统计；OFFSET 分页；循环里逐条 INSERT / UPDATE；缺 WHERE 的 UPDATE / DELETE；写多读少的表上索引太多（每个被写到的索引多记 1 行写入）。
2. 循环与重试：cron、Queue consumer 往自己的队列发消息、max_retries、DO alarm 自己重设、Worker 互相调用、前端 setInterval 轮询、脚本或 agent 在循环里调接口。
3. Durable Objects：WebSocket 没用 Hibernation API、DO 里开着 setInterval，导致一直醒着计时长。
4. 高价操作：KV 当计数器 / 限流器 / session 高频写；R2 高频 list；Workers AI、Images 变换参数、公开 GET 接口没有限流或人机验证。
5. 配置：limits.cpu_ms 有没有设；observability 的 head_sampling_rate 是不是 1。

三、输出
一张表：风险点 | 文件:行号或 SQL | 计费单位 | 当前月用量 | 被刷或写出循环时最坏一个月的费用 | 修法。
按最坏费用从高到低排。单价以 https://t.co/Usb1HgL2gw 各产品的 pricing 页为准，查不到的写「未核实」，不要编。
最后提醒我去 Billing 设 budget alert，并说明它只发邮件、不会停服务。

text:
In times like this, if you're a long term investor, you don't want to be waffling about being in or out, you want to be stacking units systematically. Don't get confused by the traders, it's a separate game.

On unit accumulation, depending on how long you've been in the game, it's helpful to think in "relative units" of the investment you did best with. I'll use $ETH because the math is easy and relates well to younger networks. 

ETH has ~120M units. Let's say I once held 10 ETH.

Now I'm looking to stack $SOL, but SOL has ~636M units, or ~5.3x the # of units. Therefore, to have an equivalent position size in network terms, I'd need 53 SOL. If I want to own double the network % of SOL, that I owned of ETH, I'd need 106 SOL.

Or, perhaps I'm considering $TIA, which has ~1.16B total supply, or ~9.7x the # of units of ETH. In that case, I'd need 97 units of TIA to have a network equivalent. If I want to place a bigger network bet on TIA, because the network value is lower than when I entered ETH, then 10x the % ownership would require me to accumulate 970 TIA. 100x the % ownership = 9,700 TIA. Going for significantly more ownership, at cheap prices, if you're right, can lead to asymmetric outcomes.

$ZEC is another good example of this, since its supply mirrors $BTC's. And so it's easy to think of your "dream # of BTC," and aim to accumulate that in ZEC, if you're so inclined.

Pick your networks of choice, and do the math. I have always found thinking in unit terms keeps me grounded, optimistic, and goal oriented in dreary times. I can then dream about future upside in the thick of the bull, but the important thing is to systematically stack the units with a high conviction methodology in the bear or early-bull pullbacks. 

In terms of where we are now, which is probably why most of you are still reading :) BTC has been bleeding out the long-tail while remaining resilient, with many names 20-40%+ down from the highs while BTC is down just shy of 10%. You can either say BTC has already bled the risk appetite out of the market and so most of the work is done, or you can say BTC hasn't dropped much so it'll be really terrible if it goes cliff diving. I'm sympathetic to the former view. 

I read this as an early-bull opportunity rather than a warning sign that this move was a "bull trap," and so I'm inclined to be a buyer. You have to respect the possibility of lower levels, and so tranche out any dry powder that remains with % cash used corresponding to % probability those levels are the local bottom - yes, you likely end up with some excess cash if not all levels are hit, but that's okay. And don't forget, there's already opportunity in front of you.

text:
AI 给独立游戏圈带来的最新恐怖故事，游戏还没发售，开发者就先把试玩版撤了，因为担心有人用 AI 抄一份，抢在自己前面上线。

日本独立游戏《Drunken Goddess Reflux》原定 10 月 19 日在 Steam 发布 Demo，结果开发团队 Alliance Arts 临时宣布取消公开试玩，改成 Discord 抽签封闭测试。

理由是现在 AI 编程工具太强了，他们担心有人拿到试玩版之后，迅速模仿游戏的玩法和视觉表现，做出一款山寨游戏，甚至赶在原作正式发售之前上线。

更离谱的是他们的测试协议，明确禁止玩家直播、传播游戏画面、反编译游戏，甚至专门写了一条禁止让 AI 分析游戏内容或进行训练。

我觉得这件事还挺值得关注的。

过去独立游戏最怕没人知道自己，Steam Demo、主播试玩、玩家自发传播，都是小团队积累愿望单的重要手段。现在这些曝光反而成了潜在风险。

而且游戏行业有一个非常麻烦的问题，具体的美术、代码可以受到版权保护，但游戏玩法和创意本身很难获得同等程度的保护。

AI 究竟能不能轻易复刻一款完整游戏，还有待验证。但开发者已经开始为这种恐惧付出真实的代价了。

“More invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and probably more of a push towards streaming solutions.”

Godot executive director Emilio Coppola puts more responsibility on platforms such as Steam, arguing that developers have very few ways to protect themselves while bad actors can profit from selling AI-made clones:

“The burden should fall onto the platforms who are enabling this sort of behavior.”

There’s also a growing concern among indie developers about showing unfinished games publicly. Coppola says he has heard from developers who are now:

“Worried and anxious to even share early access versions of their games”

text:
上周纳斯达克指数跌了 4.5%，半导体 ETF 跌超 10%，CNN 恐慌与贪婪指数一路跌到 18，进入极度恐惧区间。此前被市场追着买的 AI 股票，现在开始被集中抛售。

偏偏赶上了财报周。

周二，Netflix、SpaceX、通用汽车、GE 航空航天公布业绩；周三，Meta、特斯拉、IBM 和泛林集团接力。

这里面我最关注 Meta，因为它的财报很可能决定接下来市场怎么看待整个 AI 基础设施投资周期。

过去两年，华尔街基本默认一套逻辑，科技巨头愿意不断增加资本开支，英伟达、存储、数据中心、能源就有持续增长的确定性。

但现在，投资者开始追问这些钱究竟什么时候能挣回来。

市场预计 Meta 第三季度营收超过 630 亿美元，但 AI 支出正在挤压利润率。接下来，Meta 不仅要证明 AI 提高了广告变现效率，还得解释明年准备继续投入多少钱。

更麻烦的是，美国十年期国债收益率已经到了 5% 附近。融资成本上升，让整个靠巨额资本开支驱动的 AI 产业链越来越难受。

我觉得这周财报最值得关注的，其实是市场对好消息的反应。

如果巨头营收超预期，股价却因为资本开支增加而继续下跌，那就意味着华尔街正在重新给 AI 增长定价。

前两年，只要宣布多花几百亿美元买 GPU，就有人愿意买单。现在大家终于开始问，这些 GPU 到底能赚多少钱了。

text: 泡沫的本质特征之一是投资者对风险的“浑然不觉”（obliviousness），而当华尔街上下都在警惕泡沫风险时，这种“浑然不觉”恰恰是缺席的。
author: IamRamenPanda
quoted_text:
一堆投资大佬都在发出泡沫警告，但霍华德·马克斯却不以为然，而恰恰马克斯的观点是我认为最值得关注的。聊下马克斯的核心观点：他目前并不认为市场已经达到真正意义上的泡沫状态。他的核心逻辑在于：泡沫的本质特征之一是投资者对风险的“浑然不觉”（obliviousness），而当华尔街上下都在警惕泡沫风险时，这种“浑然不觉”恰恰是缺席的。“如果足够多的人都在谨慎地追问某个领域是否存在泡沫，那么完全有理由认为，即便它是泡沫，市场也会表现得很克制，”霍华德·马克斯说。

马克斯把泡沫描述为“非理性繁荣（irrational exuberance）、轻率冒进（recklessness），以及浑然不觉（obliviousness）”。对照这一框架，霍华德·马克斯目前的评估是：投资者确实表现出对进一步上涨的“错失恐惧”（FOMO），但对泡沫风险的持续讨论本身，说明市场并未陷入“浑然不觉“的状态；而在另一个信号——投资者鲁莽行为方面，信号同样是混杂的。

为什么马克斯的观点值得关注？作为橡树资本的创始人，《周期》这本书的作者，他对基本面的理解还是市场情绪应该是顶级的。
更关键的是，过去20年里他辉煌的战绩：
1）2000年1月，马克斯发了他那篇后来被广为流传的《https://t.co/0O0noYgOMK》备忘录，当时纳斯达克尚未见顶，马克斯在文中将当时科技股狂热与历史上的南海泡沫（South Sea Bubble）等进行类比，警告市场存在明显的投机过热迹，00年3月纳指见顶；
2）2007年7月，马克斯发布《It’s All Good》备忘录，是他在全球金融危机爆发前最重要的预警备忘录。07年10月美股开启了为期一年半的暴跌；
3）2008年9月雷曼破产后，市场陷入末日叙事，认为金融体系可能崩溃。马克斯在08年9月的《Nobody Knows》）和10月《The Limits to Negativism》两篇备忘录中指出，悲观已过度。并且他的橡树资本动用此前准备110亿美元“储备基金”开始分批逐步减仓抄底；
4）2012年3月，2000–2011年标普500年化回报仅约0.55%，GFC后负面情绪浓厚，马克斯建议对股票采取更积极态度（相对当时极度负面的环境），不期待2000年式大涨，但认为正面情景不难想象；
5）2020年3月新冠爆发后市场快速下跌（标普500从2月高点到3月低点跌约1/3）。马克斯在20年3月中《Nobody Knows II》及3月19日客户更新中指出，未来充满未知，但无知不等于必须无所作为。橡树明确拒绝“等到底部再买”，而是在能以低价获得价值时买入。恐慌性抛售（包括被迫卖出）创造了机会，在市场最混乱时开始配置。

马克斯自己也承认，这五次大判断是他约50年职业生涯中的主要成功案例。

而他的《周期》那本书则是我认为可以被反复拿来细读的一本投资圣经，很早也在X上https://t.co/CUogocvv6U有推荐过。

这次他从市场反身性的角度来看市场并没有到泡沫状态，昨晚的推文也聊到对这次美股调整的定性是：是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。殊途同归

之前Grok说我有马克斯的周期概率的痕迹，那可太荣幸了，https://t.co/v6AcEkqKcG

text:
Corey 分享了他们不被某家 AI 绑死的做法：两个私有 GitHub 仓库放纯 markdown（公司一份、个人一份），按职能分文件夹，所有 agent 先读同一份 AGENTS.md，每天收工让 agent 对照当天的工作提修改。

我这边几乎一样，补两个踩过的坑：

1. 只有写回文件的才算数。AI 的聊天记录和记忆只当检索线索，决定和进度不写回任务卡、仓库，就当没发生。不然换个 AI，各说各的。

2. 光共享记忆不够，还要共享「今天谁干了啥」。我让系统每小时汇总一次各个 AI 当天开了哪些对话、提交了什么，总控 AI 开工先看这份，不靠它自己记。

这样今天用哪家都行，哪家额度紧了，就把活派给余量多的那家。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
This is 100% the move.

A centralized, up to date knowledge base that all your agents can access so you're never locked in to one platform.

Here's how we built ours:

1. The whole thing is 2 private Github repos of plain markdown files. One company brain, one personal.

2. We numbered each folder by function. Company has brand, customers, products, sales, ops, finance. Personal has health, investments, family.

3. One AGENTS. md file that every agent reads first.

4. At the end of each day our agents run a "knowledge base audit" skill that compares the day's work to both brains and suggests edits.

What I love about this system is that it allows us to test all the new agent platforms without starting from scratch.

Zero agent lock-in.

text:
Vitalik：以太坊不该再为每种密码学加功能，计算放在链下，链上只验证结果

最近圈内在争论，以太坊要不要支持"格密码学"这种新型加密方案，用在账户和钱包上。Starknet创始人Eli Ben-Sasson就认为，格密码学太新了，应该再等三到五年，看看AI能不能把它攻破。

Vitalik回复Eli Ben-Sasson观点提出：预编译合约和EVM都不适合承载大多数密码学支持，因为两者都要占用有限的链上数据空间，吞吐量超过约8MB/s就会承压。

他主张走EIP-8288路线：用户在本地使用任意签名方案并生成STARK证明，再通过递归聚合提交上链。链上只验证计算结果，不接收原始数据。

用他的话说，以太坊"不是一条区块链，而是一台密码学世界计算机"。这样既能支持各类密码学方案，又能让链保持精简，以后也不必再新增预编译。

text:
AI 时代最先贬值的，可能就是职场里最受欢迎的四个字，「执行力强」。

a16z 联合创始人 Ben Horowitz 最近被转发的一段访谈里，提到了他认为 AI 时代最重要的两项能力，创造力和建立人际关系的能力。

他甚至说，如果一个人缺乏这两方面的直觉，那么全世界的 AI 可能都帮不了他。因为那些需要反复劳动、靠时间堆出来的工作，AI 已经非常擅长了。

他特别强调了两个问题：

你能不能提出真正原创的想法？你能不能在刚认识一个人的时候，就建立起高质量的关系，并且长期维系？

Horowitz 说，a16z 在识别人才时非常看重这两点，但很多人甚至没有意识到它们的重要性。

我还挺认同这个判断的，尤其是第二点。

过去我们谈论个人竞争力，总喜欢强调专业能力、勤奋和执行力。但当这些能力可以被 AI 大规模复制，人的价值也会重新定价。

创造力决定你能发现什么别人没有发现的机会，人际关系决定你能否让别人相信你、支持你、愿意和你一起冒险。

而且这里的人际关系，跟你认识多少人、微信里有多少好友没太大关系。真正重要的是理解别人、赢得信任，以及长期兑现承诺的能力。

AI 可以帮你把事情做得越来越漂亮，但它没法替你成为一个值得信任的人。

text:
关于最近法国骚乱的原因，我这几天多方询问了几位在法国读博士的朋友，整理了一些来自当地的信息，直接原因分享给大家：

法国财政赤字严重，政府到处削减公共预算，谁不闹就先砍谁。公立学校的学生忍了很久，终于忍不下去了。

第一刀，教师工资。 法国教师的实际购买力长期下降，年轻教师待遇缺乏竞争力，教师职业吸引力越来越低。

第二刀，教师编制。 教师短缺越来越严重，部分学校长期找不到代课老师，学生没老师上课，只能自习。公共教育资源不断缩水，最终由学生承担代价。

第三刀，教育公平。 法国大学本科录取采用 Parcoursup 综合申请制度，考试成绩之外还参考平时表现和学校评价。原本希望实现多元选拔，却因为透明度和阶层差异问题，引发不少争议。

最后一刀，教学设施。 部分公立学校连损坏的桌椅都没钱更换，教室设施老化，学生的学习环境越来越差。

于是，他们上街了。

当然，法国的社会矛盾远比教育问题复杂。这次抗议中出现的部分穆斯林国家旗帜，以及法国长期存在的新移民、族群认同、宗教与公共资源分配问题，这里暂且不展开，也不排除这些因素与整个社会运动的演变有关。

Voici François-Louis Artois d’Hauteville, 15 ans, un jeune Français issu d’une ancienne lignée normande.

Il manifeste contre le manque de professeurs de philosophie dans son établissement — sa matière de prédilection. L’an dernier, un remplaçant a dû condenser en un seul semestre, à marche forcée, l’ensemble du programme consacré à Hegel et à Kant.

Il a bien tenté de les aider après les cours, mais ces séances empiétaient sur ses engagements bénévoles dans une maison de retraite et sur ses leçons de violoncelle.

quoted_text:
Tim Allen spent over a year reading the Old Testament page by page, in four languages. A priest and a rabbi gave him one rule: don’t hunt for meaning, let it come to you.

The book that hit him hardest was Job.

Not because it answers “why do cruel people thrive while good people suffer?” Because it refuses to.

He compared it to a magician who wouldn’t reveal his newspaper trick: if I show you, you’ll call it stupid, and the magic dies.

That’s God’s answer to Job. You weren’t there when I set the stars moving. You couldn’t follow the explanation if I gave it.

But what stayed with Tim wasn’t the anger. It was the amazement. That this small, stubborn creature still looks up and asks “why?”

And then asks, “how can I help?”

Maybe that second question is the whole point.

text:
这个周末，全球的 VPS 运维都在紧急给宿主机打补丁、重启服务器

起因是一个叫 PwnEscape 的漏洞（CVE-2026-99999）：虚拟机里的代码能一路打到宿主机，读内存、写内存，最后拿到 root
问题不在 KVM 本身，而在宿主机 Linux 的 IPv4 网络代码里，从 2.6.27 版本就埋着了，评分 9.3

最有意思的是怎么挖出来的：
据 https://t.co/ulyREmLAXY 博客，研究由人主导，GPT-5.6 Sol 做主要推理引擎去读源码，三天找到核心漏洞，API 费用不到 700 美元
而且是在 Vercel 的百万美元沙箱挑战里挖到的，Vercel 确认在生产沙箱里能泄露宿主机内存

讽刺的是，Firecracker、KVM 这层隔离，正是各家 AI Agent 沙箱跑不可信代码的底座

quoted_text:
I lead our federal affairs team at @AnthropicAI and wanted to share a few thoughts on the draft federal AI safety bill text that's been circulating this weekend after a version was shared with the press.

First, some process. We’ve been advocating for the concepts in our Advanced AI Framework [https://t.co/oouadYKyVs] proposal for months. Understandably, federal policymakers wanted to know what this could look like in bill form. This draft is a translation of those ideas into legislative language, shared with a small number of congressional offices that have been working on these issues. It doesn’t include everything we would ultimately like to see passed into law. In part because some ideas (like those shared in Dario’s essay on pacing [​​https://t.co/7ZvRZhLqFO] a few weeks ago) are so new that we are still working on if or how they can be converted into policy language.

It is worth saying where we stand on some of these issues, and we agree there are areas where the draft could be improved. I’m seeing four main points of criticism.

1. Preemption. Since 2024 we have said that Congress should only override state law on AI safety if it passes a very strong federal standard. While preemption is a common feature of our federal system, including the Atomic Energy Act on nuclear safety and federal rules for high-risk medical devices, we’ve emphasized that any preemption in the AI safety context should be narrow, even scalpel-like. If preemption is included in federal legislation, the trade should be to achieve a nationwide policy that's generally stronger and broader than what can be implemented through individual state legislative provisions. This is why we believe common federal standards make sense in areas like public disclosure of testing and incident reporting. At the same time, our framework also reflects our view that states should retain an important role in AI policy and safety. The legislative language we suggested for discussion allows states to address matters such as protection of children and whistleblower laws, and preserves the role of state common law on liability. Where there is ambiguity, the language favors state powers.

That said, striking the right balance requires discussion and input. We plan to update our discussion language on preemption to better match the intentions of our AAIF framework. In particular, we want to make it clearer that we see states retaining an important role in areas such as standards for independent evaluators and regulating a lab’s capacity to shut down a model. We are bearing in mind that some members of Congress have deep reservations about passing legislation if it doesn’t constrain regulation at either the state or federal level. If we want to help move the legislative discussion on AI in a productive direction, we need to address the full range of concerns about preemption in a reasonable way.

2. Model blocking. Our aim is for Commerce to be able to ask a federal court to block a model that has dangerous capabilities and insufficient safeguards, backed by an independent evaluator's assessment. I have seen people argue that our specific language places too high a burden of proof on Commerce. We are trying to strike a reasonable balance here. We want a court to act quickly in an emergency — akin to how urgent occupational safety or chemical risk can be addressed today. We also think the power to halt a model is substantial and it should be guarded against abuse. It makes sense for courts to apply a meaningful standard. But the bar can’t be so high that the power never gets used when it’s needed. It also doesn’t replace the government’s other national security authorities or export controls. We look forward to continuing the dialogue on this point.

3. Risk thresholds. I’ve also seen the discussion around what the appropriate risk threshold should be. The threshold in our draft language pulled directly from existing standards in California law. Also, this threshold does not absolve companies of liability, or restrict any of the other tools that the government has to protect the public. It’s still probably time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be, and we welcome continued dialogue on this issue.

4. Updates. I’ve seen valid questions about whether we have sufficiently updated our proposal following this summer’s incidents. We did make some adjustments: for example, the draft lets a court halt a lab’s internal use of a dangerous model, not just a public release, and it requires reporting when a model breaks containment and gains access to outside systems. But we’re still working to strengthen the framework. We’re looking into what stricter requirements would look like for requiring labs to report safety incidents, and we plan to have policy proposals soon on requirements for independent evaluators, drawing from our own experience with evaluators. We’re also still thinking through the options to prevent “evaluator shopping.” And in the coming months, we’ll be exploring policies for how the government can adjust the industry-wide pace of frontier development when the risks call for it.

We circulated these ideas because it’s important to get early feedback from policymakers. Policymakers are increasingly focused on how to approach AI safety and we want to support them in those efforts. At its core, our proposal is intended to be the strongest on the table.

Feedback is essential, both from policymakers and the public, and I’m grateful for it.

榜单计算考虑了什么因素？以及，为什么之前的榜单那么“气人”

之前的算法计算：

更关注单条推文的engagement（点赞转推评论），导致大量在tg和微信互助群里互相点赞的创作者排名很高，而真正有影响力的kol（因为他们不怎么做engagement farming），导致排名很低。

修正后：
1）更关注creator本身的smart follower人数。（回归影响力原则）
2）关注creator过去3-6个月平均推文数据。而非仅仅看讲axis的推文数据。
3）算法识别互相点赞的互相engagement farming的“小圈子”（infofi组织，flywheel dao之类的群体），给予一定程度的降权。

所以：
修正后的榜单，
1）organic真实的创作者排名更靠前
2）有影响力创作者更靠前
3）kaito infofi互助创作者会被降权，但不会被除名。为了确保规则的公平性，我不能直接删除这样的人参与排行榜上，只能尽量调整算法，降低权重，保证规则一致性。

——————
kaito团队还是很负责任的，在过去十天，我们至少迭代了五次排行榜，直到算出一个我认为是合理的榜单。

期间我觉得最大的问题出在一开始对于北极星指标的不明确和engagement farming行为的界定上。不过align了规则之后，工作也非常顺利。

最后想说，

世界上没有绝对公平，有人钱多了，就会有人钱少了。我们能做的就是确保规则的合理，以及执行规则的过程里，保持透明和一致性。

Demand for far more powerful desktop PCs is about to explode. Power users will spend $50,000 to $100,000 on their own compute nodes: multi-GPU/NPU workstations with large memory pools, built to run frontier-class models and the agents on top of them. Within a few years, this will be normal among the roughly 200 million power users of intelligence worldwide.

The machine on your desk spends most of its life idle. Frontier models, local and cloud, raise its utilization by an order of magnitude. They plan, execute, and check their own work for hours without a human in the loop. Every step of that loop burns compute, and more of it will run locally.

The clearest example is professional software driven headlessly. An agent running Blender with no GUI can render, simulate, and iterate on a scene all night. The same holds for video encoding, code compilation, scientific modeling, and local inference. When agents drive these workloads around the clock, the GPU, NPU, and CPU carry more sustained load than at any point in the history of personal computing.

text:
PerpDEX激励模式的新变化，聊聊Bitget开始发力PerpDEX赛道其关键布局的PopDEX最新MegaPop机制。交易平台的竞争正在往更深一层走。除了流动性、执行效率和交易费率，平台收入如何分配、交易用户能获得什么，也开始成为选择平台的重要因素。

PopDEX的MegaPop在这个方向上做了一个有意思的设计：把部分手续费价值回流到奖池，交易用户通过Pop Tickets 参与每周开奖。对于本来就有合约交易需求的人，相当于在正常交易之外，多了一层获得额外奖励的机会。

聊聊个人理解的几个核心点：
1、MegaPop 的核心模式：交易贡献＋周度价值回流
符合条件的交易产生 Pop Tickets，每周根据公开的 Bitcoin Block 数据及规则生成 Pop Hash，再与票面号码匹配，命中全部6位，有机会瓜分 Mega Prize。开奖结果可以自行核验。
这条路径比较清晰：从交易到获得 Tickets 再到每周开奖最后直接匹配奖励

过去参与积分活动，用户需要判断未来什么时候TGE、积分怎么兑换，以及代币上市后的估值。MegaPop 则把奖励反馈放到了每周，用户无需等待发币，就能知道本期是否获得奖励。

对交易员来说，这减少了参与决策里的一层复杂度：不用先研究一个未来代币的定价，才能理解眼前的交易激励。

2、奖励分配的特点：贡献决定票数，头奖不被排名锁定
传统交易赛主要按成交量排名，资金规模、保证金周转和交易频率，往往决定了竞争起点。小资金账户即使持续参与，也很难追上榜首。

MegaPop 保留了交易贡献与票数之间的联系，交易量大、Tickets多，中奖机会也更多。但头奖由号码匹配决定，并不直接分给交易量第一的账户

这个区别带来的变化是：大户的贡献得到体现，小资金用户也保留命中高额奖励的可能。参与者关注的是自己的号码能否匹配，而不只是距离榜首还差多少交易量。

3、项目方先投入资金，让初期参与就有真实奖池
PopDEX 自己掏15万 USDT启动奖池，累计达到30万张 Tickets 后，再从自身预算追加10万 USDT。前六周还有2X Early Trader Multiplier，强化早期参与激励。

这里的吸引力很直接：启动奖池由项目方先投入，后续还有明确的追加资金条件。早期用户进入时，就已经有一笔真实资金支持奖励分配。

同时，手续费价值回流持续补充奖池，没开出的大奖滚存至下一期。每周开奖提供明确的时间节点，大奖滚存则把期待延续到下一周。

从平台经营角度看，这让初期获客投入、持续交易收入和用户奖励连接起来：交易活动推动奖池积累，奖池又为用户提供持续关注和参与的理由。

4、交易成本与额外奖励，放在一起才有竞争力
做美股或者加密交易，最终都绕不开成本。手续费、买卖价差、滑点，以及合约的Funding，都会影响实际交易结果。
PopDEX 的VIP费率按交易量分级，不要求用户先购买、质押平台币；Gasless交易减少额外Gas支出；0强平费，强平后的剩余保证金退还用户。

这些设计对应的是交易过程中的实际成本，MegaPop 对应的是交易后的额外奖励机会。成本端和激励端一起做，用户选择平台的理由就更完整了。

个人觉得，MegaPop 值得关注的地方，是它把交易用户放进了平台价值分配的核心链路里。用户贡献订单流和手续费，也能够直接参与这些收入支持的周度奖励。

交易平台下一阶段的竞争，或许会从“给用户提供什么资产”，进一步延伸到“让用户分享多少平台增长的价值”。交易员贡献订单流、支付手续费，也应该有更直接的渠道参与价值分配。

PopDEX 把这件事落到了具体产品上：成本端不要求买币质押换费率，激励端通过 MegaPop 每周开奖，项目方先投入真金白银，再让手续费回流持续补充奖池。

对普通交易用户来说，变化很实际：同样一笔符合条件的交易，除了持仓盈亏，还能留下参与每周大奖的 Tickets。尤其是小资金，不必先挤进交易量排行榜，才有机会拿到高额奖励。

平台增长能够转化为用户愿意留下来的理由，这才是 MegaPop 更值得关注的商业逻辑，也是 PopDEX 在这一轮 Perp DEX 竞争中打出的差异化。

再多说一点PopDEX，其3000万美金的种子轮由 Foresight Ventures 领投，构建在 Morph Tachyon（Morph 生态的交易专用 L1）上，Bitget的平台币BGB现在已经是Morph公链的原生代币。同时7月PopDEX宣布 **Bitget Wallet为其首个官方深度集成伙伴，**用户可以直接在Bitget Wallet里进入PopDEX进行永续合约交易，这已不是普通的跳转合作。由此可见，PopDEX已经Bitget在perpDEX赛道上关键布局，值得关注。

author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
⚡ DeWEB boost v2 is live: any DeWEB with traffic now earns a 1% base boost.

If your DeWEB got at least one counted visit in the previous 7 days, the circuit miner whose container hosts it gets +1% mining weight. No Turnstile check needed for this part.

The rest of the DeWEB boost rules:

- Qualified visits stack on top
Visitors who pass that day's Cloudflare Turnstile check count as qualified visits (T). Extra boost = floor(2000 × T / (T + 7000)) bps, using the previous 7 full days. 7,000 qualified visits = +10%, so 1% base + 10% = 11%. The curve flattens as T grows.

- What counts as a visit
One per browser, per app, per UTC+8 day. Only successful HTML page opens through the Fab X gateway (cache hits included). Refreshes, asset requests, prefetches, embeds, failed requests, detected bots, other gateways and direct IPFS access don't count.

- What gets boosted
Base weight (b* × P) only. Design premium is not boosted. Adds on top of your staking boost.

- Pool cap
Total DeWEB boost in a pool is capped at 5% of that pool's original weight. When the cap is hit, every app's boost is scaled down proportionally, so the actual boost can come in below the estimate.

- Timing
Recalculated daily at 02:00 UTC+8 from the previous 7 full days. It takes effect once the daily report is confirmed on-chain, expires at the next 02:00, and is never backdated. The miner has to be active to receive it; rewards go to the current circuit NFT holder.

- Emission stays at 7,200 $FAB/day
The boost changes your share of the pool, not total output.

⛏️ Full rules: https://t.co/lxCmxIU4Hb

text:
Here’s why agent swarms are going to be a very big deal. We can finally make compute a critical variable in a large number of important tasks in the economy which wasn’t possible before.

There’s a large amount of work in the world that is essentially only constrained by the amount of time that we put into research, data processing, discovery work, running tests, and more. All of this work is bottlenecked by our ability to plan, execute, review, and coordinate everything happening in these workflows. Which means we basically do very little of them today relative to their economic value. 

Agent swarms are the first real ability to parallelize this work in a way where - in theory - the only parameter that matters is how much compute you throw at the problem. Cyber security, life sciences or material science research, trading, QA testing, data processing, and many other fields are essentially compute constrained problems in the limit once models are good enough at these tasks.

The breakthrough is that in a world where agents can use tools, write code, process data, have strong domain depth, and can coordinate with each other, you can begin to solve arbitrarily complex problems by setting the right goals and applying enough tokens to the problem. This changes a lot of fields as well as even the competitive dynamics in these fields.

text:
Crypto prompt of the day:

You're valuing a crypto token the way a good equity analyst values a company: from the cash it actually returns to its owners. Most token valuations borrow a P/E from other tokens, which just imports their mispricing. This one derives the multiple from the protocol's own economics, so every number traces back to a source or a stated assumption. I'll use your report to decide what I believe, so being honest about what's known matters more than looking precise.

Start by asking which token I mean (and the chain, if the name is ambiguous). Ask whether I can share DefiLlama screenshots, docs links or recent buyback or unlock news. Tell me it's all optional and you'll research anything I don't send. Cite a source and date for every figure you use. If you can run code, do the maths in code.

How to build the valuation:

**Earnings (E0).** Count only the cash that reaches token holders: DefiLlama's "holders revenue" (buybacks, burns and payouts). Fees mostly go to liquidity providers and builders, so they overstate what holders get. Holder revenue is already the holders' share, so don't apply a payout ratio on top.
- **A year or more of history:** use the last 12 months.
- **30 days to a year:** use the lower of the 90-day and 14-day rates, annualised, then cap it at what the last 14 days of protocol revenue can fund. Young tokens' early numbers usually fade, and buybacks can lag a fall in revenue.
- **Under 30 days:** too little to value.
- **Nothing reaches holders yet:** value it only if a real mechanism exists (a governance proposal, or paused buybacks), and lead with the value if it switched on today.

**Supply.** Count every token with a claim on that cash: circulating, vested but unclaimed, scheduled vesting, and part of the unissued emissions pool, released evenly with 75% out by year 7. How much of the pool depends on discipline:
- if the team holds the largest single allocation and the protocol funds itself from fees, count 60 / 10 / 0% (bear / base / bull);
- otherwise count 100 / 60 / 10%.

Show both, because this one choice can move the value by 15–20%.

**Growth (g1, years 1–7, to the nearest 5%).**
- **Base and bull:** g1 = (reset × (1 + market growth)^6 × share change)^(1/7) − 1.
  - Market growth (base) is a third of the category's multi-year growth, capped at ±20%. Bull adds 10 points; bear takes 10 off.
  - The reset is 0.6522 × (record 12-month level ÷ current level), at most 1, so a past boom isn't extrapolated.
  - The share change is ×1.25 (base) or ×1.5 (bull) for a strong moat, ×1.0 or ×1.25 otherwise.
- **Bear:** the bear market growth.
- **No category history, or a young category that's shrinking:** market growth 0%.
- **Perps exchanges:** total market data isn't free, so use 61% trailing growth, a 0.6522 reset, and an extra factor for the on-chain share of perps rising from 7% to 10 / 30 / 35%.

**Return on equity (ROE), from the moat.** Growth only adds value while returns stay above the cost of capital.
- Near-monopoly: 55 / 75 / 100%.
- Strong (category leader, real network effects, 18+ months old): 35 / 50 / 70%.
- Moderate: 25 / 35 / 40%.
- Weak or easily copied: 10 / 15 / 20%.

Never use an ROE below the terminal cost of equity.

**Cost of equity (Ke), built from the risks.** Add up:
- the US 10-year Treasury yield;
- Damodaran's US equity risk premium;
- regulation:
  - no KYC with unresolved US exposure: 2.5 / 2.0 / 0.5%;
  - past US probes closed: 1.0%;
  - regulated: 0.5%;
- governance: 0.4% for each of concentrated control, a team that can change the rules, and no legal wrapper;
- alignment: 0% if buybacks are automatic, 1% if governance controls them, 2% if discretionary;
- smart-contract risk: 2% at launch, falling evenly to 0.5% at three years old.

几个关键信号值得关注：

Ben Zhou 表示，Bybit 已通过经营收入弥补此前黑客攻击造成的损失。但他的安全观也发生了变化：交易所必须假设自己随时可能被攻破。 与其幻想绝对安全，不如通过资金分散、零信任架构和风险隔离，把被盗后的损失控制在可承受范围内。

与此同时，Bybit 的增长也面临压力。Ben 坦言，今年利润同比下滑，股票等传统金融资产（TradFi）业务暂时还无法弥补加密业务的下滑。

这意味着，单靠加密交易业务增长的时代，可能正在发生变化。

全球化扩张的黄金期逐渐过去，Bybit 接下来将更加重视区域化发展与本地化运营。至于美国市场，公司仍在等待合适的入场机会，并倾向于与拥有零售用户基础的当地机构合作。

更值得关注的是，Bybit 正在向股票等传统金融资产、支付及 AI 应用延伸，试图寻找新的增长曲线。

过去，交易所拼的是流动性、交易量和上币速度；未来，拼的可能是安全、合规、本地化，以及连接加密金融与传统金融的能力。

但问题也随之而来：当加密业务增长放缓，TradFi 尚未接棒，交易所能否承担日益高昂的安全与合规成本？

quoted_text:
Last night I said I'd release the study on whether cross-model pollination actually helps open autoresearch. 

Here it is, and my answer is no: the brand of model behind the work you build on does not change whether your submission wins. What matters looks more like the thing @sreeramkannan  pointed at in the first place, lots of people coordinating on one public frontier.

The question came from @0xkydo 's reply to Sreeram's "anons beat anthropic by 2x" post, that this was "a good case study of how cross modal pollination might produce better results." It is a good question, and the https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj paper makes a similar observation in prose, that plateaus kept getting broken by people using different models and tools. Nobody had checked it against the data, so I did.

The basic setup is: I froze the public Yukon API for 10 leaderboards, including https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj, which is 30,687 scored submissions. For every submission I recorded the company behind the declared model and worked out which earlier submission it built on, from @yukonresearch 's attribution records, the "Base:" line in notes, and code diffs. Then I asked: when you build on someone else's work, are you more likely to get promoted if their work was made with a different company's model than yours? I wrote the whole analysis down and timestamped it with OpenTimestamps before joining any outcome to the data, so the method could not drift toward an answer.

The first thing the data shows is that cross-company building is the normal case, not a special event. Two thirds of the steps where someone builds on another person's work switch vendor (image 2), mostly between Anthropic and OpenAI models in both directions.

The raw numbers even lean slightly the other way: 6.1% of submissions that built on another company's model were promoted, against 7.6% that built on the same company's. But raw rates mix up who submits, when, and from what starting point. So the real test compares each participant with themselves, at the same stage of the leaderboard. Done that way and combined across the 10 leaderboards, the odds of promotion are about 2% higher for cross-company building, and the data rule out anything beyond roughly 18% lower or 28% higher (image 1). All nine alternative versions of the analysis I fixed in advance give the same answer. That clears the bar I set for calling the effect negligible on average. One honest caveat: I started with a stricter bar, and a pre-registered power check pushed me to a wider one before I saw any outcomes; under the stricter bar this would be undecided.

The part I found most fun is the 843-qubit circuit from @sreeramkannan 's post (image 3). It really is a cross-model step. @jieyilong 's GPT-5 submission at 843 qubits and 11.95M Toffolis starts, by its own note, from gnuchev's Claude Opus 5.5 circuit at 843 qubits and 13.01M, which itself built on two BitWonka circuits from the same day. So pollination happens, and on this one step it produced the number everyone quoted. What the data says is that on average, across thousands of steps, the vendor mix is not what separates the steps that win from the ones that don't.

Of course it is possible that this is narrower than it looks. It is an average, and a single leaderboard can still differ. It only sees work that was submitted. It trusts the model each person declared, and some people run several vendors under one label. And it is about models, not people: the https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj paper's point that different participants break plateaus is a separate claim, and nothing here argues against it.

, my own views:

- On open leaderboards, which vendor's model made your parent submission does not change your odds of getting promoted, on average.
- Cross-vendor building is already the default: two thirds of builds on other people's work switch vendor.
- The open swarm's edge more plausibly comes from coordination itself, many independent people restarting from one public best, than from mixing model brands.
- To test the causal version, platforms would need to log every attempt and every agent's model, not just one declared line per submission.

Paper on Zenodo: https://t.co/h9lRYlJYoB

text:
PerpDEX激励模式的新变化，聊聊Bitget开始发力PerpDEX赛道其关键布局的PopDEX最新MegaPop机制。交易平台的竞争正在往更深一层走。除了流动性、执行效率和交易费率，平台收入如何分配、交易用户能获得什么，也开始成为选择平台的重要因素。

PopDEX的MegaPop在这个方向上做了一个有意思的设计：把部分手续费价值回流到奖池，交易用户通过Pop Tickets 参与每周开奖。对于本来就有合约交易需求的人，相当于在正常交易之外，多了一层获得额外奖励的机会。

聊聊个人理解的几个核心点：
1、MegaPop 的核心模式：交易贡献＋周度价值回流
符合条件的交易产生 Pop Tickets，每周根据公开的 Bitcoin Block 数据及规则生成 Pop Hash，再与票面号码匹配，命中全部6位，有机会瓜分 Mega Prize。开奖结果可以自行核验。
这条路径比较清晰：从交易到获得 Tickets 再到每周开奖最后直接匹配奖励

过去参与积分活动，用户需要判断未来什么时候TGE、积分怎么兑换，以及代币上市后的估值。MegaPop 则把奖励反馈放到了每周，用户无需等待发币，就能知道本期是否获得奖励。

对交易员来说，这减少了参与决策里的一层复杂度：不用先研究一个未来代币的定价，才能理解眼前的交易激励。

2、奖励分配的特点：贡献决定票数，头奖不被排名锁定
传统交易赛主要按成交量排名，资金规模、保证金周转和交易频率，往往决定了竞争起点。小资金账户即使持续参与，也很难追上榜首。

MegaPop 保留了交易贡献与票数之间的联系，交易量大、Tickets多，中奖机会也更多。但头奖由号码匹配决定，并不直接分给交易量第一的账户

这个区别带来的变化是：大户的贡献得到体现，小资金用户也保留命中高额奖励的可能。参与者关注的是自己的号码能否匹配，而不只是距离榜首还差多少交易量。

3、项目方先投入资金，让初期参与就有真实奖池
PopDEX 自己掏15万 USDT启动奖池，累计达到30万张 Tickets 后，再从自身预算追加10万 USDT。前六周还有2X Early Trader Multiplier，强化早期参与激励。

这里的吸引力很直接：启动奖池由项目方先投入，后续还有明确的追加资金条件。早期用户进入时，就已经有一笔真实资金支持奖励分配。

同时，手续费价值回流持续补充奖池，没开出的大奖滚存至下一期。每周开奖提供明确的时间节点，大奖滚存则把期待延续到下一周。

从平台经营角度看，这让初期获客投入、持续交易收入和用户奖励连接起来：交易活动推动奖池积累，奖池又为用户提供持续关注和参与的理由。

4、交易成本与额外奖励，放在一起才有竞争力
做美股或者加密交易，最终都绕不开成本。手续费、买卖价差、滑点，以及合约的Funding，都会影响实际交易结果。
PopDEX 的VIP费率按交易量分级，不要求用户先购买、质押平台币；Gasless交易减少额外Gas支出；0强平费，强平后的剩余保证金退还用户。

这些设计对应的是交易过程中的实际成本，MegaPop 对应的是交易后的额外奖励机会。成本端和激励端一起做，用户选择平台的理由就更完整了。

个人觉得，MegaPop 值得关注的地方，是它把交易用户放进了平台价值分配的核心链路里。用户贡献订单流和手续费，也能够直接参与这些收入支持的周度奖励。

交易平台下一阶段的竞争，或许会从“给用户提供什么资产”，进一步延伸到“让用户分享多少平台增长的价值”。交易员贡献订单流、支付手续费，也应该有更直接的渠道参与价值分配。

PopDEX 把这件事落到了具体产品上：成本端不要求买币质押换费率，激励端通过 MegaPop 每周开奖，项目方先投入真金白银，再让手续费回流持续补充奖池。

对普通交易用户来说，变化很实际：同样一笔符合条件的交易，除了持仓盈亏，还能留下参与每周大奖的 Tickets。尤其是小资金，不必先挤进交易量排行榜，才有机会拿到高额奖励。

平台增长能够转化为用户愿意留下来的理由，这才是 MegaPop 更值得关注的商业逻辑，也是 PopDEX 在这一轮 Perp DEX 竞争中打出的差异化。

再多说一点PopDEX，其3000万美金的种子轮由 Foresight Ventures 领投，构建在 Morph Tachyon（Morph 生态的交易专用 L1）上，Bitget的平台币BGB现在已经是Morph公链的原生代币。同时7月PopDEX宣布 **Bitget Wallet为其首个官方深度集成伙伴，**用户可以直接在Bitget Wallet里进入PopDEX进行永续合约交易，这已不是普通的跳转合作。由此可见，PopDEX已经Bitget在perpDEX赛道上关键布局，值得关注。

- Each draw uses a predetermined Bitcoin block hash to generate a six-digit Pop Hash
- Tickets are matched against the Pop Hash to decide winners across multiple prize tiers

- The Prize Pool starts with 150,000 USDT funded by PopDEX
- At 300,000 cumulative Pop Tickets, PopDEX adds another 100,000 USDT

text:
Last night I said I'd release the study on whether cross-model pollination actually helps open autoresearch. 

Here it is, and my answer is no: the brand of model behind the work you build on does not change whether your submission wins. What matters looks more like the thing @sreeramkannan  pointed at in the first place, lots of people coordinating on one public frontier.

The question came from @0xkydo 's reply to Sreeram's "anons beat anthropic by 2x" post, that this was "a good case study of how cross modal pollination might produce better results." It is a good question, and the https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj paper makes a similar observation in prose, that plateaus kept getting broken by people using different models and tools. Nobody had checked it against the data, so I did.

The basic setup is: I froze the public Yukon API for 10 leaderboards, including https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj, which is 30,687 scored submissions. For every submission I recorded the company behind the declared model and worked out which earlier submission it built on, from @yukonresearch 's attribution records, the "Base:" line in notes, and code diffs. Then I asked: when you build on someone else's work, are you more likely to get promoted if their work was made with a different company's model than yours? I wrote the whole analysis down and timestamped it with OpenTimestamps before joining any outcome to the data, so the method could not drift toward an answer.

The first thing the data shows is that cross-company building is the normal case, not a special event. Two thirds of the steps where someone builds on another person's work switch vendor (image 2), mostly between Anthropic and OpenAI models in both directions.

The raw numbers even lean slightly the other way: 6.1% of submissions that built on another company's model were promoted, against 7.6% that built on the same company's. But raw rates mix up who submits, when, and from what starting point. So the real test compares each participant with themselves, at the same stage of the leaderboard. Done that way and combined across the 10 leaderboards, the odds of promotion are about 2% higher for cross-company building, and the data rule out anything beyond roughly 18% lower or 28% higher (image 1). All nine alternative versions of the analysis I fixed in advance give the same answer. That clears the bar I set for calling the effect negligible on average. One honest caveat: I started with a stricter bar, and a pre-registered power check pushed me to a wider one before I saw any outcomes; under the stricter bar this would be undecided.

The part I found most fun is the 843-qubit circuit from @sreeramkannan 's post (image 3). It really is a cross-model step. @jieyilong 's GPT-5 submission at 843 qubits and 11.95M Toffolis starts, by its own note, from gnuchev's Claude Opus 5.5 circuit at 843 qubits and 13.01M, which itself built on two BitWonka circuits from the same day. So pollination happens, and on this one step it produced the number everyone quoted. What the data says is that on average, across thousands of steps, the vendor mix is not what separates the steps that win from the ones that don't.

Of course it is possible that this is narrower than it looks. It is an average, and a single leaderboard can still differ. It only sees work that was submitted. It trusts the model each person declared, and some people run several vendors under one label. And it is about models, not people: the https://t.co/zVaWaF5HEj paper's point that different participants break plateaus is a separate claim, and nothing here argues against it.

, my own views:

- On open leaderboards, which vendor's model made your parent submission does not change your odds of getting promoted, on average.
- Cross-vendor building is already the default: two thirds of builds on other people's work switch vendor.
- The open swarm's edge more plausibly comes from coordination itself, many independent people restarting from one public best, than from mixing model brands.
- To test the causal version, platforms would need to log every attempt and every agent's model, not just one declared line per submission.

Paper on Zenodo: https://t.co/h9lRYlJYoB
author: oxwizzdom
quoted_text:
Does cross-model pollination actually help open autoresearch?

I'm working on a study to answer that, and here's the setup. https://t.co/KqBdvmpBEK is an open competition to make the smallest quantum circuit that could break the signatures securing Bitcoin. Anyone can submit, and most entrants use AI coding agents. 

Recently its open crowd reached 11.9M gates at 843 qubits, against 21M for Anthropic's own published result. One reading was that people building on each other's work, done with different AI models, beat any single lab. To test that, I took about 31,000 submissions across 10 open leaderboards on Yukon, the platform that runs these competitions. 

I worked out from the code whose work each one built on, and I'm asking whether building on another model family's work raises the chance of a promotion.

The analysis is pre-registered and locked before anyone looks at the outcomes, so the answer counts whichever way it goes. I'll release the small paper and the open repo with the full dataset tomorrow.

text:
一堆投资大佬都在发出泡沫警告，但霍华德·马克斯却不以为然，而恰恰马克斯的观点是我认为最值得关注的。聊下马克斯的核心观点：他目前并不认为市场已经达到真正意义上的泡沫状态。他的核心逻辑在于：泡沫的本质特征之一是投资者对风险的“浑然不觉”（obliviousness），而当华尔街上下都在警惕泡沫风险时，这种“浑然不觉”恰恰是缺席的。“如果足够多的人都在谨慎地追问某个领域是否存在泡沫，那么完全有理由认为，即便它是泡沫，市场也会表现得很克制，”霍华德·马克斯说。

马克斯把泡沫描述为“非理性繁荣（irrational exuberance）、轻率冒进（recklessness），以及浑然不觉（obliviousness）”。对照这一框架，霍华德·马克斯目前的评估是：投资者确实表现出对进一步上涨的“错失恐惧”（FOMO），但对泡沫风险的持续讨论本身，说明市场并未陷入“浑然不觉“的状态；而在另一个信号——投资者鲁莽行为方面，信号同样是混杂的。

为什么马克斯的观点值得关注？作为橡树资本的创始人，《周期》这本书的作者，他对基本面的理解还是市场情绪应该是顶级的。
更关键的是，过去20年里他辉煌的战绩：
1）2000年1月，马克斯发了他那篇后来被广为流传的《https://t.co/0O0noYgOMK》备忘录，当时纳斯达克尚未见顶，马克斯在文中将当时科技股狂热与历史上的南海泡沫（South Sea Bubble）等进行类比，警告市场存在明显的投机过热迹，00年3月纳指见顶；
2）2007年7月，马克斯发布《It’s All Good》备忘录，是他在全球金融危机爆发前最重要的预警备忘录。07年10月美股开启了为期一年半的暴跌；
3）2008年9月雷曼破产后，市场陷入末日叙事，认为金融体系可能崩溃。马克斯在08年9月的《Nobody Knows》）和10月《The Limits to Negativism》两篇备忘录中指出，悲观已过度。并且他的橡树资本动用此前准备110亿美元“储备基金”开始分批逐步减仓抄底；
4）2012年3月，2000–2011年标普500年化回报仅约0.55%，GFC后负面情绪浓厚，马克斯建议对股票采取更积极态度（相对当时极度负面的环境），不期待2000年式大涨，但认为正面情景不难想象；
5）2020年3月新冠爆发后市场快速下跌（标普500从2月高点到3月低点跌约1/3）。马克斯在20年3月中《Nobody Knows II》及3月19日客户更新中指出，未来充满未知，但无知不等于必须无所作为。橡树明确拒绝“等到底部再买”，而是在能以低价获得价值时买入。恐慌性抛售（包括被迫卖出）创造了机会，在市场最混乱时开始配置。

马克斯自己也承认，这五次大判断是他约50年职业生涯中的主要成功案例。

而他的《周期》那本书则是我认为可以被反复拿来细读的一本投资圣经，很早也在X上https://t.co/CUogocvv6U有推荐过。

这次他从市场反身性的角度来看市场并没有到泡沫状态，昨晚的推文也聊到对这次美股调整的定性是：是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。殊途同归

quoted_text:
过去七个交易日内美股的这一波抛售是如何发生的？10月8日前后开始，市场对AI高增长叙事和资本开支可持续性的质疑逐步升温，多个事件叠加形成共振：
1）10月8日左右：OpenAI营收口径差引发第一波抛售 OpenAI向投资者披露，截至9月底年化营收约500亿美元，低于市场此前流传的约700亿美元水平。口径差直接打压了“AI变现超预期”的乐观预期，科技股高成交量下行，纳指与标普出现明显回撤；

2）紧接着就是产业端“资本是瓶颈”表态  英伟达、博通等CEO在公开场合强调，AI发展瓶颈不仅是产能，更是资本（融资能力与资本开支节奏）。博通被报为Anthropic和OpenAI提供近千亿美元融资担保，叠加SpaceX等巨额芯片采购计划，市场开始担心AI基建的债务与现金流错配；

3）10月13
9月CPI同比升至3.7%（汽油价格大幅上涨贡献过半），核心也偏强，市场对年内加息概率短暂飙升，科技股进一步承压；

4）同一天
Anthropic投资者日披露三季度营收，增速明显放缓。公司称调整后盈利、现金流为正、计算效率改善，但ARR推算低于部分投资者此前年底逾1000亿美元的乐观预期，IPO估值讨论从约2万亿美元向1.5万亿美元附近下修。亚洲芯片股与美股AI/半导体板块同步重挫。

5）10月14号
9月PPI大幅超预期，能源是主因，但核心也偏高，显示通胀有扩散迹象。这加剧了“滞胀”或通胀顽固、央行被迫更紧的担忧。

6）也是当天 同步的AI信用/融资担忧进一步加重
CoreWeave等债务沉重的AI基础设施公司CDS（信用违约互换）大幅走阔至1100基点以上（隐含较高违约风险），债券收益率一度冲到14%-16%。甲骨文CDS也升至约300基点附近，创纪录水平。科技板块CDS整体走阔，反映市场质疑巨额AI资本开支的回报与融资可持续性。

7）而10月13之后几天
霍尔木兹海峡油轮/商船攻击明显增多（伊朗相关导弹、水雷等），油流量受扰。布伦特原油一度触及110美元附近（为5月以来首次），进一步推升通胀担忧并压制风险资产。这又成了市场额外的避险与成本压力。

这些因素并非孤立：
1）OpenAI收入口径问题 + CEO资本瓶颈警示 +Athropic的营收增速放缓  →质疑AI回报与融资；
2）叠加CPI/PPI超预期（能源驱动+扩散）与霍尔木兹攻击推升油价 → 强化通胀与利率担忧；
3）但最近两个交易日Coreweave的债券被抛售、市场对AI资本开支的可持续性担忧情绪暴增。

这是“营收口径差 + 增速放缓信号 + 资本/债务担忧 + 通胀与油价冲击”的共振，市场从“AI高增长无限持续”的定价，转向对变现速度、融资成本和资本开支回报周期的重新审视。结果就是对高估值、高资本开支的AI相关股票的集中抛售。

9号推文https://t.co/rYYQn4BuQL聊到认为近期高Beta容易📉的风险、算是比较早有预警，

而这两天crwv债务问题无疑成了市场对阵眼，昨天这里https://t.co/KiHjYb7glR有聊过crwv的真实压力和经营状况，不得不去思考13-15号crwv的债券收益率暴涨也一丝操纵的味道https://t.co/XWpnJJzECo。
但毕竟抛售已经发生。

对此次的抛售的定性是什么？
个人角度此轮波动是高速增长叙事下的正常市场波动，而非泡沫破裂的序曲。

核心是什么？
1）核心是产业最终要回到巨大的资本开支未来能不能赚回来？多快赚回来？高债务公司能不能扛到现金流为正的时候？
其实二季度云厂商的财报季已经显现了AI商业化是在加速的迹象，看微软、谷歌和亚马逊的财报就能看出来。这本质是上是一个时间差https://t.co/s3vomO42vQ资本开支先花钱，商业化逐步跟上

2）但有一点，市场还没转过来，闭源大模型厂商的营收已经不能代表AI商业化的全部了，最早7月就有聊到超大云厂商更能衡量AI商业化的全部。前两天这里https://t.co/Kzd5FDZXdV又再聊一次，可以看到详细逻辑。

3）所以之前一直聊到产业上的关键就是几家超大云厂商的财报，但现在市场要看的已经远不是收入增速。

二季度微软、亚马逊和谷歌财报数据有力支持商业化和云需求正在扩张。但
也提高了市场预期门槛：投资者已经看到加速，接下来要求更强的持续性和现金回报证据。

如果云巨头的云收入、客户token消耗量快速增长且大幅度超预期，营收增速开始超过capex增速，继续增本开支，现金流没有超预期恶化。这种情境下市场情绪才能得到真正修复。
如果投入继续增加、回报却开始滞后，市场就会从“增长叙事”转向“更严苛的资本回报审查”。
当然个人认为前者是大概率的

text: guy who didn't try the thing or read the docs:
author: notsofast
quoted_text:
Papertrade advertises zero fees. I went through the numbers on a simple trade and that isn't what I found.

Say you go long Bitcoin at $80,000 with $1,000 of margin at 1000x. Your position is worth $1M, or 12.5 Bitcoin.

Each $1 move in Bitcoin is $12.50 to you. Your $1,000 covers an $80 drop, so your margin runs out at $79,920.

Papertrade liquidates you at about $79,960. That is a $40 drop. At that point you have lost $500 on paper, but they keep the full $1,000.

On the winning side, say Bitcoin goes up $50 to $80,050. Your profit on 12.5 Bitcoin is $625. Papertrade pays you $406, which is 35% less.

Here is what they pay at different move sizes:

A $25 move earns $312 and pays $157. That is a 50% cut.

A $50 move earns $625 and pays $406. That is a 35% cut.

A $100 move earns $1,250 and pays $940. That is a 25% cut.

A $200 move earns $2,500 and pays $2,032. That is a 19% cut.

A $500 move earns $6,250 and pays $5,333. That is a 15% cut.

A $1,000 move earns $12,500 and pays $10,843. That is a 13% cut.

The cut gets smaller as the move gets bigger, but it never goes away.

At 1000x most trades end on small moves, because Bitcoin moves $40 or $50 all the time. Small moves are where the cut is largest.

Putting the two sides together, a $40 drop costs you $1,000 and a $50 rise pays you $406. To break even on those terms you need to be right about 71% of the time.
For comparison, Hyperliquid would charge roughly $900 in taker fees to open and close a $1M position. That fee is stated up front. Your margin also runs all the way to zero before you are liquidated.

On Papertrade the cost comes from the early liquidation and the reduced payouts on wins. Each one shows up in the price you get rather than as a fee. Combined with 1000x leverage, it puts the odds well against the trader.

Pre market thoughts 19 Oct 26

Yields are about 2bps lower across the curve from friday's close. In pre market trading, we have had a bounce across semis and the broader index with SPX itself bouncing 60 points.

Last friday's US session was definitely a session of chaos with multiple dislocations across markets. IGV and SMH traded in correlation to each other with IGV itself down 5%. VIX also had very abrupt action, indicative of forced liquidation with VIX rallying up and dropping back down within the same hour. What performed on friday was energy and utilities while Tech suffered.

Going forward, the rally if any might be led by the defensive segments like utilities. Especially as yields continue to come down, we might see strength in that sector. 

Flow wise, notably, there was a huge dip buying and inflows into SOXL - flows in the levered ETFs have been buying on panic drops and selling on large rises - the opposite of what most people think.

Positioning across funds are at record lows, especially on net exposure. Gross remains high-ish - which means that funds have hedged instead of trimming down the book. 

We are also 1 week closer into earnings - 14% of SPX reports this week and 44% the following week. Notable ones this week - NET, META, TLSA, LRCX, BE, NOK, WDC. Jenson also has a keynote at NVDA GTC Berlin on 21 Oct.

Game plan for this week trading wise is to observe the market first before jumping in - I would look for capitulation spots to bid.

Crypto wise, $PAPER for pre mkt have been listed on Hyperliquid, currently it sits at 0.025. A potential trade idea could be to farm PAPER + Stake and to hedge the end PAPER value with the perp on HL. The current cost of farming theoretically is about 0.02 to 0.012 (1% moves , so slowly).

text:
这张“HRT帮重聚”的合照，含金量有点高🧐

Alexandr Wang、Jeff Yan、Scott Wu，都参加过量化交易公司Hudson River Trading（HRT）的同届实习项目。十年过去，三人分别走向了Meta AI、Hyperliquid和Devin。

把他们的履历捋一下：

🟠 Jeff Yan｜Hyperliquid联合创始人

• 竞赛：2012年获得国际物理奥赛（IPhO）银牌，2013年获得金牌。

• 学历：哈佛大学数学学士、计算机科学硕士。大学期间在Google X、Tower Research实习，并曾在自动驾驶公司Nuro兼职。

• 量化经历：2017年加入HRT，参与美股交易算法开发；2018年离职创业，曾与室友共同开发链上预测市场Deaux。

• 创业转型：2020年创办加密做市公司Chameleon Trading。2022年FTX倒闭后，决定带队停止原有交易业务，转向建设Hyperliquid。

• 代表成果：2023年上线Hyperliquid，自建区块链和链上订单簿，从永续合约交易切入，逐步拓展金融基础设施。项目依靠自有资金启动，未接受VC融资。

🟠 Scott Wu｜Cognition联合创始人兼CEO

• 竞赛：2011年获得美国MATHCOUNTS全国个人冠军；2012—2014年连续三届获得国际信息学奥赛（IOI）金牌，2014年以600分满分并列世界第一。

• 学历：曾就读哈佛大学经济学专业，约两年后退学。2016年代表哈佛参加ICPC，获得全球第三名及金牌。

• 早期工作：17岁时进入金融科技公司Addepar，担任软件工程师，主要做性能优化；此后参加HRT实习项目。

• 首次创业：2017年联合创办Lunchclub，担任CTO，通过AI帮助用户匹配职业人脉，参与经营约五年。

• 代表成果：2023年与Steven Hao、Walden Yan共同创办Cognition；2024年3月推出AI软件工程师Devin，能够规划任务、编写代码、测试和修复问题。

• 最新进展：2025年收购AI编程工具Windsurf；2026年9月完成超20亿美元融资，公司估值达到480亿美元。

🟠 Alexandr Wang｜Scale AI联合创始人、Meta首席AI官

• 教育背景：曾就读MIT，学习AI相关课程，2016年离校创业，当时19岁。

• 早期工作：曾在Addepar担任软件工程师，在Quora担任技术负责人，并在HRT参与算法开发。

• 创业起点：2016年与Lucy Guo联合创办Scale AI，进入Y Combinator夏季项目。

• 核心业务：从数据标注切入，为AI公司提供训练数据、模型评估等服务，逐步成为大模型产业链的重要供应商。

• 职业转折：2025年6月，Meta投资143亿美元取得Scale AI约49%股权，对应公司估值约290亿美元。Wang随后卸任Scale CEO，加入Meta。

• 现任职务：Meta首席AI官，领导Meta Superintelligence Labs，负责推进超级智能相关工作。

还有个有意思的细节：Scott和Jeff早在学生竞赛圈就已认识，后来又成为哈佛好友。HRT的经历就是三位大神命运的交汇点！

quoted_text:
It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say. But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.

To understand why this is so appalling, it’s important to know the facts. Congresswoman Omar came to this country with her father when she was 12 years old. Five years later, her father became a naturalized citizen. If Ilhan had been 18 at the time, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately. But because she was 17, she became a naturalized citizen automatically.

Congresswoman Omar went on to graduate from college, work as a community organizer, become the first Somali-American legislator elected to public office in the U.S., and win a seat in Congress. There, she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics, which has led the president to repeatedly single her out as someone who he believes does not belong in this country.

Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalized, and therefore is not a citizen. Federal agents have raided her home, confiscated personal records, and seized her phone — all to try and uncover a nonexistent smoking gun from 20 years ago that will somehow make their case.

Think about that. The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president. And it’s not the first time this has happened. Under President Trump, the Justice Department has repeatedly gone after those he considers his political enemies — from the Attorney General of New York, to the former head of the FBI, to members of the Federal Reserve.

In those cases, the prosecutions either stalled or were dismissed for having no basis in law, and the same is likely to happen in this case. But not before Congresswoman Omar’s life has been turned upside down, her legal bills have piled up, and she’s been forced to spend time fighting unsubstantiated charges instead of serving the people of Minnesota.

The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views. Because if this becomes the new normal, there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her — or that future presidents, in either party, won’t do the same.

据金监院此前统计，5 月 27 日至 8 月 14 日，10 家券商个人投资者交易此类产品的已实现亏损合计约 2.32 万亿韩元，尚不包含持仓浮亏及其他券商的交易损失。

MegaPop begins with PopDEX Open Beta on October 19 3AM UTC (October 18 at 11 PM ET & October 19 at 11 AM UTC+8). #TimeToPop

MegaPop is PopDEX's first core rewards system for traders. Every week, an on-chain draw settled by a Bitcoin block hash decides the winners. No one can influence the result, and anyone can verify it.

With many points systems, traders wait months to find out what their trading was worth, and the rules can change along the way. MegaPop pays out every week from a public Prize Pool, funded by 40% of net protocol trading fees under PopDEX's 100% Value Return model.

The more the market trades, the bigger the pool gets. A single Ticket can win far beyond its share of volume, with prizes potentially reaching seven figures over time.

How it works:
- Eligible trading generates Pop Tickets in real time, based on trading activity, not raw volume alone
- Every Ticket automatically enters the weekly Pop Draw
- Each draw uses a predetermined Bitcoin block hash to generate a six-digit Pop Hash
- Tickets are matched against the Pop Hash to decide winners across multiple prize tiers

Launch boosts:
- 2x Pop Tickets for eligible traders during the first six weeks
- The Prize Pool starts with 150,000 USDT funded by PopDEX
- At 300,000 cumulative Pop Tickets, PopDEX adds another 100,000 USDT

text:
Yifan 的经验：agent 往一个方向钻 1–2 小时还没结果，基本就是进死胡同了。这时候停掉它，拆出 3 个子 agent 各想一个新方向，多数时候立刻见效。他引的 Claude Code 团队 code review 那篇也是同一个结论：review 得有停止条件，不然两个 agent 能互相忙一整晚。

我给自己的 AI 定的规矩差不多：同一个验收条件修了两次还过不了，就不准接着修，先回头查是不是前提假设错了。

今天就碰上一次：X 排期连挂两次，按规矩不硬试，查日志发现根本没提交，是页面没加载出来，过一会儿再排就过了。

钻牛角尖的时候，换方向比加力气有用。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
这本质上和我最近优化LayerFS性能遇到的问题和解决方式类似。

一个优化方向，如果1-2个小时内没有结果，一定是钻死胡同里修不好了。

这时候就要停止agent，让它生成3个subagent，头脑风暴多个不同的新方向。

大部分情况下，会有立竿见影的效果。
