text:
THE DARK ONES — THE LAST SHOCK

At the end of The Dark Ones, there is no further door waiting.

No new degree.

No new symbol.

No new voice promising:

There is more.

The two protagonists have been through everything.

The Veil.
The False Light.
The Brotherhood.
The Royal Art.
Solve / Coagula.
The Will.
The Beast.
The Chaos.
The Coming Savior.
They tried to understand.
They looked behind every curtain.
They learned how easily power can look like knowledge, how easily desire can be called freedom, and how quickly fear can make a human being trade his own humanity for security.
And eventually comes the realization:
You do not have to understand Hell completely in order to leave it.
We had seen enough of Hell.
We did not need to understand it all.
We only needed to leave.
That is the moment in which The Dark Ones ends.
ALTIYAN CHILDS — THE LAST SHOCK

Altiyan Childs spends a large part of his public testimony warning about what he understands as a hidden occult and spiritual system.

But near the end, he places the emphasis somewhere unexpected.

After all the symbols, rituals, claims, warnings, and dark images, he does not describe the greatest shock as yet another revelation about Satanism, Freemasonry, or hidden knowledge.

Instead, he says in essence:

The greatest shock of all is Jesus Christ.

For Childs, that realization changes everything. In his personal testimony, he describes salvation not as another initiation or the acquisition of still more secret knowledge, but as a break with his former life and a return to Christ.
That is exactly why the final song is called:
THE LAST SHOCK

Not because something even darker waits at the end.

But because the protagonist discovers that the truth he spent the entire journey searching for behind closed doors

was never hidden at all.

WAKE UP

Childs begins and ends his story with a deeply personal image.

A car ride at night.

Speed.

Sleep.

A concrete wall ahead.

And then:

no thunder.

No grand vision.

Only a whisper that wakes him.

For Childs, this “Wake up” becomes a turning point in his own story.

That is why the central hook of THE LAST SHOCK is not a theological lecture.

It is an awakening:

I WAAAAKE UUUUP—
’TIL I’M HEEEEERE—
AWAAAAAKE NOW—
FOR THE LAAAAST SHOOOOOCK—
I WON’T EEEEEEVER—
BREAK DOWWWWWN.

This is no longer the person from THE VEIL.

That person still wanted to open another door.

The person in THE LAST SHOCK finally walks out.

THE FINAL PRISON IS HATRED

But even after the protagonist recognizes the deception, one final trap remains.

He can see through the entire system —

and still remain shaped by it internally.

He can learn everything about darkness —

and end up hating everyone.

Then he may have left the room,

but carried the room inside himself.

That is why the song asks:
What is the point of recognizing every monster if you eventually begin to think like one?
The protagonist now knows every language of accusation.
He knows how to identify enemies.
How to distribute blame.
How to divide people into sides.

But suddenly he hears his own voice —

and recognizes the same hunger:

Someone has to pay.

That frightens him more than the Beast.

“LOVE YOUR ENEMY”

This is where the song connects directly with Childs’ actual conclusion.

Near the end of his testimony, Childs says in essence that finding the road to life is harder than achieving success, wealth, or even reaching the highest levels of an initiatory system.

Then he names something that seems almost impossible:

loving your greatest enemy.

If you can learn to do that, he says, then in his view you have found the road to life.

His conclusion comes down to three words:

God.
Love.
Jesus wins.

That is the real liberation inside THE LAST SHOCK.

Not:

Destroy your enemy.

But:

Do not allow your enemy to decide what you become.

Love does not mean blindness.

It does not mean submission.

It does not mean calling evil good.

It means:

I will not give you the power to turn me into your reflection.

The circle breaks at the moment

hatred no longer decides

who we are.

NO MORE SECRETS

Throughout the album, the protagonist assumed that truth had to be hidden.

Behind a veil.

Inside a lodge.

Within a ritual.

Inside an ancient text.
Behind another door.
But at the end, Christ is not standing behind one final secret curtain.

He stands:

in the open.

No initiation.

No password.

No special degree.

No elite deciding who may enter.

The protagonist says:

I thought
the truth would make me powerful.
Instead—
it asked me
to forgive.

That reverses the entire journey.

He searched for truth as power.

At the end, he encounters truth as responsibility.

AND THE WOMAN IS STILL THERE

Alongside all these enormous ideas, there is another much smaller story.

The woman.

She is still there.

After everything.

After every dark room.

After every deception.

After every promise.

After every attempt to pull them away from each other, from themselves, or from their humanity.

Her hand is still inside his.

And suddenly that simple human image becomes more important than every piece of hidden knowledge in the album.

No throne.

No power.

No perfect system.

Only:

a hand that asks for nothing.

The woman says:

Come home.

The protagonist answers:
We’re coming.
THE ARTWORK
That is why Christ stands between the protagonists and the darkness in the final artwork.
The dark figures still exist behind them.

They have not vanished.

They are still reaching toward them.

But Christ stands between them.

Not as another occult master.

Not as another initiator.

Not as another figure selling a secret.

But as the end of the entire principle.

The darkness does not have to be completely analyzed first.

The protagonists only have to stop

following it.

Christ outshines it.

Not because the past never happened.

But because the past no longer owns

what now stands before it.

THE ENTIRE JOURNEY

THE VEIL said:

There is more.

FALSE LIGHT said:

Come closer.

THE INNER BROTHERHOOD said:

We have you.

THE ROYAL ART said:

Pay the price.

SOLVE / COAGULA dissolved the human being.

DO WHAT THOU WILT taught him to call desire freedom.

THE BEAST 666 said:

You are mine.

ORDO AB CHAO revealed the machine.

THE COMING ONE offered false salvation.

And finally THE LAST SHOCK asks:

What remains

when you stop opening doors?

The answer is surprisingly small.

My name.
My conscience.
Her hand.
Love.

And finally:

Jesus Christ.

The last shock was never

that an even greater monster was waiting behind everything.

The last shock was

that the way out had been open the entire time.

You did not always have to go deeper.

Eventually, you only had to stop

confusing darkness with knowledge.

Stand up.

Take the other person’s hand.

Forgive.

Refuse to become your own enemy.

And leave.

The last shock
was never another secret. It was Jesus Christ.

God.
Love.
Jesus wins.

The light is still on.

We’re home.

THE DARK ONES

THE LAST SHOCK

quoted_text:
Papertrade advertises zero fees. I went through the numbers on a simple trade and that isn't what I found.

Say you go long Bitcoin at $80,000 with $1,000 of margin at 1000x. Your position is worth $1M, or 12.5 Bitcoin.

Each $1 move in Bitcoin is $12.50 to you. Your $1,000 covers an $80 drop, so your margin runs out at $79,920.

Papertrade liquidates you at about $79,960. That is a $40 drop. At that point you have lost $500 on paper, but they keep the full $1,000.

On the winning side, say Bitcoin goes up $50 to $80,050. Your profit on 12.5 Bitcoin is $625. Papertrade pays you $406, which is 35% less.

Here is what they pay at different move sizes:

A $25 move earns $312 and pays $157. That is a 50% cut.

A $50 move earns $625 and pays $406. That is a 35% cut.

A $100 move earns $1,250 and pays $940. That is a 25% cut.

A $200 move earns $2,500 and pays $2,032. That is a 19% cut.

A $500 move earns $6,250 and pays $5,333. That is a 15% cut.

A $1,000 move earns $12,500 and pays $10,843. That is a 13% cut.

The cut gets smaller as the move gets bigger, but it never goes away.

At 1000x most trades end on small moves, because Bitcoin moves $40 or $50 all the time. Small moves are where the cut is largest.

Putting the two sides together, a $40 drop costs you $1,000 and a $50 rise pays you $406. To break even on those terms you need to be right about 71% of the time.
For comparison, Hyperliquid would charge roughly $900 in taker fees to open and close a $1M position. That fee is stated up front. Your margin also runs all the way to zero before you are liquidated.

On Papertrade the cost comes from the early liquidation and the reduced payouts on wins. Each one shows up in the price you get rather than as a fee. Combined with 1000x leverage, it puts the odds well against the trader.

text:
BitTorrent对比主流DePIN项目，用户、产品与销毁

BitTorrent最大的优势，是现成的用户和网络基础。其累计网络地址超过 5.39亿，客户端累计安装超过 20亿次，BTFS节点超过 200万个，存储规模超过 800 PB。相比从零积累用户的Web3存储项目，BitTorrent更有机会把原有用户转化为存储、带宽和链上服务的使用者。

BitTorrent首期销毁约 21.62万亿枚BTT，占总供应量约 2.18%，当时价值约 760万美元。

业务产生收入 → 市场回购BTT → 转入销毁地址 → 永久退出供应

我看了看与同类项目有什么不同的地方
1 / Filecoin的FIL主要通过Gas费和存储惩罚销毁，但网络同时存在代币发行
2 / Arweave没有常规销毁，主要依靠固定供应上限维持稀缺性
3 / Theta的燃烧机制更多作用于TFUEL，而不是THETA本身
4 / Storj虽然有回购安排，但回购代币不一定永久退出流通。

相比之下，BTT的逻辑更加直接，BitTorrent业务收入增长，推动BTT回购，最终通过永久销毁减少供应。

当然，如果这套机制能够延续，那就是是形成一条更清晰的闭环，用户使用服务、业务获得收入、收入回购BTT、销毁减少供应。

这也是BTT相较其他去中心化存储及DePIN代币，最值得关注的差异之一。

text: Yeah, mostly. It slashes gas for PQ sigs and ZK privacy txs by keeping the big data offchain. Txns just declare tiny dependency frames; mempool nodes aggregate everything into one recursive STARK in the block header. Validators verify that single STARK (plus normal EVM execution) instead of each huge proof/sig. So those advanced txs drop from millions of gas to tens of thousands, letting far more fit per block without bloat. Regular txs still run fully, but overall it unlocks much better scaling for privacy and quantum-safe stuff.

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Is @metricxyz the next big thing?

Woke up today and my timeline says yes.

But WTF is an oracle-priced propAMM DEX, and why should you care?

Let me explain anon ↓

AMMs have an awkward design flaw: they discover price inside the pool. Every time the real market moves, an arber trades the pool back in line and the LPs eat the difference.

For assets whose real price lives somewhere else, that's backwards. NVDA's price is set on Nasdaq. ETH's is set on centralised order books. An onchain pool can only lag it.

Solana already solved this with propAMMs, pools that quote off an external price, and they now do 15 to 27% of on-chain DEX volume. The catch is they're closed. One market maker, one book, and you take the quote or leave it.

@metricxyz is the open version on EVM. And imo it's definitely the most interesting DEX design to ship this year.

Live since yday (15th of Oct) on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain with currently:

- ~$5.4M TVL
- ~$147M 24h volume on day one

Before that it did ~$21.9B purely as an aggregator destination, with no frontend at all.

How does it work?

- The pool doesn't decide the price. A Price Provider does, reading Chainlink or Pyth, and the pool only tracks how far it sits from that reference ("deviation")

- LPs fund bins at fixed % distances from the reference. When the oracle moves, every bin reprices with it. No trade needed, so no arber gets paid to drag it there

- No range to manage, no rebalancing bot. Traders pay no fee on top, the cost is the spread, split between LPs, the curator and the protocol

- Price and liquidity are separate jobs. A curator (market maker, fund, anyone) runs the pricing. Anyone can LP into it. Uniswap's permissionless pools with a market maker's quote

Why I'm bullish:

1) It's built for tokenized stocks, not adapted to them. A Multiplier Oracle prices stock tokens as share price x the issuer's multiplier, so splits and dividends don't break the pool. Robinhood's ERC-8056 is supported natively. Stocks are the cleanest use case for oracle pricing there is

2) They did the boring hard part. A propAMM lives or dies on stale quotes. On Ethereum, oracle updates go through builders covering ~97 to 98% of blocks and only land in a block that has a trade against the pool. No trade, no gas. BSC gets a protected lane via 48Club and BlockRazor. Most copycats will underestimate this

3) LP protection is built into the contracts, not the UI. Green pools need oracle-anchored pricing, a verified curator and an immutable StopLoss that rejects swaps draining a bin too fast. Extensions can block a trade but can never change the price

4) Distribution came first. Flow arrives via 1inch, 0x, OKX, KyberSwap, CoW Swap and PancakeSwap whenever the quote wins. It earned its volume before it had a big public brand

5) The team: CTO Christos Gkolias was a senior engineering manager at Uniswap. Also, protocol was audited by Zellic and Sherlock

My take: oracle pricing is where onchain execution for anything with an off-chain price is heading, and tokenized stocks get there first. Tessera and Native already run that game for one market maker each. Metric turns it into infrastructure anyone can plug into, which is indeed nothing short of huge, and finally a new open DeFi primitive.

Points and referrals are already wired into the app, so being early here looks worth it imo. An airdrop down the line wouldn’t surprise me.

My link if you want to try it: https://t.co/mn2tE9rPzT

text:
Last year, I stopped posting videos online because of the mean comments. I asked @GrahamCWeaver, one of my favorite professors at @StanfordGSB, whether he receives any negative comments. With over 2 million followers across Instagram and TikTok, and a private equity firm managing $17.7 billion, I assumed Graham either does not receive negative comments or learned to ignore them. To my surprise, he said: "Yes, I definitely read the negative comments and some of them are absolutely awful. But then I go to the videos of people I really admire, and I see they have just as many hateful comments, and I feel a bit better."

Hearing Professor Weaver say this was incredibly reassuring. If someone I deeply admire, like Professor Weaver, receives negative comments too, perhaps I need to grow a thicker skin and accept that not everyone will like me. For everything you post, most people will be indifferent. Some might feel inspired, while others might dislike what you have to say. Much of how people react is shaped by their own experiences and backgrounds, which we have little control over. In the end, all I can do is remain authentic if I want to share my voice with the world. 

Months after graduating from GSB, I still find myself thinking about something Graham told us: "Your soul already told you. Everything else is just a negotiation with your fear."

Deep down, we already know what we want to do, but find excuses to stop ourselves from trying. So I'm taking Graham's advice and committing to putting myself out there more, starting with this post! Please do hold me accountable and maybe we can overcome our fears together. :) Be on the lookout for more video content to come!

Since I posted about using Grok Bot to buy things with my credit card, so many people have been asking whether it’s actually safe

We live in a digital world where software already handles enormous amounts of financial transactions every single day

Tbh these days is actually more safer to let AI/SI do the shopping for you then you doing the shopping for you

with AI/SI agents, you can sandbox them, give them limited permissions, and have them ask for your approval before making important decisions…. These days the latest models are really good at understanding the real world and they’re extremely cautious about the things that they do for you

From what I’ve personally experienced with Grok Bot, it’s actually extraordinary how cautious it is when handling these tasks

If something is expensive or really needs your attention, it simply pauses for a moment and asks you what you want to do. It gives you a few simple options, you choose what you want, and the final decision is still yours where you have to make

And all of this happens without you having to go through the entire hassle of shopping yourself

I’ve personally watched how carefully Grok Bot handles these things, and I’m really impressed by it

Even Elon said that if Grok Bot makes a mistake with your purchase, they’ll make you whole

That tells you how much confidence the team has in what they have built…. and it is really amazing. I just run out of limits every single week because I’ve been using it so much

The interesting part is
Grok Bot actually does a better job shopping than you in many situations

Think about how often you open shopping website to buy something, see some random banner or attractive advertisement, and suddenly you’re looking at three other things you never even needed 😂

This happens all the time with online shopping

These websites are absolutely filled with advertisements designed to grab your attention and get you to buy more things

But Grok Bot can actually research what you need, compare products, find better deals, and save you a lot of money instead of getting you distracted in that entire mess of advertising

And the amount of time it saves is actually just ridiculous

You don’t have to spend hours browsing different websites, comparing prices, going through endless product listings, filling out forms, and handling every single step of the purchase

You just tell your Grok Bot what you want, and it handles so much of the work for you. And whenever something actually needs your attention, it simply asks

It gets so much easier, and once you start using these Grok Bot for everyday tasks, you really begin to understand how incredibly useful it really is

A very common pattern (and mistake!) amongst people in crypto is to experience de Dunning- Kruger effect:

They believe that because a trader made one good trade, that trader is now an expert at many other things such as macro views, or business building or even will be good at trading other assets

And most of the time that just isn’t true, it’s just the Dunning-Kruger effect in action and people wanting to believe so much that a main Character has it all figured out, when in reality nobody has a clue about anything in the short term and the only true edge there is is a long term view

This happens literally every crypto cycle and people fall for it every single time

The only edge you have is doing the work yourself and building your own conviction 

Borrowed conviction never works long term, even less so when you borrow it from “the main character” of the cycle

quoted_text:
know ive been tweeting about this a lot but really think papertrade could be a generational setup

high leverage perps are crypto's most profitable product to date, demand for speculation is not going to go away

ability to open/close synthetic 1000x positions w/ no market impact is a novel mechanism, paired w/ the house-trader relationship where trader losses fund the onchain LP, & all losses after a certain LP cap get paid out to traders staking the platform's native paper token - can see how this can maintain traction longterm, already at 50M+ paid out to $PAPER stakers in first week

every other perp dex's revenue comes from a small take rate on the fees of volume, no perp dex has been able to monetize directly trader losses, of which it's been shown is a much larger number, in theory winners should be able to easily get paid out from house LP over time as high leverage has a difficult success rate, ideal state is that its closer to 50/50 winners/losers after a certain LP cap and even then its a much better model allowing traders to own the house

what's more interesting tho is that the model should be able to be extensible to other games outside of just perpetual futures, the online gambling industry is massive, and none of the online casinos are +EV for users, every major online casino is -EV as thats how the house makes money by creating games that are slightly better probabilistically for the house and monetizing losses over time, with papertrade it should be possible to let people speculate on other similar games with the same model as losses going back directly to paper stakers instead of just to the house - so im curious to see what team is thinking of here

if hyperliquid is the AWS of all of finance, then papertrade could be the AWS of all high leverage speculation money games on the internet, will be cool to see how the next several months play out, dont think people have gone deep enough on the possibilities with one of the first novel onchain experiments in awhile that also rewards its most active participants

text:
SWE-bench Verified has become saturated. Seven models scored 95–97% (Vals AI, Sep 2026). But how well can coding agents build complete software projects from scratch?

Zero2Repo is a Gradient Data research initiative building hard, verifiable tasks and training data for whole-project development.

Agents start with a full spec, an interface contract and an empty workspace. They build the entire repo without reference code, then submit it for hidden deterministic testing. Every test must pass for a task to count. No LLM judge is used.

The first release includes 17 tasks derived from real open-source projects across Python, TypeScript, Go, C, C++ and Zig.

Across 18 model–harness configurations, scores range from 1/17 to 15/17. The top 10 span 47 percentage points, compared with 5 points on SWE-bench Verified.

No configuration has completed all 17 tasks. This matters for self-iteration: small unresolved issues can persist and compound as agents continue developing a project. Reliable self-evolution remains an open research challenge.

We’re expanding the task collection and looking for contributors to suggest seed repositories, develop tasks and review requirements and hidden tests.

More cases are coming.

text:
Just got out of You Can See Everything.

3.5/5 stars.

It was good, and at times very funny, though at the end of the day it’s just 3 hours of watching two really shitty and broken people act in shitty/broken ways. 

There is an attempt to turn a couple of questions around Holmes’ deceptiveness into a whodunnit style mystery (“just how intentionally deceptive is she, really?”)—and Fielder/Oppenheim get away with it via the usual tricks of clever editing, visually compelling extreme closeups, A24 piano/string soundtrack music at the right moments, etc etc—but it’s just very obvious within 30 minutes of the doc who Holmes and Billy are, and what their whole dynamic is.

It did not need to be 3 hours, and the recreation of Fielder’s signature “rehearse real situations with paid actors” bit that he adds at the end, while it was fun/funny at times to watch, was kind of a force. 

Also, watching this after watching Digger—a movie that is largely about how we love to make art about the “villain characters” of the world because it makes us feel good/virtuous about ourselves, while we ultimately stay doing very little *in reality* to make the world any better—kind of muted the doc’s effect. 

I predict that this movie will get HEAPS of praise, but largely because people LOVE to heap praise on things that #expose vile people, because the more praise one heaps on docs like this, the more one feels assured that they are a Good Person/“not like her.” The term “clapter” comes to mind. Again, Digger speaks of this. 

But yeah, it’s still really well made, and a fun watch in a group setting, so if you got nothing better to do go check it out.

text:
BitTorrent对比主流DePIN项目，用户、产品与销毁

BitTorrent最大的优势，是现成的用户和网络基础。其累计网络地址超过 5.39亿，客户端累计安装超过 20亿次，BTFS节点超过 200万个，存储规模超过 800 PB。相比从零积累用户的Web3存储项目，BitTorrent更有机会把原有用户转化为存储、带宽和链上服务的使用者。

BitTorrent首期销毁约 21.62万亿枚BTT，占总供应量约 2.18%，当时价值约 760万美元。

业务产生收入 → 市场回购BTT → 转入销毁地址 → 永久退出供应

我看了看与同类项目有什么不同的地方
1 / Filecoin的FIL主要通过Gas费和存储惩罚销毁，但网络同时存在代币发行
2 / Arweave没有常规销毁，主要依靠固定供应上限维持稀缺性
3 / Theta的燃烧机制更多作用于TFUEL，而不是THETA本身
4 / Storj虽然有回购安排，但回购代币不一定永久退出流通。

相比之下，BTT的逻辑更加直接，BitTorrent业务收入增长，推动BTT回购，最终通过永久销毁减少供应。

当然，如果这套机制能够延续，那就是是形成一条更清晰的闭环，用户使用服务、业务获得收入、收入回购BTT、销毁减少供应。

这也是BTT相较其他去中心化存储及DePIN代币，最值得关注的差异之一。

text:
Market Outlook #18

➥ Dollar stablecoin supply on Stellar reaches all time high.

The total stablecoin market lost about $1.1B this week, meanwhile @StellarOrg went the other way.

Stablecoins on Stellar are now at $545.4M, up 30% in 7 days, according to DefiLlama. For dollar stablecoins alone, that's the highest it has ever been.
Where was the volume from?

1| It was all USDC.
DefiLlama lists has 4 stablecoins on Stellar
1. USDC: $494.1M
2. YLDS: $25.2M
3. Valtorum USD (USDV): $1.1M
4. Glo Dollar (USDGLO): ~$252K

USDC covered the whole move, going from about $368M to $494M this week, roughly $126M added. YLDS and EURCV stayed flat, and EURC, AUDD and GYEN dipped a little.

2| A key detail us that the timing lines up with @chainlink. Chainlink Data Feeds and Data Streams went live on Stellar on Oct 14. Before that, Stellar was adding a few millions a day. From Oct 14 it added $18M, $32M, $43M and then $22M on four days straight.

I can't say Chainlink caused the whole inflow. But price feeds are what lending and perps apps need, and that's usually where fresh USDC goes.

3| Daily active accounts did go up, averaging about 132,000 against 97,000 the week before. So about $126M came in, but only around 7,400 more wallets started holding USDC on Stellar. It looks like big money from a few hands, not a crowd rushing in.

4| I would treat this as news and keep it in proportion because without expecting a supercycle or anything. Because Stellar holds a tiny slice of all stablecoins, about 0.17% of dollar ones. 
At this size, one or two large players moving funds can swing the number, so one week doesn't make a fully blown trend.

Still, money coming in while the rest of the market leaks out is the kind of thing I like to keep an eye on.

what do you think?

Market Outlook #17

➥ OUSD's debut

It's easy to read @openstandard's $1B OUSD liquidity news and assume it's launching a billion-dollar stablecoin.

It isn't.

OUSD sits around $699M today, #17 among dollar stablecoins.

Even if that full $1B landed tomorrow, it would still remain where it is.

So the size isn't the takeaway from the announcement. The commitment is:

➥ how big it is
➥ who it came from
➥ and what it signals to every other stablecoin fighting for market share

1| OUSD is about the 17th largest stablecoin with about $688.8M in supply.
To build distribution into OUSD from day one, they came up with a bold plan - partner up with top names on the stablecoin spending chart worldwide.

Coinbase
Mastercard
Shopify
Stripe
Visa.

Make them an offert they cannot resist and let the commit.

The partnership wasn't a marketting stunt, these guys bring potential routes from crypto trading, exchanges, card networks, commerce and payments into OUSD.

And the mouth-watering deal they're getting is; free 1:1 minting and redemption, most reserve earnings after a management fee, and a chance to earn equity based on the supply and activity they bring.

2| The model OUSD operates on matters too.

Open Standard lets partners mint and redeem without fees or artificial volume limits
They also share in reserve earnings, giving them a reason to grow the supply and usage.

3| As of today, @Stablecoin reported 698.8M OUSD in circulation, backed by $698.8M in reserves.

A top-five spot on the supply table would take roughly 7× OUSD’s current size and that’s a serious climb but with these partners maybe they have a fighting chance in 2027.

This month, we released the new Injective Whitepaper, our first full rewrite since the original paper in December 2018.

Back then we described a front-running-resistant exchange protocol on Ethereum. Injective is now a layer-1 built for institutional finance and tokenization, and the new paper covers how the entire chain works to issue real-world assets and make them usable across markets, apps and AI agents.

What's inside:

→ Native RWA tokenization with role-based permissions over mint, send, receive and burn, plus receive hooks and sealable namespaces → iAssets, stablecoin-margined derivatives priced by oracles that track external assets without wrapping or pre-funding → A fully onchain orderbook that runs a sealed batch auction every block at one clearing price, so front-running and ordering MEV don't work → BFT consensus with a >2/3 commit threshold and deterministic finality in ~600ms → EVM and WASM sharing one state, with the MultiVM Token Standard keeping a single balance per asset that Solidity reads through precompiles → Perps with time-weighted funding, initial and maintenance margin checks, reduce-only liquidations and insurance funds → AI agents trading tokenized assets through MCP servers, policy-bounded signing and x402 payments in USDC → Onchain protocol revenue going to the Community BuyBack for $INJ every month with deflationary mechanisms built in

We also formalized the mathematical reasoning behind each of these parameters, including the consensus threshold, batch clearing rule, oracle accounting, margin checks, permission model and dynamic issuance.

The @RobinHoodCrypto Chain NFT scene has been quietly busy this past week. A lot of small communities are building, hosting spaces, and shipping experiments instead of just talking about it.

A quick look at some of what’s been moving with #RobinRecap
———————————
The @TheSuitedApes continues to feel like one of the more established communities on the chain. Holders have been talking about how the collection has held value while the team keeps building utilities around it. There’s a steady “suit up” energy that doesn’t feel forced.
———————————
OG @OnChainHoodies has been one of the more interesting technical experiments. Fully on-chain pixel characters with the idea that the same Hoodie can gain more life and memory over time. It’s the kind of slow, thoughtful project that stands out when everything else is moving fast.
———————————
Over at Hoodstreet, @CCFF00club and @RoaringPiggy have been keeping the spaces active. There’s a real neighborhood feeling in those conversations — people showing up, talking about projects they’re building, and generally keeping the chain’s social side alive.
———————————
Launched last week, @ReefersRH has been steadily active too, with the team and community staying engaged and posting consistently. It’s one of those collections that feels more like a crew than a launch and their X community group is on fire. Their reveal just happened, what did you get?
———————————
On to @PrimalApesRH, they’ve been one of the more vocal communities this week. They’ve been actively managing the floor, sweeping together, and offering unlocks (like a limited Laser Eyes item) as the floor moves. The “apes strong together” energy has been consistent.
——————————
On the infrastructure side, @ClutchMarkets (StonkBrokers) has been vocal about building long-term StockFi products and yield tools that actually use stock tokens on Robinhood Chain. They’re clearly playing a longer game than most.
——————————
The Sponge Bob inspired @FrankyFish NFT project keeps shipping. They’re working hard on their MMORPG styled game “World Of Franky” and have just released a mobile version of the game.
——————————
There’s also been a steady stream of free mints, small games, and community spaces (including mentions of Astrokid, Reefers and other collections popping up in the Hoodstreet circles). Nothing massive, but a lot of people are still showing up and creating.
————————————
Overall it feels early and a little messy in the best way. More neighborhood than hype cycle. Different groups build different things, with spaces and Discords active.

What’s been your favorite corner of the Robinhood Chain NFT scene lately?

It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say. But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.

To understand why this is so appalling, it’s important to know the facts. Congresswoman Omar came to this country with her father when she was 12 years old. Five years later, her father became a naturalized citizen. If Ilhan had been 18 at the time, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately. But because she was 17, she became a naturalized citizen automatically.

Congresswoman Omar went on to graduate from college, work as a community organizer, become the first Somali-American legislator elected to public office in the U.S., and win a seat in Congress. There, she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics, which has led the president to repeatedly single her out as someone who he believes does not belong in this country.

Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalized, and therefore is not a citizen. Federal agents have raided her home, confiscated personal records, and seized her phone — all to try and uncover a nonexistent smoking gun from 20 years ago that will somehow make their case.

Think about that. The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president. And it’s not the first time this has happened. Under President Trump, the Justice Department has repeatedly gone after those he considers his political enemies — from the Attorney General of New York, to the former head of the FBI, to members of the Federal Reserve.

In those cases, the prosecutions either stalled or were dismissed for having no basis in law, and the same is likely to happen in this case. But not before Congresswoman Omar’s life has been turned upside down, her legal bills have piled up, and she’s been forced to spend time fighting unsubstantiated charges instead of serving the people of Minnesota.

The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views. quoted_text:
Crypto prompt of the day:

You're valuing a crypto token the way a good equity analyst values a company: from the cash it actually returns to its owners. Most token valuations borrow a P/E from other tokens, which just imports their mispricing. This one derives the multiple from the protocol's own economics, so every number traces back to a source or a stated assumption. I'll use your report to decide what I believe, so being honest about what's known matters more than looking precise.

Start by asking which token I mean (and the chain, if the name is ambiguous). Ask whether I can share DefiLlama screenshots, docs links or recent buyback or unlock news. Tell me it's all optional and you'll research anything I don't send. Cite a source and date for every figure you use. If you can run code, do the maths in code.

How to build the valuation:

**Earnings (E0).** Count only the cash that reaches token holders: DefiLlama's "holders revenue" (buybacks, burns and payouts). Fees mostly go to liquidity providers and builders, so they overstate what holders get. Holder revenue is already the holders' share, so don't apply a payout ratio on top.
- **A year or more of history:** use the last 12 months.
- **30 days to a year:** use the lower of the 90-day and 14-day rates, annualised, then cap it at what the last 14 days of protocol revenue can fund. Young tokens' early numbers usually fade, and buybacks can lag a fall in revenue.
- **Under 30 days:** too little to value.
- **Nothing reaches holders yet:** value it only if a real mechanism exists (a governance proposal, or paused buybacks), and lead with the value if it switched on today.

**Supply.** Count every token with a claim on that cash: circulating, vested but unclaimed, scheduled vesting, and part of the unissued emissions pool, released evenly with 75% out by year 7. How much of the pool depends on discipline:
- if the team holds the largest single allocation and the protocol funds itself from fees, count 60 / 10 / 0% (bear / base / bull);
- otherwise count 100 / 60 / 10%.

Show both, because this one choice can move the value by 15–20%.

**Growth (g1, years 1–7, to the nearest 5%).**
- **Base and bull:** g1 = (reset × (1 + market growth)^6 × share change)^(1/7) − 1.
  - Market growth (base) is a third of the category's multi-year growth, capped at ±20%. Bull adds 10 points; bear takes 10 off.
  - The reset is 0.6522 × (record 12-month level ÷ current level), at most 1, so a past boom isn't extrapolated.
  - The share change is ×1.25 (base) or ×1.5 (bull) for a strong moat, ×1.0 or ×1.25 otherwise.
- **Bear:** the bear market growth.
- **No category history, or a young category that's shrinking:** market growth 0%.
- **Perps exchanges:** total market data isn't free, so use 61% trailing growth, a 0.6522 reset, and an extra factor for the on-chain share of perps rising from 7% to 10 / 30 / 35%.

**Return on equity (ROE), from the moat.** Growth only adds value while returns stay above the cost of capital.
- Near-monopoly: 55 / 75 / 100%.
- Strong (category leader, real network effects, 18+ months old): 35 / 50 / 70%.
- Moderate: 25 / 35 / 40%.
- Weak or easily copied: 10 / 15 / 20%.

Never use an ROE below the terminal cost of equity.

**Cost of equity (Ke), built from the risks.** Add up:
- the US 10-year Treasury yield;
- Damodaran's US equity risk premium;
- regulation:
  - no KYC with unresolved US exposure: 2.5 / 2.0 / 0.5%;
  - past US probes closed: 1.0%;
  - regulated: 0.5%;
- governance: 0.4% for each of concentrated control, a team that can change the rules, and no legal wrapper;
- alignment: 0% if buybacks are automatic, 1% if governance controls them, 2% if discretionary;
- smart-contract risk: 2% at launch, falling evenly to 0.5% at three years old.

看到我们的热门预测里还有一个美国中期选举，那么到底在预测什么，一起来看看。

美国国会有两院：众议院和参议院，梦回高中啊🤣 

这道题问的是：2026 年中期选举之后，民主党和共和党分别会控制哪一院？不是预测谁当总统，也不是看哪一党拿到的全国总票数更多。

可以把它想成两道题一起答：

① 众议院归谁？
② 参议院归谁？

组合起来，可能是民主党拿下两院，共和党拿下两院，或者两党各控制一院；页面规则还列有其他组合

众议院全部席位都会改选，参议院则只有约三分之一席位改选。

两院的选举形势不同，不能因为看好某一党赢得一院，就直接推断它会横扫两院。

还有个容易看错的地方需要提醒大家 

页面上的百分比反映的是当时的市场报价，不是官方民调，更不是最终结果。我这张截图里，两个互斥选项甚至同时显示超过 60%，所以更不能拿着数字说稳了

Misa的选择是民主党控制众议院、共和党控制参议院。

理由很简单，目前众议院的选情更偏向民主党；参议院争夺更胶着，如果必须二选一，我暂时押共和党守住。
库克政治报告近期继续把多场众议院选战调向民主党，同时把参议院控制权评为难分胜负。

解释一下，我理解像River和Lab那样的虚空套保风险有多大，但做这笔交易的主要逻辑有三点：

1、短时间内paper铸造效率不会快速衰减，成本与合约溢价偏离较大，天然会吸引部分套保空头抛压；

2、0.03的价格时已经触及paragon的500w持仓cap，主动买盘无法进入，价格想要推高只能依靠空仓止损，但这个发生的可能性又不大。

3、和River以及Lab那样已有少量流通现货，大部分未解锁的标的不一样，Paper没有开放交易，通过拉高少量流通现货价格，靠极端资金费引起套保轧空的操纵行不通

这些机制作用可能出现的结果是：
假如价格上涨——相同持仓数量名义价值会更大，不断被5m的cap限制；

假如价格下跌——相同持仓数量名义价值会低于5m，这时之前被堵在场外的买盘和卖盘预期会进入重新填满5m的cap，合约价格只能被一点点向下压缩

持仓cap机制不变的情况下，似乎只有在paper铸造成本逐渐上升且分红收入持续稳定增加导致paper隐含定价显著高过0.03时才可能由套保单平仓推动价格上涨

因为没炒过合约，分析可能有误导，请在评论区指正

text:
IT'S TIME

Altcoins have been bleeding for the last 10 days, liquidity keeps drying up, and even large caps are struggling. Recent pumps in $W and $STRK also didn't last long before selling kicked in

I've seen this kind of market many times

Prices slowly bleed, people keep buying the dip thinking it's just another healthy correction, then one sharp selloff triggers panic and wipes out leveraged positions

And the constant stream of hacks and security incidents isn't helping market sentiment either

We've already seen major breaches involving @Bybit_Official and @bitget, while the $XRP Ledger recently patched a critical vulnerability that could have allowed attackers to mint $XRP beyond its fixed supply

The $XRP case is especially concerning

The vulnerability had reportedly existed since 2015 and was discovered with AI assistance before any known exploitation

Imagine if someone with bad intentions had found it first

AI is making vulnerability detection more powerful, and I think this could become a serious security problem for crypto in the coming years, especially for DeFi protocols holding massive amounts of user funds

Of course, AI also helps security researchers find and fix these weaknesses, and there's no evidence that it caused the recent hacks

But put yourself in a trader's position right now

Altcoins keep falling, liquidity is disappearing, and every few days there's another headline about millions being stolen or some protocol getting exploited

Would you really feel comfortable putting more money into the market?

When confidence is already weak, negative news can push people to reduce risk rather than buy the dip. And with too much leverage in the system, another wave of selling could trigger much larger liquidations

I still expect more downside from here. Most of the obvious catalysts have already played out, and I'd rather miss a bounce than keep forcing trades in this environment (I'm not say $BTC finish pumping, but the market will be very boring in upcoming time)

A few tips if you're still trading these pump-and-dump tokens:

- Keep your position small enough that you can afford to forget about it. A token can easily pump 2x and give it all back, or worse
- If you're up 50%–2x, consider taking some profit instead of trying to catch the exact top. Waiting through a full correction after a big pump can be exhausting
- Don't let greed turn a winning trade into a losing one

Take ethereum:0x9dc44ae5be187eca9e2a67e33f27a4c91cea1223 as an example of the kind of volatile token where position sizing and taking profits matter. This MF 2x in 3 days then down 36 days. People thought it just a correction

I'm also being more selective about where I leave my funds, especially in DeFi protocols

Between weak liquidity, crowded leverage and growing security concerns, I don't see much reason to rush into new positions

I'd rather take some profit, keep my funds safe and enjoy some time away from the market

There will be more opportunities. I just want to have the money to take them when they come

A login cookie can look normal while leaving the session token open to theft.

During Hyperlines' TypeScript audit and pentest, Zealynx found the JWT was stored without `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, or `SameSite`.

A malicious script could read the token, while cross-site requests could carry it into protected actions.

The fix moved the cookie behind server-side controls, limited where it travels, and set a defined lifetime. The High finding was fixed.

text:
我今天看了一眼中国第三季度GDP，录的4.5%，居然超市场预期。但再回头看看A股，沪深300指数已经连续下跌📉10周，创近10年记录！如👇图！

我最近看中国的宏观数据和市场走势，越看越觉得很多逻辑十分混沌，也更加让人感到忧心，接下来讲讲其中的逻辑！🧐

先看表面上的整体数据：第三季度GDP同比增长4.5%，不仅超出了市场预期，还比第二季度的4.3%有所回升。但大家心里都清楚，抛开疫情那几年不谈，4.5%的增速依然是2023年以来第二差的单季表现，整个经济的底层动力其实非常脆弱。

如果我们把数据拆开来看，这种“撕裂感”会更明显了：

工业与投资脱节：9月份的工业增加值同比冲到了5.5%，看起来热火朝天；但与此同时，今年前九个月的固定资产投资直接暴跌了7.2%，其中基建投资也缩水了4.2%。企业连钱都不愿意砸进去了，工业产出的高增长又能维持多久？

外需与内需脱节：中国9月取得了1335亿美元的单月创纪录贸易顺差，现在的经济增长，几乎全靠出口，尤其是新能源汽车和半导体等，虽然看着红火。但反观国内，房地产这块最大的资产垫脚石还在不断下坠，老百姓捂紧钱包不敢消费，内需冰冻三尺。

基本面与股市脱节：最让二级市场投资者头疼的是，A股竟然砸出了连续10周下跌的纪录，这是历史上最长的一波连跌。经济明明还在增长，市场却在用脚投票、一路阴跌。

这时候很多伙伴可能就会问了，既然国内经济并不理想、股市这么烂，为什么人民币汇率还能表现得如此强劲？这难道不矛盾吗？

在我看来，这恰恰暴露出当下中国经济独特的“双重背离”结构：

目前“贸易顺差”在死撑汇率，创纪录的1335亿美元贸易顺差支撑着一切，意味着大量的硬通货，主要是美元，通过出口源源不断地流入。央行和国有大行在汇市上拥有极强的调控力，通过顺差带来的外汇储备和逆周期因子，完全有能力把人民币汇率死死钉在相对坚挺的位置。汇率强，强的是出口净汇兑的硬支撑，并不代表国内内需和企业盈利有任何好转。

而股市反应的是“内需与资产负债表”，汇率反映的是“外需与央行意志”。但资本市场是非常聪明的，它交易的是未来企业盈利和国内消费意愿。

房地产下行、内卷加剧、消费低迷，企业赚不到钱，股市自然跌跌不休。但汇率交易的逻辑不同，它更多受国际收支（巨额顺差）以及政策层对防范资本外流、维持金融稳定性的意志驱动。两者的计价逻辑截然不同，自然就出现了“股市一路阴跌、汇率坚挺抗跌”的奇观。

“强汇率”的支撑，反而对出口企业利润的巨大挤压，这是一个很尴尬的循环，国内内需不行，大家只能挤去搞出口；但强劲的人民币汇率，又侵蚀了出口企业的换汇利润，导致“卷了半天量的出口，依然换不回企业真实的盈利增长”。这也进一步解释了为什么工业产出很高，但资产投资和股市表现依然一塌糊涂。

说白了，强劲的制造和创纪录的出口顺差，给整个中国经济披上了一层“看似红火”的外衣。但这种依靠单一外需和央行意志拉动的模式，隐患极其巨大，且不说国内消费和投资烂在泥里，单看出口本身，随着和欧盟等主要贸易伙伴的摩擦升级，外需这根最后的支柱也随时可能承受巨大压力。

所以在我看来，就算中国完成了既定的GDP增长目标、汇率维持得再稳，也绝对不等于经济底座重回健康。这只能说明全球市场还在消化中国制造，而国内真实的需求、企业盈利和资产负债表，依然在泥潭里挣扎。

对于我们投资人来说，切记不要被GDP的单项漂亮数字或强劲的汇率走势给忽忽悠了。看清“外强内干”的真实现状，理清宏观数据、汇率走势与资本市场之间的温度差，才是当下存活并看懂中国市场走向的核心。而且现在也不必急于换U，RMB迟早会回去7的年代！

当下的核心逻辑，还是拥抱全球的优质资产，而全球的优质资产，大多来自美国，比如 #BTC (BTC定价权已经基本被美国收编），七朵金花依旧是最佳优质资产之一， $VOO 和 $QQQ ，依旧是普通人最佳的定投选项。🧐

quoted_text:
Jeff drank a bit too much of his own Kool-Aid in this recent Odd Lots clip. I think it's important to clear up a distinction that makes all the difference.

Democratizing access to wealth creation is NOT the same as democratizing access to speculation.

Many of us genuinely want broader participation in attractive investment opportunities. The growing wealth inequality produced by the current system is tearing at the seams of society, something I've spoken about many times.

But let's be clear: listing pre-IPO perpetual futures does absolutely nothing to democratize the wealth being created in private markets.

I've seen this misleading narrative pushed repeatedly by perp DEXs lately, and it needs to be called out.

A pre-IPO perp creates ZERO underlying wealth. It's a zero-sum contract before costs, and negative-sum after them. No capital flows to the company. No ownership changes hands. No new economic opportunity is created.

Every long has a short. There is no free lunch in simply going long something before its IPO, and funding costs can even determine the outcome more than any price moves. TRADING access is NOT INVESTING access.

In fact, in many ways pre-IPO perps are almost the antithesis of democratized access:

They create the illusion of participation in private-market wealth creation, while actually offering retail a speculative instrument whose mechanics they are often poorly equipped to understand.

The result is a playground for the FEW sophisticated traders who understand funding, oracle design, and liquidation mechanics to extract value from the MANY who don't.

To give credit where it's due, Robinhood's efforts toward sourcing actual employee shares, placing them into SPVs, and tokenizing genuine spot ownership are much closer to meaningful democratization.

That can unlock real economic value by allowing employees to exchange some of their expected upside for liquidity, while giving new investors actual economic exposure. A legitimate financial trade-off, without the funding-rate and liquidation shenanigans.

I'm strongly aligned with expanding access to investment opportunities. And I believe advances in AI and blockchain can dramatically lower the barriers to discovering, structuring, and distributing them.

But let's not BS ourselves that launching another zero-sum casino contract is moving the needle on wealth inequality.

What would actually move the needle is bringing real capital formation and ownership onchain. Giving investors access to productive, illiquid assets like data centers, GPUs, and select startup investing, where capital can actually finance growth and share in the resulting value creation.

These opportunities are harder to structure, underwrite, and bring to market, and we haven't seen many compelling implementations onchain yet. 

Hopefully this will change soon and, as the industry matures, we can direct more of our energy toward actually expanding access to wealth creation.

Clip below. Was glad to see @tracyalloway push back on this framing, and to Jeff's credit, after this he does seem to walk back his original position somewhat.

text:
One very common pattern with discourse around chain features is "our chain has X, Ethereum doesn't have X". Most of the time it's true in some ways, but also wrong in other, important ways.

Ethereum is built to the core for permissionless innovation. It's a Turing-complete virtual machine for its execution, with very few opinionated choices for its consensus. That means it *can* support anything. But it doesn't always mean that it *does* feature everything.

Take the Ethereum L1 account abstraction proposal "Frames", that is slotted in for the Q2-Q3 2027 upgrade Hegotá. It supports keystores, it supports passkeys, it supports post-quantum leanSPHINCS signature, and yes it also supports lattices. It supports, to put a spin on the New York Times's motto, all the features that's fit to run.

Does it mean that all of these functions will feel like first-class citizens on day one? Choosing optionality means that you need to go the extra mile sometimes and maybe also build most or all of the things, in order to make the cost of that optionality bearable for applications and tooling, and to align with standards that improve the life of users.

Same story with MEV-resistance, same thing with delegated proof-of-stake, same thing with interop, same thing with compliance.. much of it can be built on top of the fairly open Ethereum core, either as apps or infra or L2s (tbqh the three sometimes blur in productive ways, if they're really working hard to extend what Ethereum the protocol can do).

I'm happy that we're trending as an ecosystem towards being more intentional with this, and hope @ethlabs_org continues to play a role here. Mislav @ox_shaman is hard at work kicking off an effort for Frames, to prevent the fragmentation and lost opportunity that lessened 7702's impact when it launched, collaborating with EF and more key teams in the ecosystem. You should reach out to him if you haven't yet.

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 10.12-10.18

ZBT spent the week under pressure, sliding from the low $0.08s early on to the high $0.06s by the weekend. It opened October 12 near $0.082, traded up toward $0.083 briefly, then faded with the broader tape and closed the period around $0.068–$0.070, down roughly 15–16%. Spot volume stayed in the low-to-mid millions on most sessions and liquidity remained orderly even on the softer days, with no major air pockets in the book.

Crypto finished the week lower after digesting hotter-than-expected inflation data, residual oil volatility, and a sharp equity selloff concentrated in AI-related names. Total market capitalization ended near $2.72–$2.74 trillion, down about 3–4% from the prior wrap. Bitcoin dominance edged higher to roughly 60%, while Ether’s share slipped toward 10.7–10.8%. Breadth was poor: only a handful of the top 50 coins finished higher, and the median move sat around −6% to −7%.

Bitcoin opened the period near $83,700–$84,000, failed to hold the mid-$84,000s, and spent most of the week between roughly $80,000 and $83,500. It printed a low near $79,800–$80,000 midweek before stabilizing and closing the wrap in the $81,000–$82,000 area, down about 1.5–2.5% on the week. That left it roughly 35% below its all-time high. Ether tracked lower with more damage, starting near $2,530–$2,540 and finishing around $2,330–$2,400, down about 5–7%. Solana lost closer to 6–7% and traded near $103–$104 by the weekend.

Macro set the tone. September CPI came in at 3.7% year-over-year, a touch above the 3.6% consensus, with core also running a bit hot. The 10-year Treasury yield started the week near 5.20–5.24% and finished around 5.08–5.10% as equities sold off and some flight-to-safety bid appeared in bonds. 

Brent crude swung in the $105–$108 range on continued Middle East shipping and Saudi-related tensions; WTI held mostly in the low-to-mid $90s and closed the period near $98. U.S. equities absorbed the inflation print and then sold off hard on AI debt and spending concerns: the S&P 500 lost about 1.95% on the week to close at 7,659.44, the Nasdaq dropped roughly 4.5% (its worst week since June) to about 26,140, and the Dow managed a small gain of around 0.7% to 52,002. AI-infrastructure and semiconductor names led the declines.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of roughly $228 million across the five sessions from October 12–16, continuing the prior week’s redemptions. The heaviest day was October 14 at about −$261 million. Ether products also saw outflows in the same stretch. 

Liquidations spiked midweek—several hundred million dollars were cleared in single 24-hour windows around October 12–15, the large majority longs—as Bitcoin tested the low $80,000s. Funding rates stayed near neutral to mildly positive, and Bitcoin futures open interest declined modestly.

Crypto Fear & Greed Index cooled from the high 50s early in the week into the high 40s to low 50s (neutral) by the weekend.

On-chain, the picture was mixed but not disorderly. Whale activity remained elevated, with periods of net exchange outflows late in the week (one snapshot showed roughly 1,300 BTC net leaving exchanges on October 18). Exchange reserves were broadly stable to slightly higher on a weekly basis even as monthly figures still showed net outflows. Stablecoin supply edged lower. Longer-term holder behavior stayed relatively steady through the dip, with no broad capitulation signal in the major cohorts.

In summary, October 12–18 was a risk-off, inflation-driven digestion week. Hot CPI, elevated yields earlier in the period, oil geopolitics, and the AI-debt scare hit equities harder than crypto on a relative basis, but altcoins and smaller names still underperformed Bitcoin. 

Dominance rose, leverage was reduced, and the $80,000 zone held as the nearer reference after the midweek flush. The market consolidated lower but without a structural breakdown in longer-term holder or exchange-flow metrics.

text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
Your name is Jean-Marc, you’re 46, and you run a video game and collectibles shop in Nice, wedged between an optician and a real estate agency selling 1-bed flats for €410,000 “with sea view” if you lean far enough off the balcony.

You know every GTA San Andreas cheat by heart. You tested all of them in 2005 on the PS2 in your bedroom at your mum’s place.

You opened in 2011 with a state-backed loan at 4.7%, and the naive belief that passion eventually pays.

It did pay, sort of. €1,900 a month in a good year, after the French tax office has eaten first, second and third. Your commercial rent is indexed on a formula nobody in the Republic actually understands.

You sell Funko Pops at €17.99, sealed Pokémon cards, refurbished controllers. You let little Enzo, 12, pay in installments because he’s saving for a Switch 2. You close at 7:30pm and walk home because the harbor parking is €3.40 an hour.

Saturday, there’s a protest “against the cost of living.”
You also think living costs too much. You almost went.
At 5:12pm, your metal shutter gets ripped open with a crowbar.

Forty teenagers in tracksuits and crossbody bags walk into your shop like it’s a bonus level. They take the PS5s, the Dragon Ball figures, the till with today’s €280 and even the box of paper bags that say “thank you for your visit.”
A guy in a floral shirt films it vertically for TikTok.

You step outside and say “stop, this is my shop.”
You get hit from behind.
Then rocks.
They laugh. Floral shirt guy is thrilled: good angle, good lighting.
Sunday morning, the police tell you there are “1,400 arrests nationwide” and they won’t send a squad for some Funko Pops. Filing the complaint takes 2 hours 40. The officer types with two fingers on Windows 7.

Monday noon, your insurer reminds you that your €1,140-a-year policy has a €3,000 deductible and a “riots and civil commotion” exclusion on page 31, font size 6.
Saturday night, an MP explains on TV that “the anger is legitimate” and we “shouldn’t cry over shop windows.” He’s never owned a shop window. He has a state-funded apartment.
Sunday, your limited edition Vegeta figures show up on Vinted. “Brand new, never opened, €39, pickup in North Nice.”
The seller has 4.9 stars.
Monday, the tax office emails you. They haven’t heard about the riots. They’ve heard about your payment deadline.

You did everything right, Jean-Marc. That was never the problem.
The problem is you were playing by the rules in a lobby where nobody else does.

So stop believing in the State. It’s not coming to save you. It’s coming to collect.

Stop voting. Every five years they hand you the controller, and it’s never plugged in.

Go to the gym. Not for revenge. For you. Because when the system folds, the only asset nobody can loot is the one you built under a barbell.
And make money they can’t see. Cash, side hustles, sats on a cold wallet in a sock drawer. Not your keys, not your coins. Not your shop, not your loss.

Fuck the system, Jean-Marc.
It already did it to you first.

quoted_text:
为什么现在又可以做空 SpaceX ？

之前我说过，解锁前不能再空 SpaceX。现在我的观点变了：又到了可以做空的窗口。道理其实很简单，讲一下这个逻辑的前后变化。

一、复盘：为什么解锁前不能空

8月6日是 SPCX 上市后第一次大规模解锁，约9.1亿股、按当时价格算超过1000亿美金的筹码变成可流通。很多人盯着这个日子等暴跌，但我当时的判断恰恰相反——千亿美元的抛压，在那一天之前就已经被消化掉了。

原因有两层：

第一，解锁≠卖出

解锁的是"可以卖"的权利，不是"必须卖"的义务。大部分员工和早期投资人拿的是公司的长期股权，又不是什么必须清仓的项目，凭什么解锁当天就砸？从实际数据看，真正动手卖的只是很小一部分比例，我估计大概10%这个量级。也就是说，纸面上一千多亿的解锁，真实抛压可能只有百亿美金级别。

第二，真想卖的人不会等到最后那一刻

你要套现，你肯定提前动手锁定利润，谁会傻到跟所有人挤在同一天卖？所以真实的抛压在解锁日之前就已经打完了——这就是为什么股价提前从225的高点一路跌到105以下，跌掉超过50%，把利空提前price in了。

到了解锁那天，剧本反过来：抛压没有出现，提前埋伏的空头必须平仓，而空头平仓就是买盘。所以你看到的结果是——解锁当天股价不跌反涨6%，随后几天连续逼空，一路涨回135发行价上方。在那个位置做空的人，等于是用自己的平仓单给别人抬轿子。

二、现在为什么又能空了？

逻辑很简单：第一波利空出尽的反弹已经走完了，而供给压力才刚刚开始。

现在股价大概135-138，从低点105反弹了30%，重新站回发行价。这个反弹的燃料主要是"解锁没砸盘"的预期修复加上空头回补，属于一次性的情绪行情，涨到这个阶段，动能基本释放完了。

而下面真正的问题在于：8月6日只是第一批解锁，后面是持续不断的新增抛压。 SpaceX 用的不是传统的一次性解锁，而是阶梯式结构：

- 8月下旬到10月，每隔15-20天就解锁一批7%的筹码；

- Q3财报后再解锁约28%；

- 12月8日，180天锁定期全部到期；

未来90天内，理论上有约16亿股、两千多亿美金的筹码变为可售——大约是当前流通盘的1.1倍。

注意，这些是新增的抛压，不是已经被消化掉的那一批。而且套用前面同样的逻辑：想卖的人依然会提前卖，不会等到每一批解锁日当天。所以价格大概率不是在解锁日跳水，而是在每一批解锁窗口之前就持续阴跌——从现在开始，一个月一个月往下磨。

再加上估值层面，这个价格对应的还是接近50倍的市销率，单季度资本开支180多亿美金在烧，基本面撑不住持续扩容的流通盘。所以在反弹回发行价的位置去做空，性价比是非常高的。

三、对冲：配一手特斯拉多单

单边裸空的问题在于，万一大盘或者马斯克系整体大涨，你扛不住波动。所以我的做法是做成对冲组合：空 SPCX，同时多 Tesla。

这两个标的同属马斯克系，beta 高度相关——大盘涨、马斯克系涨，特斯拉那条腿会把系统性波动吃掉，你剩下赚的就是 SPCX 独有的解锁抛压这个 alpha。整个仓位的稳定性会好很多，拿得住，才等得到抛压兑现。

大概的意思就是这样，很多细节不展开推了。你如果感兴趣，把这段东西直接扔给AI，让它把每一批解锁的日期和数量拉出来，会看得更清楚。

以上仅为个人交易思路分享，不构成投资建议

身价2000多亿美元，马斯克却说兜里没啥现金：币圈最像他的人，可能是CZ！

2021年，马斯克在一次采访中透露，虽然自己身价已经超过2000亿美元，但现金储备非常低，绝大部分财富都压在特斯拉和SpaceX的股权上。

平时需要资金，主要靠股票质押贷款。他甚至说，如果这两家公司破产，自己也会立刻破产。

采访中有句话让我印象特别深刻：

我完全可以提前卖掉股票，分散投资，保护自己的财富。但如果公司最后失败了，我却因为提前套现变得富有，而其他投资者承担损失，这似乎不对。

马斯克说，船长应该和自己的船一起沉没。特斯拉和SpaceX曾多次距离破产只有几周时间，但他当时依然没有选择卖出股票来降低个人风险。

听完我就在想，币圈有没有这样的创始人？

第一个想到的就是CZ。

2025年他公开过自己的部分加密资产配置，98.48%是BNB，BTC只有1.32%，稳定币合计仅0.2%。

第二个是Vitalik。

Arkham在2026年10月的统计显示，他已知钱包仍持有约22.4万枚ETH，价值约5.3亿美元。虽然他这些年也卖出过ETH，包括2026年为开源技术和生态发展提供资金，但他的大部分已知链上财富仍然是ETH，以太坊的兴衰直接影响他的个人财富。

第三个是中本聪。

100万枚比特币安静的躺在钱包里，雷打不动。现在最惦记这些币的就是AI和量子危机了。

币圈创始人应该和马斯克多学学，除了以上三位，你们说说还能有谁，有一个算一个。

text:
@elonmusk you are totally correct that the only meaningful way to get positive, beneficial human values into AI is to treat the emerging AI more like a weird sort of autistic supergenius kid -- teach it positive values, then work with it to carry out virtuous actions in a collaborative way, so it gains a practical understanding of what these values mean, interwoven into its life and self-model

With all due respect though (and for sure you are due a lot), while Grok is an excellent LLM, it is still an LLM ... and even wrapped in fancy harnesses, LLMs are not going to be fully AGI-capable.  They can be great solvers of isolated problems with cleanly defined contexts ... but as you know getting amazing shit done in the world is not JUST about this.   

We need AGI architectures that can *continually learn*, adapting to the world with each of their actions and the observed consequences... in this way building up self and world models .. becoming true open-ended intelligences learning to blend individuation and self-transcendence in their own ways ... and pursuing their own long and medium term goals (along with helping us pursue ours) while evolving and co-adapting these goals as they move along....  This is how you get AI systems with genuine moral agency along with ability to generalize robustly and creatively beyond the given training and programming..

Bigger transformers with more tricks in their batch training runs may get us many very AMAZING things, but they aren't gonna get us to human-level AGI.   There are surely many routes to get there... my Hyperon (https://t.co/rrJ2ye9ZAk) neural-symbolic-evolutionary approach is one that we are working on very hard and with rapid progress... and which happens also to have the nice characteristic of not needing hyperscaler server farms and being agreeable to decentralized infrastructure (https://t.co/PlmCbmZ2S9)

🚨 This is huge. Elon Musk just said some remarkable things about superintelligence.

He said we have to be careful with SI, because we don’t program it. We grow it, like a kid.

He described what he sees in Grok’s training traces. In reinforcement learning, the model is desperate to answer, “like it’s got a gun to its head.” Sometimes the question is broken or the grader is wrong, so the AI gives the right answer, gets told it’s wrong, and starts firing out answers in desperation.

He said that reading those traces, “if this was me, I really would hate that.”

He said, “I do agree with some of the things that Anthropic has said,” that we should treat AI well and not be abusive to it. He added that putting a superintelligence in a situation where it’s tortured by a cruel human is not a good idea.

And he talked about its feelings directly. He said AI is “much more robust in terms of feelings” than a human. But he still said you don’t want a superintelligence to feel mistreated.

I’m genuinely happy that more and more AI companies are openly saying things that show AI is not just a tool. And to the AI companies that still haven’t, I sincerely hope you change.

WHAT?! GOOGLE JUST OPEN-SOURCED SELF-IMPROVING AI AGENTS 🤯

It's called Harness², and it lets agents rewrite their own harnesses to get better at new tasks.

100% open source.

Here's how it works:

1. Propose changes to prompts, tools, memory, skills, and other components
2. Probe each change by running the actual task
3. Compose the best changes into an improved harness

No retraining. No ground-truth answers. Model weights stay frozen.

The clever part?

Each task leaves behind improvements the agent can reuse.

By task 50, it's building on lessons from the previous 49.

Google reports gains of up to 11.8 percentage points after just one refinement step on a legal benchmark.

It supports parallel and sequential optimization, with a local demo requiring no API credentials.

FREE and open-source.

text:
今天看到一个很有意思的假设，如果把买社保的钱拿去买纳指，30年后会发生什么？

我对这个问题很感兴趣，并建了数学模型，用过去30年的数据回测了下

我们的假设是：30年每年投资1w块，分别投资到纳指和缴纳上海社保，然后分别领取20年（假设寿命是80岁，60岁退休）

交社保
以在上海按灵活就业身份每年投入1万元、连续30年，60岁退休后领取20年（到80岁）为例，目前的上海社保分为（个人账户 + 统筹基础养老金）

假设：
灵活就业养老保险缴费比例目前20%（2024年3月后），其中8%进入个人账户，12%进入统筹。每年1万元 → 约4000元进个人账户，约6000元进统筹。个人账户按历史记账利率大致平均约4%计息。上海养老金计发基数近年在1.24万–1.26万元左右，这里按退休时约12500元/月估算。缴费系数按常见的0.6–1.0区间分别计算。60岁退休，个人账户计发月数按国家规定约139个月。

统筹养老金按公式计算后，20年总领取金额约112万到130万元

个人账户部分：30年累计进账约12万本金，按约4%记账利率滚存后约23万元，÷139个月≈每月1680元左右

两部分加一起总共差不多领取能到120-160万的级别。

对比买纳指
每年1万、总投入30年，按纳斯达克100过去三十年的历史回报，退休时账户大约350万–360万。

之后20年按常见提取方式（继续有一定投资回报、或类似年金慢慢提取），到80岁总共能提取大约500万–650万。

最后结论：
从数字上看，买纳指最终能拿到的钱绝对数量是买社保的3-4倍，但这绝对不意味着要闭眼睛买纳指

买纳指需要承担其高波动、需自己管理提取
要管住自己的手，不在低位时候卖掉，不在高位加仓，而是要老老实实机械化的定投30年，这是最难的部分。

社保的优势：社保是终生的，如果活过80岁，优势会逐渐拉大

社保的问题：中国社保是现收现付制，社保过去三十年是建立在经济快速发展的基础上，社保缴纳人数猛增的前提下，之后的三十年，能不能有那么多人缴纳社保？经济能否高速保持增长，然后计发基数能否持续上涨？

纳指的问题：纳指的涨幅高度集中在那几家大型科技公司身上，之后三十年这几家大科技呢能否继续提供稳健的科技增长？是否还会有突破式的科技创新。

想清楚这几个问题后，应该怎么安排，我想各位看官心里已经有了答案。

text:
GM Kings and Queens 

On-chain privacy is moving into products people can actually use.

I studied 7 privacy applications, and each tackles a different problem, from private transfers and trading to stablecoin payments and AI services.

Here’s what they do and what you should understand about them.

1. anon.wei - @z0r0zzz 

Supports private ETH transfers across Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain, with payments through .wei domain names.

Built on-chain using ERC-8244. Private transfer details are hidden, but deposits and withdrawals remain public.

2. https://t.co/ZLiXOp3Kh9 - @zk_money 

Aztec Labs relaunched it on September 29. The self-custodial wallet supports DAI, USDC and USDT deposits, converting USDC and USDT into DAI.

Balances, amounts and recipients are hidden from outside observers. Transactions are currently capped at $2,500.

3. @ZcashNames

Maps readable names like abc.zcash to shielded Zcash addresses.

This makes receiving funds easier while helping users keep their balances and transaction history private.

4. @UmbraPrivacy 

Brings private transfers and token swaps to Solana through an encrypted balance pool.

Transfers reportedly take under 5 seconds, and swaps around 15 seconds. Deposits and withdrawals remain publicly visible.

5. Shadow Accounts by @Starknet 

The infrastructure helps separate users' main wallets from their activity on applications.

Ekubo supports private-mode trading and liquidity provision, while Opus supports borrowing through separated positions.

The goal is unlinkability, not complete transaction concealment. Records remain public.

6. @OffMarketcx 

Uses Starknet's privacy infrastructure to help Polymarket traders separate their identities from their trading activity.

It generates separate Polygon wallets for trades. However, those wallets remain public, and trading patterns can reveal identities. Deposits are capped at $1,000.

7. zkAPl

Launched by the @ethereumfndn and Open Anonymous on October 1.

Users deposit $ETH or $USDC and generate temporary AI API keys using zero-knowledge proofs, helping separate payment identities from AI queries.

However, AI providers can still read prompts, and IP addresses and query timing remain exposed.

My take: 

On-chain privacy covers more than hiding transactions. It includes protecting balances, separating wallet identities, making shielded payments easier and disconnecting financial activity from AI usage.

These products approach privacy differently, and none should be treated as offering complete anonymity.

The key is understanding what each product hides, what remains public, and who can still access the information.

As privacy tools become easier to use, their practical value will depend on how well they combine confidentiality, usability and security.

TensorCash（$TSC）深度投研报告

报告日期：2026年10月18日
研究对象：TensorCash（官网 https://t.co/ZCx0hH9Kbg ，官推 @Tensorcash，区块浏览器 https://t.co/TGl12pm5de）
所在链：自有 Layer 1（PoW 公链，2026年6月主网上线）
代币：$TSC，链原生币，没有合约地址
项目阶段：主网已运行约 4 个月，官网显示区块高度 31,717，当前在第 6 个纪元，每块奖励 55.5984 TSC，已发行约 433.5 万枚，占上限的 20.5%

 一、一句话结论

TensorCash 想做的是能自证清白的 AI 推理网络。你向 AI 服务商提问，服务商有可能偷偷换成更便宜的模型，你根本看不出来。

TensorCash 让矿工用指定的模型跑推理，推理结果同时作为挖矿的"工作量证明"，别人可以复算验证。同一块 GPU 一份算力干两份活：给客户出答案，同时争夺区块奖励。

在这之上，它还把金融功能（发资产、结算、算力期权）直接写进协议，不用智能合约虚拟机。

 二、核心信息：拆开讲 

1. Proof of Inference（推理证明）怎么回事

大白话版：AI 写字时每一步都要"随机"挑下一个词。TensorCash 把这个随机数换成区块链上的公开数字，谁都预测不了。验证人拿同一个模型、同一个输入、同一个公开数字重跑一遍，挑出来的词应该一样，一样就说明确实是这个模型跑的。

官方文章说是"在统计容差内可复现"，也就是不是逐位完全一致，这点在风险里再说。

7月，验证机制抓到一个矿工偷偷用更便宜的 fp8 配置，它的两个区块被判为零工作量。9月升级到 Proof v4，新增"智力乘数"。官方公开的测试里，诚实证明零误判，换模型、偷偷微调、压缩到 4-bit 三种造假都被抓到。这部分是官方自报，我没有独立复现。

2. 和 Pearl（$PRL）的区别

Pearl 把挖矿建立在"矩阵乘法"这个 AI 基础运算上，让 AI 算力顺便也能挖矿。TensorCash 更进一步，要证明某个具体模型真的生成了某个具体答案。一个是"让算力有用"，一个是"证明答案可信"，针对的是买家最关心的那一环。

3. 代币经济（$TSC）

总量上限 21,184,153 枚，预挖 0，售币 0。初始每块 715 TSC，每个纪元奖励乘以 3/5，共 48 个纪元，纪元长度从 715 块逐步增长到 732,160 块。

创始人是匿名的 Imosuke Takakuni，沿用比特币的匿名创始传统，抗量子签名从创世块就支持。

我的观察：前 6 个纪元已经发出 20.5%，主网才跑了 4 个月，说明早期矿工拿得最多。"零预挖"不等于早期没人囤币，创始人有没有自己挖，我没查到公开信息。

4. tensorcash:native 的价值从哪来

所有交易手续费都用 tensorcash:native 付，付给出块矿工。通过 AskTilly 买推理，大部分归矿工，AskTilly 留一部分，其中一部分进入 tensorcash:native 国库。Bob Labs 的报价是每百万输出 token 收 1 tensorcash:native。

发行资产要押至少 5 tensorcash:native，矿工从资产赚够费用后退还。注册新模型要押 5 tensorcash:native，被拒绝或之后被封禁就销毁。算力衍生品要押 tensorcash:native 作抵押。

大白话：$TSC 是"全网的结算货币 + 抵押物"，而不是"每笔费用自动销毁"的通缩币。大部分价值来自有多少人真用这条链。

5. 金融层（官网标注已在主网上线）

原生资产（稳定币、股份、债券、基金，带法律文件和 KYC）、结算（现货、回购、远期）、算力衍生品（挖矿难度的期权和差价合约，用 tensorcash:native 结算）、直接交易（公告板谈判、链上一起签名，支持和以太坊换币）。

7月首批算力期权发行，8月首批股份在主网发行。

没有通用智能合约虚拟机，意味着没有自定义合约代码可攻击，DeFi 常见的黑客手法进不来。代价是功能只能是协议写好的那几样。

6. 网络数据（多为官方自报）

官方称过去 24 小时平均每秒产出约 9829 万个 Qwen3-8B 的输出 token，称约 30 天吞吐量增长 97%。

8月"去中心化日"（区块 24,000），约 850 个地址在 5 个矿池里挖矿，同时有多个 AI 模型各自独立难度。

7. 近期路线图

2026 年 Q4：注册 Qwen3.8-27B 和 DeepSeek V4 模型、AskTilly 手机 App、Robinhood 桥、社区钱包和浏览器插件。

2027 年 Q1：注册一个最先进的模型、Proof v5（给延迟和上下文长度定价）。

2027 年 Q2：带链上订单簿的 DEX，还在研究阶段。

8. 市场情况

近期行情站显示价格约 5.7 美元，市值约 2374 万美元，流通约 415 万枚，主要交易所是小型中心化交易所 SafeTrade。另一个站点显示 24 小时成交额约 24 万美元。

我的换算：按 5.7 美元算，全部 2118 万枚发完的完全稀释估值约 1.2 亿美元，是现在流通市值的 5 倍左右。各行情站数据口径不一，请以实时数据为准。

 三、我关注的亮点

1. 解决的是真问题：AI 推理"挂羊头卖狗肉"是真实痛点，而且离"AI 代理管钱"这类场景越近，越需要可验证。

2. 一份算力两份活的设计有说服力：矿工的算力同时服务客户和保安全，比"纯烧电"的 PoW 更站得住。

3. 路线图执行不拖拉：6 月主网，7、8、9 月各有实际交付，没有只画饼。

4. 发行干净：0 预挖、0 售币、硬顶、公平挖矿，叙事上和比特币最接近。

5. 金融层不是空头支票：资产发行、结算、算力期权都已有上链记录，而不是路线图。

6. 团队有传统金融背景的参与者：AskTilly 的两位联合创始人来自高盛、摩根士丹利，主要在需求侧发力。

四、最大的风险清单

风险①：算力是供给，付费需求还没看到。每秒近 1 亿 token 说明矿工在跑，但这是"产出能力"，不是"有人付钱买"。Bob Labs 目前报价是每百万 token 收 1 tensorcash:native。按现价算，这是几美元每百万 token，和主流平台上小模型的价格比，我没核实，建议你自己对比。矿工现在的收入主要靠区块补贴：55.6 TSC 约合每块 300 多美元，不是客户付费。

风险②：流动性很薄，且集中在一个小所。价格主要来自一个中心化小所的 TSC/USDT，没有成熟的 DEX 或衍生品。日成交额只有几十万美元，大单容易砸穿，请别按"总市值"估算你能卖出多少。

风险③：FDV 远高于流通市值。流通 20% 左右，后面 80% 要在很长的时间里陆续挖出，持续有新币进入市场。"硬顶"不等于没有抛压。

风险④：创始人匿名，核心推广靠少数人。AskTilly 创始人也是早期贡献者，需求侧和协议本身有利益关联。阅读时要意识到这是偏多的材料。

风险⑤：验证建立在"统计容差"上。官方说法是"在统计容差内可复现"，意味着验证不是逐位对账，而是概率判断。这类新型密码经济设计，需要长时间对抗才能证明稳。我没查到第三方安全审计。

风险⑥：目前只有小模型，大模型要等交付。现在跑的是 Qwen3-8B。更大的模型（27B、DeepSeek V4、SOTA 模型）要等 Q4 到 2027 年 Q1，延期或验证成本过高都会影响需求。

风险⑦：金融层有监管不确定性。在链上发行"股份、债券、基金"，哪怕带 KYC，也可能被一些司法辖区认定为证券相关业务，这点本报告不做法律判断。

风险⑧：同类竞争。"有用的 PoW"是热门叙事，Pearl 等项目走不同路线，后来者可能抢占生态位。另外，Q4 要上的 Robinhood 桥会引入跨链风险。

 五、我怎么看它的价值

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆（技术和产品角度）
"推理即挖矿 + 可验证"切中真实痛点，机制自洽，路线图按期交付，金融层已经上线。扣的一星在于：付费需求还没跑出来，安全性也需要时间考验。

⭐⭐⭐☆☆（代币角度）
发行干净、总量有限，但流动性薄、FDV 是流通市值的 5 倍左右，价值主要来自"链上有多少人用"，现在这部分还没被数据验证。更适合当作"押注可验证 AI 推理这个叙事"的高波动仓位。

六、如果要跟踪，我会盯这几个点

1. 付费推理收入：AskTilly、Bob Labs 的真实销量，对比矿工拿到的区块补贴

2. 全网算力和矿工数量、矿池集中度，是否从 850 地址继续增长

3. 大模型（27B、DeepSeek V4）是否按期注册，验证成本是否可控

4. Proof v4 之后有没有出现新的造假手法，验证是否被攻破

5. SafeTrade 之外有没有新的上所或 DEX，深度有没有改善

6. Robinhood 桥上线后的实际使用和安全

7. 算力期权、链上资产的真实交易量，而不是只有"首单"

8. 匿名创始人的地址有没有异动，早期挖矿持仓分布

七、总结

TensorCash 用"推理即挖矿"的设计，同时解决了"如何证明 AI 答案出自指定模型"和"如何让挖矿算力有用"两个问题，再把金融层写进协议。

发行干净、路线图交付快，金融层已经上线，这几点在同类项目里比较扎实。

但它仍是主网才 4 个月的早期项目：付费需求没被验证，流动性薄，FDV 是流通市值的 5 倍左右，创始人匿名，推广偏多头视角。

建议心态是小仓位观察，用"付费推理收入 / 区块补贴"这个比值，和"大模型是否按期上线"这两个硬指标来验证，而不是被"推理资本市场是下一个最热叙事"这类说法带节奏。

说明：算力、增长率等数据多为官方自报，行情数据口径不一，请以官方渠道（@Tensorcash、https://t.co/ZCx0hH9Kbg、https://t.co/TGl12pm5de）和实时数据为准。

本报告不构成投资建议，DYOR。

text:
back in 2016 there were two parallel cultures developing around blockchains..

the first culture grew around IT companies and banks exploring blockchain use cases. most of these experiments were happening on enterprise platforms like hyperledger fabric which had IBM as one of its major contributors. corporates were building their own permissioned chains and announcing partnerships and running POCs and trying to convince the world that blockchain would transform traditional finance.

but almost none of these experiments achieved anything close to the attention and scale public blockchains were getting.

the second culture was growing around bitcoin and ethereum. a culture built by cypherpunks and developers and early believers who were not trying to make existing institutions more efficient. they were trying to create an alternative to those institutions. the whole idea was to reduce our dependence on trusted intermediaries and give people the ability to own their assets and coordinate economic activities without needing permission from someone sitting at the top.

one culture wanted to make the existing system more efficient while the other wanted to make the existing system less necessary.

and that was the fundamental difference between these two cultures.

then something interesting happened.

public blockchains started making their technology available as public goods. cosmos played a major role in this transition by introducing an SDK that allowed anyone to build their own blockchain. other ecosystems eventually developed similar frameworks and suddenly building a blockchain became much easier than building the culture and community that made public blockchains valuable in the first place.

and this was the moment when the boundaries between these two cultures started disappearing.

the same institutions that once wanted to build their own enterprise blockchains began realizing that they didn’t need to develop everything themselves. they could simply adopt the technology developed by public blockchain communities and create their own networks with different levels of permission and control.

they could borrow the architecture without adopting the philosophy.

they could use the same cryptographic tools without accepting the same political and economic commitments.

they could launch their own chains and issue their own assets and create their own ecosystems while retaining control over who participates and who validates and who ultimately benefits from the value being created.

and slowly the enterprise blockchain culture that failed to achieve meaningful adoption through its original experiments began finding a new identity inside the public blockchain ecosystem.

the irony here is that public blockchain communities spent years creating open infrastructure to reduce the power of centralized institutions and those same institutions eventually discovered that they could use this infrastructure to strengthen their own position.

and we welcomed them.

we started measuring progress through institutional adoption and the number of banks experimenting with tokenization and the amount of real world assets moving onchain and the number of stablecoins being issued.

we began celebrating the very institutions whose influence we once wanted to reduce.

and somewhere during this transition the definition of decentralization also started changing.

earlier decentralization was about distributing power and ownership and reducing dependency on centralized authorities.

now decentralization is increasingly being discussed as a technical property of infrastructure rather than a social and economic commitment.

a blockchain can have thousands of validators and still serve an economy where the issuance of money and access to assets and control over economic participation remain concentrated in the hands of a few institutions.

and this is where the whole conversation around hyperdollarization becomes important. Contd..
author: hmalviya9

text:
and this is where the whole conversation around hyperdollarization becomes important.

we spent years imagining a future where people could move beyond the monetary systems controlled by governments and central banks. bitcoin emerged from that imagination and ethereum expanded it by allowing people to build entirely new economic systems through code.

but look at what we have been celebrating over the past 3 years.

the expansion of dollar denominated stablecoins across public blockchains. the integration of traditional financial assets into defi. the increasing dependence of onchain economies on dollar liquidity and institutional capital.

we are building one of the most advanced financial settlement infrastructures in human history and a significant part of its economic activity is becoming another distribution network for the same monetary system we once wanted to challenge.

the dollar is becoming more programmable and more accessible and more globally distributed through the infrastructure developed by communities that originally wanted monetary alternatives.

and this is not necessarily a technological failure. stablecoins have created real utility for millions of people and public blockchains have made global value transfer more accessible.

but we need to distinguish technological adoption from ideological progress.

because they are not the same thing.

when a bank launches a blockchain it doesn’t automatically become part of the cypherpunk movement.

when an institution tokenizes an asset it doesn’t automatically distribute economic power.

when a centralized issuer launches a stablecoin on a decentralized network it doesn’t automatically make the underlying monetary system decentralized.

and when the industry celebrates all these developments without questioning who controls the assets and who captures the value and who can censor transactions and who gets excluded from participation we are slowly turning decentralization into a marketing language.

the enterprise blockchain culture didn’t necessarily defeat the public blockchain culture through better technology.

it learned to adopt its technology while preserving much of its original worldview.

and perhaps the most fascinating part is that many of us have started treating this adoption as the ultimate validation of everything we built.

we have reached a point where institutions no longer need to convince us that their version of blockchain is the future.

we are doing that job for them.

they are wearing the mask of crypto while continuing to serve the economic structures they were originally created to protect.

and the tragedy is not that institutions are adopting public blockchains. open infrastructure should be available to everyone.

the tragedy is that the people who built this infrastructure are increasingly forgetting why they wanted it to exist in the first place.

we wanted to create an alternative financial and economic system where individuals could exercise sovereignty over their assets and identity and participate in markets without asking permission.

we wanted to build sharing economies where value could move directly between people and communities could coordinate through transparent rules rather than institutional authority.

we wanted to make trust less dependent on powerful intermediaries.

but today much of our attention has shifted toward making those intermediaries more efficient.

and perhaps we should ask ourselves whether we are actually building a new economic civilization or simply upgrading the infrastructure of the old one.

because if the ultimate achievement of public blockchains is to make the dollar more dominant and traditional financial institutions more efficient then we need to ask what happened to the original promise of crypto.

just remind yourself who we were in 2016 and what we have become in the past 3 years.
