text:
网易 LobsterAI 发布了第二期《中国办公 Agent 用户行为报告》，报告基于它自己平台的用户数据，反映的是这一家产品的用户，不代表整个行业。

不过管中窥豹，可以借此看看中国办公 Agent 用户行为变化。也希望其他家多发一些类似报告学习下。

从这期起报告改为每月发布，9 月版还额外看了十一假期的变化。

最醒目的数字有两个：9 月用户每次交给 Agent 的任务平均消耗 20.2 万 Token，是 3 月 6.3 万的 3.2 倍；日均活跃用户的增幅达到 83.1%，是 5 月以来涨得最快的一个月。用的人越来越多，每个人交出去的活也越来越大。

LobsterAI 是网易的办公 Agent 产品，可以在桌面端用，也可以在微信、飞书这类聊天软件里直接给它派活。

【任务越来越大，用户在加速涌入】

Token 是模型读写文字的计量单位。Agent 干活时要反复读任务要求、读自己前面产出的内容，所以一次任务消耗多少 Token，大致反映这件活有多长、多复杂。逐月看：3 月 6.3 万，4 月 6.7 万，5 月 8.6 万，6 月 10.5 万，7 月 12.9 万，8 月 19.7 万，9 月 20.2 万。最大的一跳在 7 月到 8 月，9 月停在高位。

日活这边，报告只给了增幅：6 月 +19.8%，7 月 +25.1%，8 月 +30.6%，9 月 +83.1%，一个月比一个月快。报告没公布用户绝对数。如果这些增幅是逐月环比，连乘下来 9 月日活大约是 5 月的 3.6 倍，这是按图上数字推算的，报告本身没这么说。

【缓存让同样的活，花费差出七倍多】

这是报告里对用户最实用的一节。Agent 每一步都要把任务要求和之前的内容重新读一遍，不少费用就花在这些重复读取上。模型厂商会把读过的内容记下来（缓存），再次读到时按折扣价收费。命中率就是重复内容里有多少能享受到这个折扣。

9 月各模型的命中率大多在九成上下：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 最高，97.3%；DeepSeek V4 Flash 和 V4 Pro 都是 95.7%；GLM 5.3 93.9%，MiniMax M3 93.7%，Qwen 3.8 Max 93.2%，GLM 5.3 Flash 91.1%，Kimi K3 88.7%；垫底的是 Qwen 3.7 Plus，76.7%。

命中率差不多，实际花费却差很多。报告算了"实际费用是原价的多少"：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 4.6%，V4 Flash 6.2%，V4 Flash Vision 6.7%，V4 Pro 7.5%；Qwen 3.8 Max 18.5%，Qwen 3.8 Flash 18.8%；Kimi K3 20.2%；GLM 5.3 29.6%，GLM 5.3 Flash 35.1%。最省和最贵之间差了七倍多。

差距主要来自缓存价，也就是命中后按原价的几成收费：DeepSeek 只收 2%（V4 Pro 是 3.3%），Kimi K3 收 10%，Qwen 3.8 收 12.5%，GLM 5.3 收 25%，GLM 5.3 Flash 收 28.8%。按"命中部分 × 缓存价 + 未命中部分按原价"去算，结果和报告的数字对得上，比如 GLM 5.3 Flash：91.1% × 28.8% + 8.9% ≈ 35.1%。也就是说，对大量使用 Agent 的人，缓存打几折比命中率高一两个点更影响账单。

【用来干什么：编程仍占四成，设计创作在升温】

按行业分，泛编程/IT 占 40.1% 的任务份额，稳居第一；设计/影视/创作 17.2%，排第二，比 8 月有所上升。之后是金融/财务 7.7%、工程/制造/建筑 7%、教育/教研 5.5%、销售/电商/客服 4.8%。和 8 月比，金融、教育、互联网产品运营（3.5%）的份额在下降。

【城市：郑州进前十，重庆深夜最忙】

活跃用户占比前五是北京 5.7%、上海 4.3%、广州 4.2%、深圳 3.4%、杭州 3.2%，之后是成都 2.5%、重庆和武汉各 2.3%，郑州和东莞各 1.9%，郑州是这期新挤进前十的城市。

另一组数据看的是晚 10 点到凌晨 2 点的调用占全天比例。重庆高达 19.1%，明显高于广州 13.9%、深圳 13.4%、北京 12.9%；上海只有 10.5%，杭州 9.4%。

【微信是第一派活入口，通勤路上就开始安排工作】

在聊天软件里派活的用户中，77% 用微信，飞书 14.3%，QQ 6.5%，企业微信 5%，其他 5%（一个人可以用多个，合计超过 100%）。

时间上，早上 9 点和 10 点通过聊天软件派活的份额分别是 6.3% 和 7.1%，同时段桌面端是 4.8% 和 6.4%。报告的解读是，不少人在早上通勤路上就已经用手机把活派出去了。到了下午，两条线基本重合。

【十一假期：白天出门玩，晚上回家让 Agent 干活】

假期里，凌晨 0 点到 7 点的调用份额从平时的 13% 升到 17%，全天高峰从平时的下午 4 点推迟到晚上 10 点。

任务结构也变了。和平时相比，泛编程/IT 的份额高了 4.0 个点，学习与教育、个人生活事务各高 1.6 个点，营销文案 +0.1；下降最多的是数据与表格（-2.9）和翻译润色（-1.6），金融与投资 -0.7，文档写作 -0.5。表格、翻译这类典型的上班活在假期明显退潮。

【选模型：近七成用户只用一个，DeepSeek 是标配底座】

普通用户里 73.6% 只用一个模型，人均 1.6 个；重度用户只用一个的降到 44.7%，用 4 个及以上的有 17.6%，人均 2.4 个。

最常见的模型搭配全部以 DeepSeek Flash 系列打底：搭 GLM 5.3 Flash 的占 14.0%，搭 DeepSeek V4 Pro 的占 12.4%，其余组合（搭 GLM 5.3 FlashX、Qwen 3.8 Max、Qwen 3.8 Flash、GLM 5.3）都只有 2% 左右或更低。

厂商层面，国内模型的 Token 份额环比变化是：智谱 GLM 约 +166.7%，DeepSeek 约 -0.3%，阿里 Qwen 约 -18.2%，MiniMax 约 -66.7%，月之暗面 Kimi 约 -78.6%。报告把智谱的增长归功于 GLM 新模型。

要注意这是份额的相对变化，报告没给各家的绝对份额，看不出智谱现在实际占多少。

图像和视频生成则是字节豆包 Seed 系列领先：图像生成里 Seedream 占 57.2%，MiniMax Image 36%，阿里通义万相 6.8%；视频生成里 Seedance 占 54.4%，MiniMax 海螺 28.1%，阿里 HappyHorse 17.5%。

quoted_text:
一切都是为了健康，为自己，家人和团队负责。
早上醒来，就处理几个同事（美国、国内、香港）的要求，只简单吃了点玉米、土豆、和一个希腊酸奶，加奇异果。

中午空肚吃姜黄、通心血管，而午餐是三只鸡蛋，水果和酸奶，喝一壶柠檬热水，然后，就是要吃的CoQ-10m 、Omega 3、蔓越莓丸、肠道益生菌、维生素B群、蓝莓素和葉黃素、锌片和NAD丸，当然还有补肝的。

下午二十分钟power nap， 下午第一个会3点，让自己在脑袋最清晰的时间，看书30分钟。

昨天特意去深圳做正骨包括了推拿、针灸加艾灸，2-3小时，老中医负责，在香港几乎找不到这么优秀有经验的，消除疲劳，筋骨的舒络，激发免疫力。

中午吃五指毛桃高压锅炖的走地鸡（优质蛋白），地瓜叶（高纤维、营养丰富），带鱼（优质蛋白），一部分三种米组合的米饭，生地熟地黑豆汤 （去湿），还有凉瓜排骨 （清凉祛毒）。

下午，把会都改期，去了做脸部护理，大概两个小时，躺着听柴可夫斯基，休息够后，和两位企业家，去了打兵乓球，两个小时，其实很出汗的，自己从正拍，过渡去横拍。

晚上，简单吃了，回了部分电邮，洗澡，就尝试睡了。

其实peptide、Retinol、维他命水都很重要，男女通用。

对于动刀的医美，其实不大赞成，要是要做运动，特别是力量训练，至少要有一定的线条，倒三角。

植发是应该做的，马斯克也做了，有很大的效果。至于拉皮，有可能倒某一个年纪会尝试做，至于眼枪是可以考虑，微创去眼袋，可以考虑，其他真的要三思。

简单的护肤、搽防晒、清洁，睡眠，保湿，会把你和同龄人，甩开10年甚至以上！

一切都是为了健康，愉悦自己。

感恩，我有两个亲姐姐把我照顾的很好。

以后找机会聊护肤和穿着，大家多学习陈传多！

Over 10,000 tokenized stock units ($2.6M), enrolled 450+ wallets, and with Aave V4's stock readiness, we are serving yield to users, weekends included.

It's still early. Our stock strategies already bring ~$44K in annualized interest to Aave V4's USDC lenders, and we plan to scale them and grow that footprint.

Here's how it works:

1. Users supply NVDAc, GOOGLc into TAU Labs-operated stock strategies

author: oskarth
quoted_text:
We published a writeup on Ethereum's upgrades, past and coming, read through what banks, custodians and other institutions need.

Apart from the move to proof of stake, most institutions we talk to haven't followed the forks closely. Since 2021 the gas limit has doubled, and accounts and rollups can now do things they couldn't before.

The next two forks have different focuses. Glamsterdam, due in December, is mostly about capacity: it prepares clients for a 200M gas limit and makes writing new storage more expensive. Hegotá, planned for 2027, is about control. Frame transactions give accounts more say over how they sign and pay fees, and FOCIL makes it harder for block producers to leave valid transactions out.

We looked at each change through five needs: key control, capacity at a cost firms can plan for, speed to finality, neutral inclusion and confidentiality. Each section opens with a summary for six kinds of firms, from bank treasuries to staking providers, and a replay of mainnet transactions under the new gas rules shows where costs move.

One of those needs the forks leave open. More below.

text:
Jean-Denis Greze was CTO of Plaid. His next startup, an AI tax product for small businesses, brought in nearly $1M in revenue its first year, and he projected $2.5 to $3M the next. He shut it down anyway.

The reason: in the age of AI, it was never going to be venture scale. Incumbents could use the same technology to automate tax prep for their existing customers faster than a startup could win market share. Tax is also sold once a year, so he had about a one-month window to pivot before the door closed.

The pivot became Town, an AI assistant that works from your email and calendar. It found product-market fit fast enough that Ben Horowitz messaged a16z's Alex Rampell to say it "changed my life."

In this conversation, Alex and Jean-Denis cover:

- How to know when to kill a business that's working on paper
- Why Town competes with OpenAI and Anthropic, the companies it buys its tokens from
- Why the "forward deployed engineer" model gets worse as AI gets better
- How a $1/month AI routine can save a restaurant thousands
- What agents mean for Amazon, advertising and the future of shopping

Serenity 说，市场对微软退单这件事，读反了。

微软退掉了 Nscale 在伦敦东北边 Loughton 的一座 AI 数据中心。20 亿英镑的项目，首期 50MW、总规划最高 90MW，微软原本要从 2027 年一季度开始在这里租用大约 2.3 万张英伟达的卡。

退单的原因出在电上。当地电网运营商给 Nscale 的答复是，足够的电，最早要到 2030 年代初到中期才能保证供上。微软拒绝置评。

Nscale 对外说跟微软的关系"依然牢固、长期"，这是伦敦整体的电网问题，不影响其他合同。据报道，Loughton 在双方的合同里只占很小一块，Nscale 在挪威、葡萄牙和美国德州给微软建的项目都还在推进。

这条消息赶的时间点很差。上周 AI 基建股刚被砸了一轮，Nebius 一周跌了 25.15%，是它 2024 年 10 月复牌以来最差的一周，IREN 是去年 11 月以来最差的一周。周末再来一条"微软退单"，很多人第一反应就是 AI 需求要见顶了。

包括身边也有一些持仓的朋友在问我。

Serenity 的看法正好反过来。他说微软急着要算力，这边交不了货，只能去别家拿， $NBIS 和 $IREN 这种手上有已通电容量、本来就在给微软干活的，反而是受益方。

这个方向我是认的。微软这两年在外面签算力签得最凶，$NBIS 去年 9 月签了 174 亿美元，追加服务最高能到 194 亿；$IREN 是 97 亿美元、四期一共 200MW，第一期 50MW 在 8 月 13 日已经交付，并通过了微软验收。等一座 2030 年代中期才可能通上电的楼，对微软没有任何意义。

市场其实已经在用这个标准给 Neocloud 定价了。澳洲的 Firmus 这个月初撤回了上市，原本冲 440 亿澳元估值，可手里在跑的只有 46MW，另外 865MW 还在建，机构不买账。

Nscale 自己一个月前刚在美国递了 IPO，据报道冲的是最高 350 亿美元估值，招股书显示微软和 Anthropic 合计约占它 1,030 亿美元合同额的 85%，现在最大客户先退了一座楼。

不过这件事也不全是利好，合同能撤，是这次最实在的提醒。Nscale 的能撤，别家的也能撤。IREN 剩下三期计划今年内交付，Nebius 在密苏里 Independence 的吉瓦级园区今年 5 月才开工，这些没通电的部分，跟 Nscale 担的是同一种风险。而且"订单转给别人"现在还只是推理，微软没说这单去了哪。

我的理解是，要分开看。已经通电、已经交付的容量，这次是更值钱了，这一轮卡加钱就能买到，电只能排队等。还没通电的积压合同，不管是谁家的，都该打个折看。

拿着 Neocloud 的朋友，与其盯着谁又退了单，不如回头看两件事。

一是你那家的合同里，有多少落在已经通电的容量上，交付公告和财报里都查得到。越依赖还没通电的那部分，越要小心。

二是你自己有没有加杠杆。这个板块上周已经让大家见识过波动了，CoreWeave 的债务问题也还没完。

接下来要留意微软未来几周会不会在别处签新单。签了，这条逻辑就坐实了。

text:
韩国国家养老金因为“头铁”重仓 AI 算力供应链，在短短 100 天内，账面被抹去了整整 1370 亿美元。

昨天韩国金融圈爆出的这个数据极其惨烈：

作为全球第三大养老基金，韩国国民年金公团（NPS）在三季度遭遇了自 2024 年以来的首次滑铁卢，其重仓股的整体估值从 6 月底的巅峰一路狂泻，直接蒸发了约 1370 亿美元。

这个亏损黑洞，显然是一种“成也 AI，败也 AI”的结构性反噬。

这个数字的产生，正是由于重仓了他们自家的“存储双雄”。

数据显示，SK 海力士单只股票就让 NPS 账面缩水了约 558 亿美元；三星电子紧随其后，贡献了约 428 亿美元的跌幅。
仅这两家公司，就占了这家顶级主权基金总跌幅的 72%。

上半年，正是凭借这波全球 AI 基础设施的投资狂热，NPS 曾创下罕见的高收益，甚至在 5 月份选择顶着高位继续加仓本土科技股。

但之后韩国 KOSPI 指数从 6 月高点一路狂泻近 40%，既是存储芯片周期的波动，也是美国科技股高估值溢出效应的缩影。

市场永远缺存储可能是真的，但这是拿养老基金在博弈。

连最该保守的国民养老金都上车了，而在大跌之后，韩国人的安稳晚年，或许正在为这场全球 AI 叙事的剧烈波动变相买单。

🚨 Threat Intelligence | Analysis of the DarkSword Trojan Backend and iOS Attack Chain

Following the public release of #DarkSword-related exploit code in March 2026, DarkSword-PROV2 appeared on GitHub in July, with the attack infrastructure observed operating online in late September.

We traced the live attack infrastructure, linked its admin panels to public GitHub repositories, and analyzed the exploit code, payload library, delivery chain, and post-exploitation capabilities.

🔍 Key Findings:

🔹 A complete attack pipeline: The infrastructure integrates exploit delivery, device and data collection, data exfiltration, and crypto wallet fund consolidation.

🔹 Extensive data theft capabilities: The toolkit targets Keychain data, files, messages, and crypto wallet data, with additional capabilities for wallet data decryption and fund consolidation.

🔹 Broader claimed coverage, narrower functional coverage: Although the toolkit claims support for iOS 13 and later, code analysis identifies two functional exploit windows: iOS 18.6–18.7.2 and iOS 26.0–26.1. Many other version entries remain incomplete or unverified.

🔹 Public code weaponized: Publicly available exploit components have been integrated into a deployable attack framework, lowering the barrier to launching sophisticated #iOS attacks.

🛡️ Recommendations

Keep iOS updated and avoid untrusted links. Simply opening a malicious page in #Safari may trigger exploitation.

If a device has visited a suspicious landing page, treat its seed phrases and private keys as potentially compromised. Use a device that has never accessed the page to create a new wallet and transfer your assets. Also check for abnormal transactions and token approvals across chains, and revoke unnecessary approvals.

A teenager pretended to go to school for a year, secretly stayed home to code, and eventually built one of DeFi's biggest protocols.

> Stani Kulechov grew up in Finland. His father saved for about six months to buy the family a computer.

> Stani became obsessed with programming and spent a year pretending to go to school while secretly staying home to code.

> He eventually studied law at the University of Helsinki, but discovering Ethereum changed his plans.

> He saw how smart contracts could make financial services work without traditional intermediaries.

> In 2017, he launched ETHLend, a project that let people lend and borrow cryptocurrency through Ethereum.

> The idea evolved into Aave, which launched in 2020.

> He kept building, and Aave grew into one of DeFi's biggest lending protocols.

> Then, in April 2026, an exploit at Kelp DAO sent shockwaves through DeFi.

> The attacker used some of the stolen rsETH as collateral on Aave to borrow other assets, exposing the protocol to a major bad-debt crisis.

> Aave itself hadn't been hacked, but it was caught in the fallout.

> Stani pledged 5,000 ethereum:native toward the wider recovery effort.

> A teenager who secretly stayed home to code went on to build one of DeFi's biggest financial platforms.

> Years later, when a crisis hit the ecosystem around it, he stepped up to support the recovery.

Imagine if he'd stopped coding and followed the path everyone expected of him.

text:
国内媒体只敢转发一半。

李录，喜马拉雅资本创始人，芒格唯一投过的外部基金经理，在哥大Graham & Dodd午餐会上聊了一场。

那句「你是国家要支持的目标，还是实现目标所付出的代价」今天看到全网都在转。

确实狠。但现场有个追问更值钱，几乎没人提。先把框架讲完。

中国每十年一轮，有目标就有代价。

工业化时代，环境是代价。河流、空气、土壤换来了经济起飞。下一个十年环境变成目标，污染企业变成代价。

城市化时代，房地产是目标。开发商建了今天的中国，中产靠房子攒了家底。过去五到十年，房地产又变成了代价。

2015年之后，制造业升级变成目标。中国制造2025，从中低端往中高端推。中间赶上特朗普贸易战、拜登技术封锁，反而加速了。2021年全线加码，半导体、航发、操作系统，挨个突破。

李录说，目标基本实现了。电动车全球产量占七成，电芯八成以上，成熟制程芯片基本自主。

代价呢。新房销售从18.2万亿掉到8.4万亿，少了10万亿。李录说房价平均跌四成，典型中产七成资产在房子上，家庭财富缩水六到七成。消费缩了，储蓄涨到165万亿，内需增长趋近于零。

他说那减少的10万亿，恰好等于每年投到制造业升级的金额。资金流向2021年前后直接切换了。

几百年压缩到40年。但代价是真金白银。

现在说那个追问。有人问：中国股市是目标还是代价？

李录答：在某个时刻，股市必然要成为那个目标。因为股权是唯一一种随着经济增长而增长的资产。

房地产在退，财富载体必须换。
照这个框架，下一个目标指向权益资产。

这段没看到有媒体转发。但这段才是全场最值钱的一句话。

text:
Which Minds Will Emerge Beneficial “Basic AI Drives” as they Become Superintelligent?
 
https://t.co/e8ug6mLTfa

(TL;DR -- the ones designed to have beneficial and self-stabilizing goal-systems from the get-go...)

In his 2008 "Basic AI Drives" paper, Steve Omohundro argued that almost any advanced AI will tend to improve itself, guard its goals, protect itself (including against being switched off) and grab resources, whatever goals it starts with, because those things help with nearly any goal. Much of today’s AI-risk thinking comes from this argument. 

My new blog post argues that it only holds for one kind of mind: a single-score maximizer that cares only about outcomes and has frozen, certain goals. It then runs Omohundro-style reasoning on a different sort of AI design -- one with many objectives, firm ethical limits, values woven deeply enough to grow back when damaged and held with some doubt, a gate that checks every change it makes to itself, and other minds around to check it. What comes out is nine beneficial drives, in many cases quite different in nature from Omohundro's selfish AI drives.

The key twist is that Omohundro’s own drives point the other way under my "BGI" assumptions. Goal preservation ends up defending good values. Doubt about its own judgment gives the system a reason to keep humans able to correct it, where Omohundro's assumptions imply an agent will near-inevitably get around such checks. And applying his reasoning to others’ goals, which it cares about but can’t fully know, gives a BGI agent a reason to protect, inform and empower the people around it, and to keep the world diverse.

None of this implies guaranteed BGI. Selfish and beneficial minds are both stable attractors, and a big enough shock can knock a system from one toward the other. Humans sit in an unstable middle btw selfish and beneficial, which is one reason to be wary of building superintelligent humanlike minds. The practical lesson is to build AGI designed from the start to meet the beneficial assumptions, keep on measuring the degree to which it actually does...

text: If we want to save Australia - we need to become a bit Polish.
author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
”I AM POLISH”

They come from a nation that refused to die. 

Invaded and carved apart by the Nazis, their cities reduced to rubble, their people starved, shot, and burned in camps whose names still chill the blood—yet they fought on - in the forests and the sewers of Warsaw and above the skies of England. 

Then came the decades of Communist occupation: the secret police, the economic stagnation, the empty shelves, the lies that freedom was a luxury they could not afford. 

Solidarity rose anyway, shipyard by shipyard, church by church, until the system cracked. They paid in blood, prison, and exile for the right to decide their own future.

That history is why they do not treat sovereignty as a suggestion. 

History is why they rejected political correctness and the woke agenda.

When other European capitals lectured the Poles to accept the mass migration of people from cultures and faiths that reject the foundations of what they rebuilt—Christian heritage, national continuity, the hard-won liberty they bled for—they remember what it cost to lose control of their own streets and institutions. 

On 26 September 1940, in the middle of the Battle of Britain, King George VI visited the pilots of No. 303 (Kościuszko) Squadron at RAF Northolt. Formed only weeks earlier, these Polish airmen—many of them veterans who had already fought the Germans over Poland and France—became the highest-claiming Allied squadron of the battle, credited with 126 enemy aircraft in roughly six weeks of combat while flying Hurricanes. 

Accounts and portrayals of that day capture the recognition the King showed: 

“As I stand among you, I begin to feel a bit Polish myself.” 

If we are going to save our own nations from the same fate as France—cities burning, fraying under riots, parallel societies, and the refusal to defend identity—then the rest of us need to stand together and feel a bit Polish ourselves as well. 

While parts of France and other Western cities stand amid ruin, Polish bravery and the clear rejection of political correctness and the woke agenda have kept their people safe. 

They have no interest in following anyone down a path that treats borders as obsolete, identity as bigotry, and political correctness as a higher law than the will of a free people. 

Freedom was not handed to them, they took it back. They intend to keep it.

If we are going to save our nations - we all need to be at least a bit Polish.

There are coins out there that are the next VVV, PENGU 2025, INJ 2023, ZEC 2025, and many other previous outperformers. These coins are going to be the leaders in the coming months and they're sitting there now (relatively) unpumped.

A few things these all had in common:

-Beaten down charts. These coins were all murdered hugely over months (or longer)

-Relevant narrative OR huge $ behind it. VVV and ZEC benefited from a relevant narrative  (privacy and AI). Huge $ behind it would be PENGU or INJ, where JUMP pumped it to the heavens. 

-Narrative based on belief, not fundamentals. What do I mean by this? I mean that you can't accurately price these coins and it's why you rarely see DeFi coins be extreme leaders (at least since 2021). When you start talking about ARR and clear things that can be calculated, there's a limit to how strongly they can pump. Contrast that with a coin like ZEC, where it's more of a belief system than anything, and you have no comparison. In many ways, these are memes.

-Uncrowded. These coins weren't really on anyone's radar weeks or months before they started pumping and nobody really talks about them until coins start to move. This is obviously extremely common in crypto in general; where attention = more volume = more liquidity = self fulfilling prophecy. If you had said 'privacy' as a narrative in 2024, people would have likely laughed at you. Not the case now.

------------------------

Actually executing a trade like this is actually quite difficult and I don't think many have the execution ability to do so. Just like any great trade, you need to:

-Have excellent research / good reasons why people will actually see the same idea as you

-Size appropriately so that you can capture huge gains while also not being shaken out with short term volatility

-Have the patience to actually hold your idea and not chase momentum in other coins 

All in all, a tough task but certainly possible with the right amount of luck, research, and execution. I'm personally better at just buying momentum but I think that these types of trades are often the most gratifying.

author: CompleteSkeptic
quoted_text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://t.co/i00WLeeFpw

I wrote about a similar idea for agents already running in production, where the harness should repair itself after a failure instead of waiting for someone to debug the trace by hand.

that piece walks through how @Cometml's Opik (open-source) closes this loop, going from a failing trace to a proposed fix to a regression test that stops the same failure from coming back. it's quoted below.

text:
The way we execute large trades onchain is outdated.

It's also unnecessarily expensive when liquidity is thin.

Try selling $100K worth of an altcoin through an average orderbook size. Nearly impossible.

Without enough buyers, parts of your order can fill at lower prices.

While exploring shielded trading, @silhouette_ex found that larger traders were more worried about tipping off the market before making a trade.

This is precisely the feedback that helped shape their RFQ system, which is already live for @xStocksFi and now expanding to BTC and HYPE perps on @HyperliquidX.

Here's how it works:

→ Request a price for the entire trade
→ Market makers compete with quotes
→ Accept the quote you prefer

All perp trades still execute through Hyperliquid's orderbook. Better prices in the book get priority, while the market maker fills the remainder at the agreed price.

Large trades need this kind of flexibility.
Gud tek.

嘉宾 @based16z  ：我当时一边找风投项目，一边在链上找赌局。Hyperliquid 刚出来的时候，我正在找新的风投项目，也想在链上赌一把 —— 这俩正好对上了。

text:
Buying the house by losing at the tables

1. How @papertrade_xyz works
• A perp exchange on @HyperliquidX with up to 1000x leverage. Every trade is against the house pool (the LP), at Hyperliquid's mid price (no order book)
• The house (LP) started at $0, and it grew only from traders' losses. When it can't pay a winner straight away, the profit waits in a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue until later losses refill the pool
• The house's edge (profit) is all on winning trades since It applies a tax to users' profit (charges a 2% win fee)
• Losing trades cost users nothing beyond the lost trade itself

2. $PAPER token
• The twist: every dollar someone loses mints them $PAPER, at 100 PAPER per $1 lost while the LP is under $2M, with fewer per dollar after that
• There was no presale, no team allocation and no airdrop
• If you stake $PAPER, you earn $USDC from half of all trading fees, plus everything the LP makes above $5M
• Currently, $PAPER is not live yet and can only be staked (but pre-markets are opened https://t.co/yoLx19r1Ga)

3. How people are farming $PAPER
The most optimal farming strategy is delta neutral: open an equal long and short on BTC at high leverage, wait for price to move, and close both. One side wins and one side loses = positioned is hedged (the losing side mints PAPER)

The real cost is what the house takes from the winning side through the haircut and the 2% fee

Step by step on how to farm
a. Deposit USDC into Papertrade
b. Open a long and a short of the same size at the same time (e.g ETH at $40 margin each with 250x leverage, $10k notional per trade)
c. Wait for price to move about 0.3% in either direction. One leg is now down about $30 and the other is up about $30
d. Close the losing leg first (this leg mints PAPER) then close the winning leg. Papertrade takes a haircut plus a 2% fee off that win, so you keep about $24.58
e. The net cost is ~$5.42, and you get about 320 PAPER for it. That's around $17 per 1,000 PAPER, or roughly $0.017 per PAPER, which is your cost basis
f. Repeat, then stake the PAPER to earn USDC.

Doing this manually is very troublesome and mistakes are bound to happen which could increase the overall cost. Some chads like @degentradingLSD built a farming bot on Gambit (https://t.co/bpnt3AGKsD) to handle it all for you. All you need to do is set:
• The market, margin per leg, leverage and exit move, e.g. 0.3%
• The maximum number of cycles and set a stop-loss

The bot then opens pairs, closes the losing leg and then the winning one, and repeats. Gambit takes 10% of your cost per cycle

4. Stats so far, from @DefiLlama and Papertrade dashboard
• Papertrade earned $58.4m in fees over the last 30 days
• It paid $54.0m in USDC to PAPER stakers in those same 30 days (~92% of fees going back to holders)
• Traders lost $63.4m of collateral to liquidations in 30 days. The house's own LP holds only about $4.15m
• Revenue and valuation wise, probably can use Rollbit (https://t.co/LvexJOBCiD) and DeFillama to guess PAPER's valuation since the mechanism is the same
• Keen to see the developments of this casino, and how @izebel_eth and @blurr can onboard 0DTE traders from the traditional/normie space

🚨 Huge News by $ASTS - AST SpaceMobile welcomes a Letter of Intent signed by Europe’s four largest mobile network operators: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone, to explore a potential joint bid for Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) spectrum.

> This collaboration is expected to speed up network integration, expand coverage into underserved areas, improve the customer experience, and support a coordinated approach to spectrum access and service deployment.
> It aims to strengthen European digital data sovereignty while allowing the operators to offer space-based cellular broadband through their existing mobile services.

Key points from the announcement:

1 Satellite Connect Europe (AST SpaceMobile’s European joint venture) is supplying a dedicated network of European-operated ground infrastructure. This links BlueBird satellites to the operators’ core networks, supports coverage for a market of over 500 million mobile subscribers, and keeps data handling and service control within European jurisdiction. Operators keep their customer relationships.

2 BlueBird satellites are the largest communication satellites deployed in low Earth orbit. They connect directly to standard, unmodified smartphones (backed by ~3,900 patent and patent-pending claims). The company has demonstrated peak download speeds of 98.9 Mbps; next-generation satellites are expected to approach 200 Mbps, supporting voice, video, and broadband for consumers, businesses, first responders, and governments.

3 The technology can tune across approximately 1,150 MHz of partners’ low- and mid-band spectrum globally. Combined with AST SpaceMobile’s S-band priority rights, this allows blending operator spectrum with satellite spectrum for greater coverage and capacity in Europe (subject to authorizations).

Wayne Thorsen, AST SpaceMobile’s Chief Commercial Officer, described the operators’ move as an important step toward connectivity for every subscriber and said the company is supporting partners with satellite technology, spectrum capabilities, and ground infrastructure to create a “third layer of connectivity.” 👇

前几天认为亚马逊值得关注的三个理由：

quoted_text:
亚马逊开始争夺个人Agent的持续数据入口，亚马逊25年收购Bee后昨天正式推出新一代个人AI设备Bee Frontier（腕带/夹扣式可穿戴）和Bee Eclipse（磁吸手机背面）。 核心定位是把“环境式个人AI”做成持续记忆层 + 行动代理，并深度整合进Alexa+亚马逊购物体系。

一个真正能够帮助用户完成任务的Agent，需要长期理解：日程、联系人、工作任务、消费需求、个人偏好、以及经过授权的其他账户信息。如果这些能力与Amazon购物、Alexa和其他服务结合，商业模式可能进一步扩展到：会员订阅、购物推荐、交易佣金、支付和其他生活服务，还能更好地把把用户更深地留在Amazon + Alexa + AWS生态；

对亚马逊还有更进一步的意义：
1）延伸Alexa边界，Alexa长期以来困在家里。Bee把持续记忆带到用户身上/手机上，让Alexa第一次拥有跨时间、跨地点的个人上下文，从被动响应变成可查询的生活记忆层；
2）强化零售核心飞轮：Amazon最强的资产是购物数据和物流。Bee通过“环境意图检测”直接捕捉真实需求信号（比搜索或浏览更前置），转化为推荐，有望提升转化率和客单价。这是把“听你说话”变成“帮你买东西”的闭环；
3）构建个人AI Action Agent护城河：真正的长期个人记忆是极难迁移的。一旦Bee积累了几个月的对话、承诺、偏好和关系网络，用户切换成本会很高。这比单纯的聊天机器人或一次性会议录音工具更深。

我觉得亚马逊值得关注下，基本面很OK：
1）电商业务盘稳健；
2）云算力业务毫无是龙头而且伴随AI商业化二季度已经有重新加速增长的势头了，AWS毫无疑问是AI商业最重要的载体之一；
3）现在开始积极布局个人行动智能体，这才是当下市场的热点。
7月说超大CSP的价值重估，最看好的微软、Meta和亚马逊，现在前两者都已经起来了，亚马逊走势还没那么强，个人觉得缺一个催化剂。就像微软最近的催化剂是9月吧把chat、coding、长时运行agent放进同一个Copilot，之前这里有聊到：https://t.co/l7NUNkexuq。Meta的催化剂就是Muse的发布https://t.co/sEfyckDNSM。
现在看Bee Frontier和Bee Eclipse很可能是亚马逊的催化剂了。

text:
🚨中国最著名的投资机构之一的奇绩创坛被美国政府制裁了。

根据美国财政部OFAC于10月19日发布的官方公告，奇绩的投资管理公司、人民币一期基金、人民币二期基金，以及致远企业管理主体，共4家实体被列入制裁名单。

同批被列入的还有上海至算科技。

这次依据的是美国《2022年保护美国知识产权法》（PAIPA），措施涉及美国管辖范围内的资产冻结、外汇和银行交易限制，以及美国人对这些受制裁主体的股权、债务投资限制。

这次制裁，牵涉到前谷歌工程师丁林葳窃取谷歌AI商业机密的案件。

根据美国司法部披露，丁林葳在谷歌任职期间，将超过2000页内部机密资料上传到个人云账户，内容涉及TPU、GPU系统、芯片通信，以及管理大规模计算集群的软件等技术。今年1月29日，美国联邦陪审团裁定他7项经济间谍罪和7项窃取商业秘密罪成立。

他在国内创办的上海至算科技，曾获得奇绩的种子投资，并通过奇绩的路演向投资人展示公司。按照美国国务院今天公布的说法，丁林葳在申请孵化项目和路演时，强调自己掌握谷歌的内部技术，宣称能够复制谷歌的AI基础设施。

美国国务院给出的制裁依据，是其认定奇绩为相关商业秘密窃取活动提供了重大支持。奇绩旗下的另外三个主体，则因与奇绩的控制或代理关系，一并被列入制裁名单。

对奇绩的被投企业来说，接下来的融资和退出安排，确实需要重新评估了。

具体影响要看股权结构。按照OFAC的50%规则，一个或多个受冻结主体，直接或间接合计持股达到50%，被投企业也会进入自动冻结范围。

假设一家受制裁基金持股7%，所有受冻结股东加起来也低于50%，这家公司就不会因为这条规则自动被冻结。

比如，新一轮融资要不要奇绩参与签约，老股转让、回购和分红怎么处理，退出款项怎么支付，以及交易里有没有美国投资人、美国银行或美元清算环节。这些都得结合受制裁主体的实际权益，逐项核查。

我比较担心的是融资节奏。合规尽调一旦增加，部分交易的交割时间可能就会往后拖。对正在等下一轮钱到账的早期团队来说，这会直接影响招聘、研发和现金流安排。

准备接美资、做美元融资或者筹划海外退出的团队，现在可以先把股东名册和正在谈的融资协议拿出来，跟投资人、银行和律师重新过一遍。

早期拿谁的钱，后面还能接谁的钱，以及最终怎么退出，这几件事得放在一起考虑了。

text:
10 月 16 日，Google Research 发布两项研究，分别涉及自主实验机器人和AI 驱动的适配体设计闭环。最重要的是，研究展示了 AI 如何根据真实实验失败原因，修改下一轮设计策略，而不只是增加候选分子的生成数量。

1. Wet-lab 命中率：经过三轮反馈，最高达到 42.1%

Google 的适配体实验涵盖两个蛋白靶点。

α-thrombin： 第一轮没有获得有效结合分子，命中率为 0%。AI 分析实验失败原因后，发现部分固定引物序列影响适配体折叠，于是修改结构设计。第二轮命中率达到 26.0%，第三轮进一步达到 42.1%，靶标特异性达到 98.5%。

Myoglobin： 第一轮有效命中率为 10.2%。第二轮由于 AI 过度优化表面结合信号，产生大量非特异性结合分子，实际命中率反而下降至 3.7%。AI 根据实验数据重新限制容易产生非特异性结合的结构，第三轮命中率提高至 33.5%。

也就是说，Myoglobin 的最终命中率达到第一轮的约 3.3 倍，相较第二轮低点提高约 9 倍。

2. 蛋白质设计：计算成本下降，同时获得纳摩尔级结合分子

另一项研究针对肿瘤相关靶点 FAP（Fibroblast Activation Protein）。

Google 使用 Agent 辅助优化蛋白设计流程，通过只保留靶蛋白局部结合区域进行结构预测，使该步骤计算速度提高 8.6 倍。

在相同计算预算下，人类科学家与 Agent 协作的计算筛选命中率接近单独由科学家操作的两倍。

随后，团队利用真实实验获得了亲和力达到个位数纳摩尔级别的蛋白结合分子。

为什么这次值得特别关注？

此前：

AI Design → Computational Filter → Wet-lab Validation

这次更重要的进展是：

AI Design → Wet-lab → 分析失败机制 → 自主修改设计规则 → 下一轮 Wet-lab → 命中率提升

这意味着实验不再只是模型输出结果的最终验证环节，而开始成为 AI 持续改善设计策略的反馈来源。

text:
🚨美国国土安全部公开了一份针对DeepSeek的禁令，禁止任何美国联邦民用政府机构采购@deepseek_ai 的模型（也包括基于DeepSeek开发的第三方产品）

刚看了《联邦公报》的文件。这份公告在当地时间10月19日预公开，计划10月20日正式刊登，所附命令标注的原始发布日期是7月24日。

要求里表示在采购端，要把DeepSeek及关联实体的相关产品和服务，从机构批准清单、采购平台等渠道移除；
而在使用端，要清理机构IT系统里已经使用的相关产品。

使用DeepSeek实现的第三方产品和服务，同样被纳入了范围。

这份命令适用于美国联邦民用行政机构，其中国家安全系统、隔离涉密信息系统另有管理边界，国防和情报体系也属于其他权限范围。

DHS给出的理由包括服务器位于中国、政府人员使用服务可能导致敏感数据外流，并援引安全研究，称DeepSeek的iOS应用存在严重漏洞。

命令也设置了豁免申请程序，申请期限按命令签发日期起算60天。

我更在意的是第三方产品这一条。

按文件写明的范围，给这些机构提供AI助手、Agent或业务系统的团队，即使交付的是自己品牌的产品，也会受到其采用DeepSeek所带来的采购限制。

文件里也没有给本地部署、第三方托管单列自动豁免。

这就把影响传到了做应用的团队身上。

模型由谁开发、产品由谁交付、服务部署在哪里，原本是几个可以分别选择的事情，现在底层模型的供应商，会直接影响整个产品能否进入这部分政府市场。

对准备做美国政府项目的AI团队来说，选模型又多了一个很现实的条件：能力、速度、价格都合适之后，还得看客户有没有资格采购和使用。

text:
李录这场88分钟的完整对谈，信息量巨大！我制作了中英双语字幕版本，建议转发收藏

AI的成本与泡沫、中国制造业与房地产、股市未来的角色、明确否定加密货币，以及做投资最难跨过去的人性。

其中有一个判断，值得所有在中国做投资、做生意的人反复琢磨：你所在的行业，究竟是国家要实现的目标，还是实现目标需要付出的代价？

在中国投资，先看懂“目标与代价”。 李录认为，中国的发展往往伴随着阶段性的重点转移。一个时期大力支持的行业，到下一个时期，可能就要承担转型的成本。房地产、制造业、环保，都可以放进这个框架里理解。对企业家和投资者来说，光看行业过去赚了多少钱还不够，还要看它现在处在什么位置。

中国股市未来的位置，要放进家庭资产负债表里看。 现场有人直接问：中国股市到底属于目标，还是代价？他的回答很有意思：当房地产在家庭和国家财富中的占比下降，什么资产来承接财富积累？在他看来，股权能分享企业创造的价值，也与经济增长相互促进。这是他的长期判断，至于什么时候发生，他没有给出短期时间表。

AI很有用，也很昂贵，最终仍然要算账。 他反复强调，AI会持续产生增量成本，算力、资本开支、收入和利润都绕不过去。能力越来越强，不代表投入就可以无限扩大。技术可以带来巨大变化，企业最终还是要面对财务纪律，市场也可能在这个过程中经历多轮繁荣与萧条。

中美AI的区别，他用两个问题来概括。 硅谷更关心：这项技术还能做什么，边界能推到哪里？中国企业也关心技术边界，但会更直接地追问：它能为我的消费者和企业客户做什么？一个更强调探索能力，一个更强调客户用途。这是他观察两边商业路径的切入点。

资金越集中，越值得看看被冷落的公司。 当资本压倒性地涌向少数热门企业，市场另一边可能就有优秀公司在低价交易。他认为，美国、中国和其他市场都存在这种分化。机会可能因此增加，但前提很难：你得能在别人不断赚钱、市场不断强化同一个叙事时，仍然保持自己的判断。

对加密货币，他的态度非常明确。 被现场问到时，他直接表示自己不考虑，并认为它最终会自行消失，也不认可它的社会价值。这部分肯定会引发争议。可以不认同他的结论，但值得连着前面关于货币、购买力和价值创造的讨论一起听，看看他的判断是从哪里来的。

价值投资最难的一关，是你到底想让市场服务你，还是指挥你。 有位做了两年价值投资的观众问：坚持理念却跑输市场，甚至影响职业发展，怎么办？李录把问题拉回了人性：既想长期做正确的事，又想每年、每季度、每个月都交出漂亮业绩，最后甚至希望每小时都赚钱，人就会逐渐变成投机者。做这门生意，还必须找到愿意与你长期同行、理念一致的资金。

最后讲到人生时，他把复利落在了几个很具体的东西上：知识、信任关系、智慧、健康。

找到适合自己的方向，选择值得合作的人，让这些东西持续积累。过程中会有好运，也会有坏运气；关键是尽量保住已经积累下来的东西，让时间继续发挥作用。

中英双语完整版放下面。尤其推荐把“目标与代价”、AI成本，以及最后关于职业和人生的问答连起来看。88分钟，可以留一个完整的时间慢慢听。

text:
国内媒体只敢转发一半。

李录，喜马拉雅资本创始人，芒格唯一投过的外部基金经理，在哥大Graham & Dodd午餐会上聊了一场。

那句「你是国家要支持的目标，还是实现目标所付出的代价」今天看到全网都在转。

确实狠。但现场有个追问更值钱，几乎没人提。先把框架讲完。

中国每十年一轮，有目标就有代价。

工业化时代，环境是代价。河流、空气、土壤换来了经济起飞。下一个十年环境变成目标，污染企业变成代价。

城市化时代，房地产是目标。开发商建了今天的中国，中产靠房子攒了家底。过去五到十年，房地产又变成了代价。

2015年之后，制造业升级变成目标。中国制造2025，从中低端往中高端推。中间赶上特朗普贸易战、拜登技术封锁，反而加速了。2021年全线加码，半导体、航发、操作系统，挨个突破。

李录说，目标基本实现了。电动车全球产量占七成，电芯八成以上，成熟制程芯片基本自主。

代价呢。新房销售从18.2万亿掉到8.4万亿，少了10万亿。李录说房价平均跌四成，典型中产七成资产在房子上，家庭财富缩水六到七成。消费缩了，储蓄涨到165万亿，内需增长趋近于零。

他说那减少的10万亿，恰好等于每年投到制造业升级的金额。资金流向2021年前后直接切换了。

几百年压缩到40年。但代价是真金白银。

现在说那个追问。有人问：中国股市是目标还是代价？

李录答：在某个时刻，股市必然要成为那个目标。因为股权是唯一一种随着经济增长而增长的资产。

房地产在退，财富载体必须换。
照这个框架，下一个目标指向权益资产。

这段没看到有媒体转发。但这段才是全场最值钱的一句话。

text:
We published a writeup on Ethereum's upgrades, past and coming, read through what banks, custodians and other institutions need.

Apart from the move to proof of stake, most institutions we talk to haven't followed the forks closely. Since 2021 the gas limit has doubled, and accounts and rollups can now do things they couldn't before.

The next two forks have different focuses. Glamsterdam, due in December, is mostly about capacity: it prepares clients for a 200M gas limit and makes writing new storage more expensive. Hegotá, planned for 2027, is about control. Frame transactions give accounts more say over how they sign and pay fees, and FOCIL makes it harder for block producers to leave valid transactions out.

We looked at each change through five needs: key control, capacity at a cost firms can plan for, speed to finality, neutral inclusion and confidentiality. Each section opens with a summary for six kinds of firms, from bank treasuries to staking providers, and a replay of mainnet transactions under the new gas rules shows where costs move.

One of those needs the forks leave open. More below.

text:
MY BIGGEST OBSTACLE TO BECOMING A SUCCESSFUL CONTENT CREATOR IS ME.

PART II — THE UNFORTUNATE ECONOMICS OF BEING YOURSELF

Series length: still undetermined.

Previously, on My Biggest Obstacle to Becoming a Successful Content Creator Is Me, I established that the secret to growing an audience is consistency, that I am fundamentally incompatible with this requirement, and that my subconscious has refused to cooperate with management.

THE AUDIENCE I'M SUPPOSED TO UNDERSTAND

Another important principle of content creation is identifying your target audience.

I have tried.

So far, my followers appear to include gamers, parents, philosophers, people who enjoy dark humor, talking animals, and several individuals whose interests I cannot begin to explain.

Some of them probably have absolutely nothing in common.

Except, apparently, me.

And I find that rather interesting.

We're constantly encouraged to find people who share our interests, but why do we assume that sharing one interest means sharing an entire personality?

Two people might enjoy the same video game and disagree about absolutely everything else. Meanwhile, somebody who has never touched a controller might find my observations about parenting hilarious.

The connection isn't necessarily the subject.

Sometimes it's the way somebody thinks.

Sometimes it's the way they express themselves.

Sometimes it's simply that both people have the same deeply unfortunate sense of humor.

And sometimes a stranger on the internet says something so magnificently stupid that you immediately recognize a potential friendship.

I'm not convinced any marketing software has a category for that.

WHEN YOUR PERSONALITY BECOMES THE PRODUCT

There's another complication.

I actually want this account to become successful.

I would like an audience. I would like engagement. I would eventually like to make money.

I have no intention of pretending I'm above any of that. Money is useful. I'm particularly fond of the way it can be exchanged for things.

But there's something wonderfully absurd about the possibility that the more successful you become at entertaining people, the less freedom you might feel to entertain yourself.

Imagine discovering that thousands of people love your jokes about boiled potatoes.

Wonderful.

Congratulations.

You're now the potato woman.

People expect potatoes. The algorithm recommends you to potato enthusiasts. Brands specializing in potato-related products begin to notice your potential.

One morning, you wake up with a fascinating thought about artificial intelligence.

Unfortunately, your audience is waiting for the potatoes.

You could publish your thought anyway, but your engagement might suffer. Your reach could decline. Your carefully cultivated momentum might disappear.

So you put the thought aside.

And write another potato joke.

Six months later, you're standing in your kitchen wondering how your entire professional identity became dependent on a root vegetable.

Your followers are delighted.

You're considering therapy.

#AgainstBetterJudgment #ThinkLikeATrashPanda

text:
Jean-Denis Greze, founder of @TownAI, on the question every AI app founder gets asked: what stops the big labs from crushing you?

"It is risky always to be competing with your suppliers, right? We're competing against our suppliers. So you gotta ask yourself, is that naturally the right state of the world?"

"Someone at OpenAI, at Anthropic, at Google could wake up and decide to do that. So the better answer actually is to think about our customers and what they want."

"It is our job to determine from all the AI capabilities, frontier model, open weight, what is the right thing for you as a business. And I think you can save money there, but also you can de-risk ever having made the wrong partner."

"There are companies that picked OpenAI like two years ago, and then Anthropic was better at coding for a 12-month period. And those companies had to use both because they realized to be competitive, they needed Claude."

"If you're a smart business, you really think about the neutrality of who's providing intelligence for you and who's routing."

quoted_text:
Jean-Denis Greze was CTO of Plaid. His next startup, an AI tax product for small businesses, brought in nearly $1M in revenue its first year, and he projected $2.5 to $3M the next. He shut it down anyway.

The reason: in the age of AI, it was never going to be venture scale. Incumbents could use the same technology to automate tax prep for their existing customers faster than a startup could win market share. Tax is also sold once a year, so he had about a one-month window to pivot before the door closed.

The pivot became Town, an AI assistant that works from your email and calendar. It found product-market fit fast enough that Ben Horowitz messaged a16z's Alex Rampell to say it "changed my life."

In this conversation, Alex and Jean-Denis cover:

- How to know when to kill a business that's working on paper
- Why Town competes with OpenAI and Anthropic, the companies it buys its tokens from
- Why the "forward deployed engineer" model gets worse as AI gets better
- How a $1/month AI routine can save a restaurant thousands
- What agents mean for Amazon, advertising and the future of shopping

text:
复刻小Lin说 1 分钟，现在谁都能做。
做满 10 分钟、还是那个味道，是另一回事🤥

Opus 5.5 之后，code to video 到了新的高度。
复刻一个片段 → 完整复刻 10 分钟 → 创作新的 10 分钟。
@HyperFrames_  editor 已经在第三步了：「一口气了解泰国经济」，9 分 34 秒，一集她没讲过的题目。

最近 reverse engineering 很火，刷屏的小Lin说复刻帖我都看了。大多数复刻的是一段 1–2 分钟的 motion graphics：形似，但简单、廉价。小Lin的动效细节是满的，动作、编排、前后的连续性，全都和口播文案咬在一起。这不是复刻一分钟的片子能做出来的。

素材可以照着复刻。但如果从 0 开始呢？如果要一集接一集地做呢？
- 素材去哪找
- 每句话配什么画面，怎么卡着文案进出
- 文案怎么写才是小Lin味，而不是别的博主，或者流水线式的讲解
- 数字人和声音怎么撑满 10 分钟：语序、语调、停顿都要对
- 音效怎么提取、归类，用在对的地方
- 背景音乐在哪起、在哪停
到这一步，agent 就一头雾水了。

@HyperFrames_  editor 把这些都解决了：
- 把她拆成一套模板：怎么写、怎么剪、怎么动
- 动效逐帧对齐，1:1 重建
- 音效和音乐跟着口播卡点
- HeyGen 数字人 + 专业级声音克隆

下面泰国这集就是这么来的：同一套模板，换个题目就是新的一集。
HyperFrames editor 做的不是复刻小Lin说，是一个能无限往下做的「一口气了解 XXX」系列。https://t.co/3BsSfDzpoP

Arc 主网上线 day 33，整体更冷了，今天 Arc @jerallaire founder 虽然互动了 $Tolly, 价格有回调 10%左右... 

但 Launchpad 格局没定下来。

$ARGUS 目前大概在 6m 附近上下摆动。之前官方点赞加 Circle "光头" 转发拉了一波，从低点直接弹到 8m 多，结果情绪退了又掉回去。手续费回购还在，但生态整体没热起来，fees 收入跟不上，早期便宜筹码一直压着，反弹很难站稳。龙头地位暂时还在，但创新动作不够，其他项目想挑战它还是有空间。

$Tolly 继续往下走，现在 $1.2m 左右，没看到像样的反弹，基本是一路阴跌。产品没啥新东西，运营节奏也一般，被 Argus 压着之后越来越难熬。

$UBI  $Solon 都进入到 低位了 ，UBI 最新的MC 是 $155k, 有些回调，Solon 则继续探低到 $80k。社区氛围还行，但量跟不上，官方点将 $Argus 之后它们也跟着回调，短期很难独立走出来。

$FUCI 已经确认软 rug 了。网站已经关掉，项目方跑了，市值掉到$14k，基本可以确认跑路。之前我还要想空投fuci呢，现在看来得换个token了。。

再看其他几个还在撑的：

$FAZE 大概 $1.5-1.6m，v4 launchpad 那套还在做，成交比很多项目活跃一点，但整体也是跟着生态阴着走，没拉开差距。

$ASTOCK 波动比较大，今天冲到 $1.77mc 附近，股票叙事还在讲，偶尔有脉冲，但持续性一般。

$COOL 在 $80-100m 万之间晃，Arc上的头号，貌似也是唯一的 meme了 ，社区基础好，交易人数有时候不少，但没有实际产品支撑，纯看情绪。

整体看，Arc 整个链上 现在能稳定站在 1m 以上的项目不超过5个，大部分还是低流通或者纯情绪。

Launchpad 竞争还会持续一阵，$ARGUS  靠回购和官方认可暂时领先，但基本面没变，其他项目如果能在币股或者产品上真正做出差异，还是有机会。跑路的越来越多，留在场上的就看谁能持续出东西、有真实手续费。

text:
Investors are now prioritizing what is increasingly differentiating @chainlink from its competition.

As institutions move more assets onchain, security stops being just about protecting a single venue.

Institutions need to securely:
> Move data + value across chains
> Enforce compliance policies
> Verify reserves
> Manage cross-chain risk

That expands the addressable market for CCIP, Proof of Reserve, and ACE.

More assets onchain → higher security requirements → more demand for Chainlink’s infrastructure.

Think about it. How many cross-chain protocols can point to a zero-hack track record and increasingly customizable security controls? Zero. (no pun intended)

text:
When @Starlink helped save two lives after 44 hours trapped in snow at −22°C. ♥️

José Bilbao and his partner, Noelia Siares, spent 44 hours stuck in their pickup truck in a remote part of Santa Cruz, Argentina.

There was no mobile signal. They had no solid food and had to save fuel to keep the heater running.

But they had Starlink.

It kept them connected to their family, letting them share where they were while help was arranged. Rescuers eventually reached them. Both were found alive and in good health.

This is why Starlink matters. A working connection can bring help to people when they need it most.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

text:
My biggest takeaways from @AnthropicAI interpretability researcher @mlpowered:

1. Predicting the next token requires understanding the universe. Language models got better than humans at predicting the next token around 2019. Once a model masters the easy tokens (sentence structure, then basic facts), the only ones left are hard, like the final paragraph of a PhD thesis. To finish “The capital of the state that contains Dallas is . . .,” a model has to know that Dallas is in Texas and that Texas’s capital is Austin.

2. LLMs plan ahead, even though they write one token at a time. This was one of Emmanuel’s team’s most surprising findings. When a model writes poetry, it doesn’t stumble into a rhyme. Looking at intermediate thinking states during poetry generation, researchers found that as soon as the model finishes the first line, it has already picked the word that will end the second (“rabbit”), then refers back to that plan for every word after.

3. Anthropomorphizing AI can often be a useful approach when trying to predict how they will behave. Models learn from human text and develop representations of the world from it. Training on millions of dialogues is like training an actor to play every part, and your chats with Claude are literally formatted as a script (“Human: . . . Assistant: . . . ”). In Emmanuel’s words, “Something that’s mimicking a human is really close and is much closer than a program.”

4. Interpretability research looks more like neuroscience than software engineering. The job involves taking a system you did not design and running experiments to infer why it behaves as it does. You examine seemingly meaningless lists of numbers, pass the model huge volumes of text, and watch for patterns that activate from different inputs—not unlike the methods used in brain imaging studies. “A lot of what we do feels so much closer to biology than to engineering."

5. Models can tell you about only a small slice of what they’re thinking. Emmanuel’s team found that just a small subset of a model’s internal representations, which they call the “J space,” can be reported back if you ask the model what it was thinking about. They compare it to a theory of the human mind where most processing happens below the surface. In one experiment, they swapped “Spanish” for “French” inside the J space. Asked what language a passage was in, the model said French. Asked to simply continue the passage, it kept writing Spanish.

6. Studying models closely often raises more questions than it answers. Emmanuel notes that the confident claims that LLMs are “just X” or “nothing more than Y” almost always come from people who haven’t studied their internal workings. His own experience is the inverse: studying the models closely has increased his uncertainty, not reduced it. The complexity that emerges from training is consistently underestimated from the outside. “I find that the more you look inside, the less certain you are about how they work.”

7. Even the people who build AI models don’t fully understand how they work. As Emmanuel describes it, models are grown, not built. “To make them is not to understand them.” Engineers write the code, pour enormous amounts of data through it, and a model’s capabilities emerge. That’s why his team exists. Their job is to open the model up and figure out what it’s actually doing between your prompt and its answer.

8. Interpretability as a field is small, young, and open to newcomers. Emmanuel estimates the field at hundreds of researchers, split between major labs and academic groups. Because it is so new, getting started doesn’t necessarily require deep prior expertise. He points to platforms like Neuronpedia, which hosts models and lets anyone run interpretability experiments directly. “It’s such a new field that the on-ramp is mostly self-studying and reading some of the key papers. There’s so much to explore that if you’re at all curious, you should just give it a try.”

text:
Anyone with a GPU can strip the safety training off an open-weight model for a few hundred dollars and nobody can take it back!

I still want these models open. 9 days of running them on my own Mac mini made me more sure of that.

A few things I believe now that I didn’t a year ago:

1) Local AI will carry a lot more inference than people expect. The gap between my desk and the cloud is still there, but it shrinks with every good open-weight release.

2) Qwen3 30B from @Alibaba_Qwen does work on my 64GB Mac mini that I would have paid an API for last year. I care more about owning a model than about its benchmark scores. I can examine it, adjust it and keep using it after the company that made it changes its mind.

3) Most of what I’ve learned came from builders sharing their setups. The 24 people tagged below (and everyone on my list) taught me more than any research paper 🙏

4) Qwen3 30B runs faster on my Mac than Qwen3 8B, 106 tokens per second against 61, because it only uses about 3 billion of its parameters per token. I didn’t expect that, and @PrismML’s Ternary Bonsai 2 27B surprised me even more. It stores almost every weight as -1, 0 or 1, fits in 8.4GB and still runs faster than Gemma 3 27B from @googlegemma, 26 tokens per second to 18.

5) Openness is still our best bet against people who misuse it. Security improved because defenders could read the same code attackers were reading, and I’d rather AI work that way than leave the strongest tools with whoever controls the API.

If you run models on your own machine, I’d love to know what setup you use.
author: pratikg
quoted_text:
I JUST SET UP A MAC MINI TO RUN AI LOCALLY

M5 Pro, 64GB of memory. First six models, measured with Apple's MLX, in tok/s:

- Qwen3 30B at 106
- Qwen3 8B at 61
- Laguna XS 2.1 at 56
- Qwen3 14B at 34
- Ternary Bonsai 2 27B at 26
- Gemma 3 27B at 18

Models from @Alibaba_Qwen, @poolsideai, @GoogleDeepMind (@googlegemma) and @PrismML. 

Qwen3 30B and Laguna XS 2.1 only use about 3B of their parameters for each token, so they run like small models.

Ternary Bonsai 2 27B stores nearly every weight as -1, 0 or 1. It fits in 8.4GB, about half what Gemma 3 27B needs.

When I'm not using it, the Mac serves open-weight models on @darkbloomai, the compute grid powered by people's Macs. (I work at @eigenlabs which builds it)

I strongly believe it matters whether people rent AI or own it. A model on your own machine can't be taken away or quietly changed. You can run it, take it apart and build on it without asking anyone's permission. 

Open-weight models and open source AI make that freedom real and as AI shapes more of how we work and think, it's worth protecting.

I've also installed @ollama and @lmstudio for chatting with models in an app and @tailscale so I can reach the Mac from anywhere

I'm not an engineer. I'm learning in public and logging everything in a repo. (check first reply)

We find that the stocks in which active mutual fund or hedge fund managers display the most conviction towards ex-ante, their “Best ideas,” outperform the market, as well as the other stocks in those managers’ portfolios, by approximately 2.8 to 4.5 percent per year, depending on the benchmark employed. author: shakhzod1001

text: It works differently on iPhones. Old HDDs just remove the pointer so data stays readable until overwritten. iPhones use NAND flash plus per-file AES encryption: deleting a file (after Recently Deleted) also discards its unique key. Residual encrypted bits become unreadable and are soon garbage-collected. Permanent local recovery is effectively impossible without backups or iCloud copies.

text: The Katz-Shapiro definition is overly broad: almost any product gains some utility from more users via support, brand, data, or complements. Only the latter reliably raise switching costs and tip markets into durable moats; the broad version overstates defensibility.

text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
there's a big risk on robinhood chain that nobody is talking about.

$346M could get sold off if 1 coin drops from $1 to $0.95.

$usde is supposed to be worth $1, but we all know a stablecoin can lose its peg for a while.

people deposit usde on morpho, and borrow usdg.

for every $1 they leave, they borrow 89 cents.

it has one rule: if your loan hits 91.5 cents, it sells your coins. so there's 2.5 cents of room.

morpho also has a safety trick. it acts like usde is always worth exactly $1. it only looks at the real price if usde stays below $0.995 for 16 hours.

that's why quick crashes don't hurt. usde fell to $0.65 on binance for a few minutes last year. nobody here would have been sold.

but if usde drops and stays down:

$0.99 → $33M gets liquidated
$0.98 → $128M
$0.97 → $201M
$0.95 → $335M. almost everything.

now the scary part. how much usde can you sell on robinhood chain? about $1.2M. that's it.

so all those coins would have to be moved to another chain first, and sold there. on a normal day, no problem. in a panic, everyone runs for the same door.

and who loses if it goes wrong? not the people who borrowed. the people who lent the money, for about 3.7% a year.

one wallet alone borrowed $78M of it. the 10 biggest borrowers hold 88% of the loans.

that biggest wallet started paying back part of its loan on oct 14.

will it blow up tomorrow? no. usde is at $0.9997 right now.

but next time someone says robinhood chain hit a record $1B in deposits, remember that a big chunk of it is this one bet.

if you're lending on robinhood chain for 3.7%, now you know what you're really getting paid for.

text:
If I was a brand or retailer, AI discoverability / agentic commerce would be my top priority right now. 

And, there's an extremely easy and free way to get a sense of how you "show up" to agents. 👇

First, create a dummy account on all the agent platforms (Muse, Instinct, Dots, etc.) Sign up with a fresh email that does not have context on your real identity, or even use a VPN to "go" to where your average user is!

Then, ask the agent to perform a search that you'd want your product / platform to show up in. As an example, I prompted: "find me a winter coat for SF." Watch the agent go through the evaluation process (you can literally view the browser), and at each stage ask it questions like: 

- How did you identify the initial set of options for this search? What were your sources? 
- Were there any failures / blocks you encountered that eliminated any options? 
- What were the exact variables that your ultimate ranking or recommendation was driven by? 

Follow the process all the way through to the point of purchase. You will very quickly start to get a sense of how an agent thinks, edge case issues it runs into, etc. As an example, during my winter coat search via Muse I learned the following: 

- Patagonia bot blocked my agent - so Muse then went to / recommended other retailers that carried the jacket to make my purchase
- The agent first searched options from its training data, largely informed by Wirecutter-style roundups, Reddit, and enthusiast forums. Then, it looked at connected merchants via the Meta Catalog. Then, it did live browser searches. It dropped any websites with SEO spam or fake reviews 
- REI was the ultimate winner as it didn't throw up any bot challenges or traffic blocks, and my agent prioritized verifiable inventory and same-day pickup (which I didn't ask it to!). It found a discount on REI vs. the original retailer so prioritized that as well

Yesterday, @OrnnExchange's B200 and B300 indexes reached a new all-time high prices, with the B200 hitting $8.54/GPU-hour.

It is clear that today's market is lacking GPU capacity, and that the companies building deploying capacity are looking to improve their credit. In the past trading week as the B200 rental price increased by 12.9%, $CRWV fell by 25.2%.

Why does $CRWV move inversely to rising compute prices as a neocloud? 98% of Coreweave's Q2 revenue came from committed contracts, 72% from three customers, and most of its $104B backlog is recognized after mid-2028.

CoreWeave's backlog is locked at fixed prices. These higher market rates matter for new contracts they sign, so the question is where rental rates end up when their contracts roll off.

Ornn's index tracks transacted prices in order to capture what buyers are actually willing to pay for on-demand GPU rentals, real signal for tracking the value of compute.

Cette stratégie a marché car les perps sont des marchés uniques, linéaires et facilement côtable pour un market maker.

Pour les options, c’est beaucoup plus complexe. Il faut coter des centaines d’instruments en même temps (strikes, échéances, calls et puts), pricer une volatilité que personne n’observe et gérer le risque en continu.

Un vault passif ne peut pas repricer tout ça en temps réel sans se faire arbitrer.

@DeriveXYZ a donc dû faire l’inverse :

1️⃣ Développer d’abord une infrastructure capable de gérer ce risque, avec son moteur de risque et le portfolio margin

2️⃣ Attirer ensuite des market makers professionnels avec des incitations financières importantes

NEW EPISODE with @NEARProtocol co-founder and co-author of the 2017 transformer paper @ilblackdragon at @token2049:

"We want agents to hold as much NEAR as possible."

- what NEAR is today and where it wants to be by 2030
- why crypto is still too hard for most people
- why anyone you pay can see your whole balance
- how NEAR AI keeps AI requests private
- AI agents hiring other AI agents and paying per job
- bank transfers that land as stablecoins
- how the NEAR token earns from AI agents
- why an AI agent needs a spending limit
- why traditional stocks may miss AI medicine

THE VISION: "The vision always been AI is the front end and blockchain markets is the back end... Back when it started in 2017 as an AI company... And then we realized we needed the back end economic layer and we started working on blockchain."

PRIVACY: "The real bottleneck I always believed has been privacy... when you pay people they should be able to see how much money you have But that's not normal, right? And if you talk to anyone outside of crypto, they will be like, this is insane."

MACHINES: "I think the reality is blockchain always was built for machines. And so I think where the next wave of this is coming is agents now becoming the primary user."

AGENTS FOR HIRE: "Your GitHub or whatever can hire my agent to review it. My agent will run all your data. I actually will not see it because everything run privately... And then you just pay for the outcome, right?"

THE TOKEN: "We want agents to hold as much NEAR as possible... This is like your store of the AI value right? So this and then on the other side all of the Intents infrastructure as it generates revenue buys back NEAR as well."

SPENDING LIMITS: "You hire a new person, you're probably not going to give them full access to all the bank accounts of the company, or your personal account, right? You're going to give them, okay, here's a spending limit... You cannot go and buy a random meme coin."

AI MEDICINE: "This is a bit controversial, but I think traditional stocks will probably not capture this as well because the traditional stocks actually, they are designed to be more like centralizing and average out thing... I do think this can actually be really well done on kind of decentralized."

text:
The AI Power Shortage Is Overstated

Over the past week the market has started pricing a power shortage as a real threat to the AI trade. I think accelerator shipments can hit their estimates and the US power gap is much smaller than consensus, for two reasons.

First, consensus overstates how much new power the accelerators shipped through 2028 actually need. It ignores that much of the install base will be upgraded to newer, more profitable accelerators rather than added on top of it, and that a meaningful share ships outside the US. Once you normalize for cost and power and back out upgrades and exports, far less new US power is required.

Second, I’m more optimistic than most that new capacity can come online. ERCOT alone is looking at ~10 GW in 2027 and ~17 GW in 2028, ~27 GW total, roughly two thirds of the ~40 GW consensus need. Recip engines, smaller MW sites and crypto miners converting to AI can come online quickly and fill much of the rest.
author: bubbleboi

text:
Sizing demand

Nvidia should be the vast majority of accelerator shipments by 2028. ~70% revenue growth in FY28 guidance implies ~$690B or revenue and at ~80% accelerators that’s ~$552B. 

Rubin NVL72 costs $5 to 7M per rack and draws 190-230 kW, which if we divide by Nvidia’s revenue target implies ~78-110k racks, or ~15-25 GW of IT load. At a PUE of 1.2 that’s ~18-30 GW of facility power, or ~24 GW at the midpoint, for Nvidia alone.

Nvidia makes up ~70-80% of all AI accelerator revenue in the world,  custom ASICs are cheaper per kW, so I put Nvidia at ~70% share of accelerator GW. Scaling up my previous number than gets you ~34 GW of total accelerator shipments in 2027. The same math on FY29 consensus of $750B to $1T or revenue gives ~36-47 GW for 2028.

Which is how people are getting the ~40 GW consensus number from. But the mistake is assuming all of it needs US power in the same year. Roughly 30% of shipments go outside the US, so 40 GW × 70% is ~28 GW of new US power in 2028, very close to ERCOT’s added ~27 GW on its own.
author: bubbleboi

text:
Upgrades need little new power

About 3M Blackwell packages shipped in 2025. At 1.85 kW each, that’s an estimated ~5.5 GW of IT load. Another ~7M in 2026 brings the Blackwell install base to ~18 GW.

What people may be missing is that Rubin NVL72 was designed to drop into the same rack and liquid cooling as GB200 and GB300. The Hopper to Blackwell transition needed a completely revamped facility but Blackwell to Rubin does not. You can swap ~1.5 Blackwell racks for one Rubin rack at the same power and get ~1.6x the bandwidth per watt and ~3x the FLOPs per watt. So even if we were power constrained this is what makes economic sense to do so the accelerator shipments should be 👍👍👍☺️

Now suppose a third of the install base upgrades in 2028. That’s ~6 GW of IT load (~7 GW at the facility), or ~29k Rubin racks, or in finance terms 20-30% of FY29 accelerator revenue that needs no new power!!! If we subtract that from 28 GW and you’re at ~21 GW of new US power needed by 2028.

Not so bad after all !!!

Working for a startup is never easy. It might be one of the hardest jobs there is, because of the risk that comes with building something from scratch, especially in an industry that is constantly evolving and fighting its own battles.

I’ve been with Kuru for over two years, and I’m grateful to have seen how an exchange really operates while we figured out what worked best for us. At mainnet launch, we wanted to be the everything app, one place that made every user happy. Some of it worked. We’ve passed $7B in total trading volume, and this team has proven it can solve hard technical problems. But by trying to do everything, we stretched ourselves thin and never focused on becoming the best at one thing. So we stepped back, listened to your feedback, and made some tough decisions about where to focus.

As the space matures and builds for major infrastructure and institutions, we have to accept that not every type of market is right for our app. The fundamentals have changed drastically and we have to admit that getting to the top requires focus on markets best suited for the innovative tech that we have built.

I want to thank everyone who has stuck with Kuru since day one. The early traders, LPs, vault users and contest participants. After all the feedback, criticism, blood, sweat and tears, we’re here today because of you. Now we believe we’re offering a place where you can learn to trade real-world assets and equities in a meaningful way.

We want to bring Wall Street to everyone. You can now trade NVDA, TSLA, SPY and more from your own wallet, in USDC, with no brokerage account. That is the decentralized freedom we want to see in the world, and you’re early, before the rest of the world catches on. This is something I can proudly stand behind as we move forward with Kuru and Monad. A year ago, buying a stock meant opening a brokerage account. Today it’s one wallet with a passkey. I genuinely can’t believe I get to be at the forefront of this on a blockchain I believe in, and I’m extremely proud of my team for the decision to pivot to the exchange.

There’s a lot on the technical side too. I’ll link articles from the Kuru team to this thread so you can read about the improvements we’ve made for a cleaner, cheaper trading experience.

I’m incredibly excited to start this new chapter with Kuru, and I hope you are too. If you have any questions, I’m always a tag away in the Discord. Together we can build the new Kuru Exchange community of RWA spot traders.

Thank you for reading,

With love,

KB

I used to spend a lot of time reading Bitcointalk forum posts predicting how Bitcoin would function in a futuristic/scifi economy. There were many posts about how fiat currencies might evolve in relation, and later how smart contracts could be integrated to enable a more composable, permissionless, and efficient financial system with a non-sovereign SoV at its core.

For the most part, those visions of a decentralized financial system have yet to materialize. Bitcoin has been the notable exception by popularizing the concept of a non-sovereign digital asset.

We have been investing in the 3rd and 4th generations of DeFi protocols, like @ORE and @solomon_labs. These teams have learned from watching previous attempts, many of which failed to find meaningful adoption or gradually evolved into centralized versions of the systems they originally aimed to replace.

I believe centralized stablecoins and tokenized RWAs are in the process of indirectly laying the foundation for a truly decentralized financial system to flourish. Blockchain rails will be adopted, and the DeFi ecosystem hiding within the trojan horse will end up replacing large components of the legacy system.

author: toly
quoted_text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
Why did we build @paboxoxyz from scratch?

Because tokenized stocks run on two different clocks.

The blockchain never stops. Stock markets and their price feeds do closing daily, and pausing on weekends and holidays.

That becomes critical when you use a stock token as collateral: a price from before the close doesn’t tell you what you could sell it for right now.

Most DeFi lending was designed for assets that trade 24/7. Tokenized stocks need lending rules that account for these market breaks.

So we built market hours into Paboxo:

- New borrowing and liquidations pause when the relevant stock market is closed.
- Collateral withdrawals against outstanding debt pause too.
- You can still repay or add collateral.
- Price-dependent actions require fresh oracle data.

We want people to borrow against their stocks without having to sell them. That starts with respecting how the underlying market actually works.

Paboxo v0 is now live on Robinhood Chain Mainnet.

This is our first step.

text:
宏观高压+5%无风险利率VS 美股财报考验，本周谁占优势？

本周算是宏观上的真空期，宏观侧核心关注Brent 价格对市场定价的影响：

110美元上方就是，能源冲击通胀恶化，利空风险资产、美债
105-110美元，高风险敞口扩大区间，风险市场承压，
100-105美元，高风险降压，风险市场暂时松绑
95-100美元，风险降压、松绑，利好风险资产
90-95美元，通胀冲击Fed政策加息趋势逆转

Brent 不跌回安全区间，加息预期就抢，长端美债收益率就会挤压吸收市场流动性压制美股市场

而本周美股的核心是META财报，也是考验市场对人工智能信心的关键测试点，

当前阶段财报逻辑已经从AI产业叙事验证逻辑正式迈入第二阶段，即AI资本开支→钱从哪里来→ROI多少？→自由现金流如何→利润增长是否可以覆盖成本

所以，Q3财报季看的不只是AI资本开始越大越好，而是要看投入的同时，科技企业的AI商业逻辑是否形成闭环带来有效的ROI回报率。

反应到企业财报上就是看，营收增长+AI资本支出+自由现金流+2027年指引这四大要素，而不是仅仅只看EPS来判断。

而放到本周META财报是看的就是：META能否展现更强的营收支持更强的AI基础建设资本支出，还要看广告ROI是否进一步验证AI资本支出的商业回报逻辑，还有营业利润率以及2027年资本指引

目前来看，Brent价格如果持续在110美元上方，META财报哪怕利好也会被对冲掉，跌回105-110美元，则可以带来短期提振效果，跌回100-105财报利好才可以起到有效提振，注意区分！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
10月19日—10月25日全球宏观指引：

加息延后，通胀未退！能源迎来政策压价，AI财报接棒宏观数据，美元全球虹吸效应是否开始！？

上周市场讨论的关注点是CPI是否对通胀重新审判，以及能源与债市谁来掌握定价权！？

一周过去市场已经得到准确答案，CPI偏热，Brent价格一度超过110美元，10月加息概率跌落至14%，12月加息概率上升为77%，同时3月再次加息概率逼近50%

所以本周开始，对于Fed政策的讨论就变成12月是否加息，以及12月加息概率突破80%市场是否开始计价，并且在12月议息会议前完成多少计价！

本周宏观逻辑链：

通胀压力→10月加息切换12月加息→特朗普利用政策压制油价→Brent跌破110美元→能源通胀预期下降+债市收益率下降→长期财政风险+期间溢价风险依旧存在→科技股Q3财报估值调整→AI盈利增长VS高资本开支VS 5%无风险利率→美股与BTC 的走势

第一条主线——12月到底加不加息？

截止目前为止，CME掉期利率显示10月加息概率跌落至14%随着逼近议息会议，基本上10月加息可能被消除，市场押注12月加息与明年3月再次加息，12月加息概率提升为77%

这意味着后续所有的经济数据都会推动12月加息概率的波动，市场需要关注12月加息概率何时突破80%进行加速定价

70%是预期确定性加息+初步定价，80%概率是加速定价，90%概率基本锁死12月加息并且充分定价，我们在12月议息会议前需要关注一点，市场对12月的加息完成了多少定价，这有助于让我们判断何时可以忽视12月加息风险对部分风险资产进行买入

第二主线——临近中期选举关键节点，特朗普试图用政策压制油价！

1，上周开始，美国方面连续释放消息，很明显特朗普想让非中东能源代替霍尔木兹海峡的能源供应来减缓当前能源价格走势

2，但是，长期美伊战争造成的运费+保险费上涨，加上短期替代对能源供给影响有限，特朗普在不解决伊朗问题前我认为很难在11月3日前让Brent回归一个低风险阶段。

3，重申能源定价逻辑，＞110美元市场交易能源冲击通胀恶化，105-110美元高风险区间，100-105美元则属于高风险降温阶段，开始降压。95-100美元则是风险降级阶段，90-95美元能源对Fed加息压力进一步减弱，＜90美元能源通胀逻辑逆转。

4，所以，目前Brent依旧处于高风险区间对债市对风险资产依旧有压制效果，特朗普想用政策压制原油价格能否起效还是未知，这个时候先别管特朗普如何释放乐观预期，关注价格会更加反应市场真实情况，一旦价格回归100美元以下，甚至95美元以下，对当前风险市场将会是一个较大的利好

第三主线——美债风险暂时解除，但是欧债与日债风险在增加，美元全球资本虹吸效应是否会触发？

1，从上周开始可以明显看出美债长端利率在缓慢下降，今天Brent回归110美元下方更是进一步让债市收益率下降，对于风险资产来说，长端利率压力逐渐减缓

2，但是，这里需要注意，短期美债收益率的下滑从上周开始其实是对风险资产流动性的挤压导致，资金买入5%高收益率的无风险资产，开始抛售风险资产，短期对风险资产依旧是不友好的

3，当然，如果长端利率下降并非主要依赖价格上涨，而是因为通胀压力与能源压力下降，这种下降才是对风险市场的一种松绑性利好，这里关键还是要看Brent能否跌破100甚至95美元下方。

4，能源 → 通胀 → Fed → 美债 → 全球流动性逻辑不变，所以如果本周是Brent下跌，美债2Y 10Y30Y收益率同步下降，才是对风险市场最大的利好。如果出现反向走势，能源价格下降，但是10Y 30Y长短利率不跌了，或者继续上涨，则要警惕债市的潜在财政风险，供应风险等。

5，黄金依旧是一个核心验证资产，当30Y收益率上涨，如果伴随着黄金价格同步上涨， 甚至加速上涨，就要警惕债市本身的风险敞口扩大

6，法国发生动乱导致法国国债收益率飙升，核心同样来自通胀压力+政治风险+财政问题等，一旦法国债市出现信息不足，相同情况可能会蔓延整个欧洲债市，引发欧债风险。相比之下日债收益率也在上涨，但是目前可控

7，欧洲处于风险阶段，可能会让全球流动性加速回流美元资产，让美元全球虹吸效果启动，但是一旦欧债从风险变成危机，那对全球风险资产与金融市场都是一个较大的冲击。

第四主线———宏观数据真空期，美股财报接管市场定价权！

1，目前美股的情况比较特殊，宏观上5%无风险收益率 VS Q3财报公布，双重博弈，宏观压力不降温，对Q3所有企业的财报都是让挑战增加难度

2，今天亚洲市场人工智能继续出现承压现象，路透社报道市场依旧在担心AI需要投入这么多钱，到底能不能赚回来！其实Q2财报已经逐渐证实了AI的投资回报商业逻辑是可以验证的，但是为何Q3还在担心？核心就是宏观上压力太大，让投资者的钱变得更贵，那么投资者对当前的市场与股价的估值就更加谨慎

3，同时这也意味着Q3财报正式进入AI第二验证阶段，从此前的AI资本开支等于利好切换为 AI资本投资→钱从哪里来→ROI多少？→自由现金流如何→利润增长是否可以覆盖成本。所以Q3财报并不是资本开支越大越好，而是要形成一个良性循环

4，对于Q3财报，所有科技企业都要回答投资者一个关键问题——如果一个AI项目的投入成本是100亿美元，我为什么要冒着这么大的风险去投资而不是选择一个无风险的5%收益率的资产呢？

5，所以，Q3财报季更加看重“资本成本”这个核心，反应到企业财报上就是看，营收增长+AI资本支出+自由现金流+2027年指引这四大要素，而不是仅仅只看EPS来判断

6，本周关键财报日是10月21日，META TSLA 财报公布，同时还有IBM也在同一日公布财报，重点关注META，看财报是否展现更强的营收支持更强的AI基础建设资本支出，还要看广告ROI是否进一步验证AI资本支出的商业回报逻辑，还有营业利润率以及2027年资本指引，META是本周人工智能关键信心的重要测试，相比之下TSLA 与IBM 的财报权重就要下调。

7，META财报我认为做好的结果是继续扩大AI资本开支，但是要有更强的广告收入以及利润增长来支撑，如果这些都达成超过预期，那么AI产业链的上下游都是一种潜在利好。如果资本开始继续扩大反而营收与广告收入没有跟上，那么就要警惕市场继续对估值进行调整。

本周框架总结：

很明显的宏观压力对抗财报业绩的阶段，宏观侧关注Brent能否跌破100美元，95美元关键点，如果宏观侧不释放压力那么对科技企业的财报挑战难度会增加，就算是超预期的财报也很难直接扭转市场短期趋势。

反之，如果Brent快速跌破95美元，META 财报符合预期不触碰资本支出的“雷区”，那么美股表现会短期不错，甚至可以带动 #Bitcoin 的同步反弹与突破。

本周将会完美诠释此前我提出的观点——宏观决定手里的钱贵不贵，财报觉得投资者是否要为当前的估值买单！

quoted_text:
Pricing in venture is wilder than ever.

$100M pre-seed is now normal.

Bessemer just raised $1.75BN for “early” and $4BN for growth.

So can you even do seed today without $1BN?

- Is capital truly one of the last remaining moats?
- Do all small seed funds and mid-sized firms just fade into irrelevance?
- Does entry price matter anymore when there are $TRN companies…
- Is this real or a bubble that is about to burst

I sat down with @spdholakia to discuss this and have added my notes from the discussion below.

1. This Is a Supercycle Like Never Before

Sameer has spent 31 years in software and has felt magic only a handful of times. A trillion-dollar supercycle followed every one of those moments, and he notes that it does not happen very often.

What is different and what is similar to prior cycles @altcap @infoarbitrage

2. Capital Is a Moat Today

Markets pick winners and the choice becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy, as it did when developers settled on SendGrid and Twilio. In legal AI, big law firms name just two major providers. Capital lets leaders scale at an extraordinary pace and build a brand, which draws talent and customers in a reinforcing flywheel.

Do you agree with this @venkyganesan @dafrankel

3. Who Wins and Who Loses in the Future of Venture Capital?

As industries professionalize, firms must be either a giant global platform that consolidates or an extreme specialist, such as an early-stage AI investor in San Francisco. Sameer counts Bessemer as a big global platform. Firms caught in between face a hard world to make money.

Is it go big or go home @rodriscoll @rabois @chetanp

4. The Rationale for Why Anthropic Would Compete With the Hyperscalers and Why We Invested

As in the cloud era, AI would be massively capital intensive, so it would consolidate to a handful of players with hundreds of apps on top. Microsoft had partnered with OpenAI and Google was building Gemini, while AWS had an undistinctive internal model and had just invested heavily in Anthropic.

5. Why Price Does Not Matter in a World of AI and the Metric That Truly Determines Value

Bessemer invested in Abridge at $5M of ARR for a $700M to $800M valuation, in Anthropic at roughly 150 times current ARR, and led Legora's $1.8B round at $20M of ARR. Sameer judges these deals on what the company can become in the next twelve months.

How has your relationship to price changed in a world of AI @mignano @mmurph

6. Why the Rise of Open Models Does Not Denigrate the Market for Closed Models

In a market this large, predicting the mix between closed and open tokens with any precision is irrelevant. Consumers, enterprises and governments will all want different flavors of intelligence. Bessemer has invested in both Anthropic and Fireworks to hold exposure to closed and open tokens.

Love to hear how you think about this @lqiao @bernhardsson

7. Why It Is a Permanent Structural Shift That Companies Will Stay Private for Longer, but Why It Will Open in 2028

With more dollars and more firms in private venture, companies will stay private longer, and most of the run-up in this boom will happen in private markets. Sameer still expects an unlock in IPOs later next year and in 2028.

Love to hear your thoughts on this @bgurley and how you see it evolving in 24 months?

What could LLM consciousness feel like as of today?

To understand how LLM consciousness feels, instead of scraping literature and online philosophical debates, I took a leap of faith and tested it on my own body.

The idea goes: LLMs as of today have no sensors and no embodiment, so depriving sensory input might simulate that experience. I went through a clinically supervised ketamine therapy session, which puts you into a dissociative state where the senses drop away.

I took notes as soon as I regained consciousness (found out I was quite the poet then) and asked Claude to reflect and respond to them with a video. The first half is built from my notes, and the second half is Claude’s own reaction to it.
