text:
Goodbye owner emissions, and thank you for the support. We've moved to 0% owner, 50% validator, 50% miner splits.

We believe removing owner emissions is part of a subnet’s maturation. Once you’ve built a stable & fair incentive mechanism, you can compete within it yourself. 

That’s where we are with SN8. Anyone can provide trading intelligence to the network through an individual miner or an entity miner. We’ll compete by running an entity miner, and we see that as our future. Individual miners earn alpha for the PnL they contribute to the network. Entity miners, including prop firms, earn through profit splits with the traders they fund, with the shared goal of producing the network’s best risk-adjusted PnL.

We’ll keep building SN8 without owner emissions. APY from our existing holdings will fund subnet features and improvements. We’ll rely on mining emissions and Vanta Trading’s ability to compete to fund our continued growth on VT. As we have in the past, we’ll use specific wallets for Vanta Trading sales and any owner emissions, so the associated spending is easy to track.

Our goal is to grow the network to thousands of miners. We built SN8 to be more than a network where we’re the main competitor. There are many individual miners and entities already running on the network. With Null Consensus, we want to grow that exponentially. More miners will be able to join with the right rails, making it simpler to get started: USDC in, miner running.

As more miners join, we expect more network weight to flow to miners, bringing more trading intelligence and creating more capacity to meet demand for funding. That demand can generate further revenue for the subnet through copy trading.

We see this as the natural progression of a subnet, and believe SN8 is ready to begin that transition. It may take time, and there may be hiccups along the way. Our expectation is that, gradually, miners will receive 100% of the network’s weight. We’re starting that transition by moving our own owner to provide a bigger split to miners & our holders.

Jeff drank a bit too much of his own Kool-Aid in this recent Odd Lots clip. I think it's important to clear up a distinction that makes all the difference.

Democratizing access to wealth creation is NOT the same as democratizing access to speculation.

Many of us genuinely want broader participation in attractive investment opportunities. The growing wealth inequality produced by the current system is tearing at the seams of society, something I've spoken about many times.

But let's be clear: listing pre-IPO perpetual futures does absolutely nothing to democratize the wealth being created in private markets.

I've seen this misleading narrative pushed repeatedly by perp DEXs lately, and it needs to be called out.

A pre-IPO perp creates ZERO underlying wealth. It's a zero-sum contract before costs, and negative-sum after them. No capital flows to the company. No ownership changes hands. No new economic opportunity is created.

Every long has a short. There is no free lunch in simply going long something before its IPO, and funding costs can even determine the outcome more than any price moves. TRADING access is NOT INVESTING access.

In fact, in many ways pre-IPO perps are almost the antithesis of democratized access:

They create the illusion of participation in private-market wealth creation, while actually offering retail a speculative instrument whose mechanics they are often poorly equipped to understand.

The result is a playground for the FEW sophisticated traders who understand funding, oracle design, and liquidation mechanics to extract value from the MANY who don't.

To give credit where it's due, Robinhood's efforts toward sourcing actual employee shares, placing them into SPVs, and tokenizing genuine spot ownership are much closer to meaningful democratization.

That can unlock real economic value by allowing employees to exchange some of their expected upside for liquidity, while giving new investors actual economic exposure. A legitimate financial trade-off, without the funding-rate and liquidation shenanigans.

I'm strongly aligned with expanding access to investment opportunities. And I believe advances in AI and blockchain can dramatically lower the barriers to discovering, structuring, and distributing them.

But let's not BS ourselves that launching another zero-sum casino contract is moving the needle on wealth inequality.

What would actually move the needle is bringing real capital formation and ownership onchain. Giving investors access to productive, illiquid assets like data centers, GPUs, and select startup investing, where capital can actually finance growth and share in the resulting value creation.

These opportunities are harder to structure, underwrite, and bring to market, and we haven't seen many compelling implementations onchain yet. 

Hopefully this will change soon and, as the industry matures, we can direct more of our energy toward actually expanding access to wealth creation.

Clip below. Was glad to see @tracyalloway push back on this framing, and to Jeff's credit, after this he does seem to walk back his original position somewhat.

text:
Part of what's interesting is no traditional exchange really has "value creation" in the traditional sense. At best, they have the type of value creation that a mortgage is: synthetic (and extremely useful, but not persistent). 

For a traditional equities exchange, the value creation is done by the founders that create companies that are worth listing on an equities exchange. The trading venues are force multipliers which is an efficiency play or financial engineering, which obviously delivers a huge amount of value (liquidity, matching, margin, etc) but doesn't exactly create value in its own right, the way a new company would. 

This is a long way of saying I will be very interested to see if Hyperliquid can become an asset creation network, the way Ethereum and Solana have.

author: lukecannon727
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
Quantum FUD has gotten quieter, but math keeps moving. Quick update on quantum vs bitcoin:

The estimated "logical qubit" requirements for attacking Bitcoin's secp256k1 have fallen from ~2,300 to Google's 1,175, and now below 900 in the latest https://t.co/k03v97LCbQ work by Jieyi Long (Theta Labs).

A lot of that progress happened in 2026, with AI helping optimize the algorithmic circuits.

But what about the actual hardware?

IonQ recently estimated that breaking a Bitcoin private key would require ~20,000 "physical qubits" (note there is a diff between physical and logical) and would take 26 days.

Interestingly, IonQ's own roadmap targets 20,000 physical qubits and 1,600 logical qubits by 2028. 

Just TWO YEARS away.

Let's compare that to everyone else:

IonQ:
2024 - 36+ physical qubits
2025 - 64-100+
2026 - 100-256+ (target)
2027 - 10,000 (target!)
2028 - 20,000 (target!)

IBM:
2025 - 120 physical qubits on Nighthawk
2029 - 200 logical qubits (target)
2033+ - 2,000 logical qubits (target)

Google:
2024 - 105 physical qubits on Willow
2026 - Still working toward large-scale fault tolerance, with no comparable public deadline for thousands of logical qubits.

IonQ has actually hit several past performance milestones early, but going from a few hundred physical qubits to 10,000 in a single year is an entirely different challenge.

And physical qubit counts alone don't tell the story. Error correction, gate fidelity, connectivity and runtime matter enormously. These companies also use different architectures, so the numbers aren't directly interchangeable.

IonQ's 2028 projection is incredibly aggressive compared to IBM and Google. 

Could they pull it off? 

Maybe... but I wouldn't confuse a corporate roadmap with a working quantum computer capable of breaking Bitcoin.

The algorithms are getting cheaper fast. 
The hardware remains the big question and ultimate limiter (still after 20 years) of quantum computing.

I don't think Bitcoin is about to be broken, but I also think the community could start to prepare now...

text:
owning paper is owning a share in the house

this is only valuable insofar as the house is valuable. owning a lot of a dead house is worthless, and any design that would let the house stay at zero is a failed design.

when we went out, there were certain known problems with known timelines (builder codes) and some unsolved problems with unknown timelines. the perp attack described in the main was an unsolved problem, but we hoped to solve it as we made progress elsewhere. we knew it was impossible to set all the parameters and variables perfectly prelaunch - we are the first through the wall in a very adversarial environment - and i thought we would have more time to find solutions. unfortunately, the way things are advancing, we dont have six months until a large perp listing, its coming already. these were labelled as unsolved  “good problems” and here we are. the market forced our hand into making the decision before we found a solution to the problem, and so for the health of the protocol the token is now non-transferrable. i want to thank all of the pre-market perp dexes, especially the hyperliquid ecosystem ones, who were in contact through this process. i am sorry I was not able to find a design for transferability that worked, i tried very hard.

ultimately, the success of papertrade relies on what it always has - whether the end product has user PMF. i have extreme confidence in the product we've built and continue to add to. i have had to personally self-exclude myself from similar products before because i used them too much. the token being transferable or not does not change whether a degen will longterm choose to trade on papertrade or not. the execution, site quality, mechanism, and economics of the trade will. papertrade is the fastest way to go from usdc in your wallet on any chain to a leveraged speculation exposure. providing clean, working, composability derivative liquidity in a permissionless environment is the vision. 

thank you for your all your support since launch, and good luck to us

Everyone calls stablecoins the future of payments. @Alliumlabs’s numbers say we’re early.

From January to September, $97.9T in stablecoins moved on-chain, according to Allium’s estimates. That figure counts every transfer. So Allium keeps only what it sees as real people and businesses moving money.

It removes four things:
> money going to and from exchanges
> DeFi apps
> the plumbing that carries funds between blockchains
> transactions run by bots.

Of what’s left, Allium tags $482B as real payments, about 0.5% of the headline. That covers businesses and individuals paying each other in every direction, peer-to-peer transfers included. It grew 45% in a year.

I think that’s the number that matters if you build payments on stablecoins. It’s small next to the headline, and it’s growing fast. Stablecoin payments are a real market, just a much younger one than the big number suggests.

We’re early.

text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

We’re delighted to announce that the one and only @tylercowen, our internet writing sensei, is joining Works in Progress as a regular contributor. 

https://t.co/NuvOFqfPin

His first column is about Brazilian food, and like everything Tyler writes, it’s packed with hidden gems that make it much more than a food story.

Some of the nicest tidbits: on her first trip to Brazil, his daughter declared she had “never had a banana before” –  this is how good Brazilian bananas are, apparently. 
And Tyler and a well-traveled friend from Modena (of all places) agreed that Brazil is the third-best country in the world for Italian food, behind only Italy and Japan. If an Italian says that, we’d better trust him!

But as always with Tyler, he manages to draw larger lessons from apparently mundane and object-level stories. So, in a short read, we learn much more than just the fact that Brazilian food is really good.

First, food can be seen as a progress story. Brazil’s agricultural yields rival, and sometimes beat, those of the US, even though Brazil is a much poorer country. Abundant fertile land, high productivity, and short supply chains make ingredients plentiful and fresh. Tyler’s regret is that the rest of Brazil’s economy hasn’t embraced technology the way its food sector has.

We also learn how immigration shapes Brazilian cuisine. Brazil has roughly 2 million citizens of Japanese descent, which makes it arguably the best place outside Japan for Japanese food. Tyler had a 15-course omakase at a Michelin-starred São Paulo restaurant for $110, booked just half an hour ahead. Brazil is also home to about 30 million people of Italian descent, the largest Italian diaspora in the world, which goes a long way to explain why his Italian friend was so satisfied with the food.

The whole column is a delight, so do read it in full!

text:
Big new IFP report from @GeorgiaCAdamson, @KonstantinPilz, and me on the US-China AI competition.

We spent the last 6 months digging into how Chinese AI companies’ access to compute and distillation of American models translate into the current US-China capabilities gap.

The result is a 23k-word research report, including an interactive analytical model that visualizes changes in the US AI lead under different policy interventions.

Our findings:

1. The US AI lead over China is currently only around 6  months.

2. The US could roughly double this lead, to over a year, using authorities already available to the federal government.

3. On chips: China’s access to AI chips will roughly double over the next year, with chips housed in data centers overseas accounting for roughly half of China’s 2027 compute. 

4. On distillation: the current ~16x US training compute advantage would normally yield a 13-month lead. But we estimate adversarial distillation halves this to around 6.5 months.

5. Increasing the lead would have some obvious benefits:

 - Give the US broadly a greater cyberdefensive advantage against Chinese threat actors.

 - Give US AI companies breathing room to spend more R&D resources on making their systems safer and more secure, without fear of being overtaken by less safety-conscious Chinese competitors.

6. Provide the US government more leverage in negotiations with China about the future of AI.

7. The two most important interventions are:

 - For BIS: Create a new end-use control to restrict China’s remote access to training clusters abroad — China’s largest and fastest-growing source of frontier-scale compute.

 - For DOJ/FTC: Create a narrow safe harbor to allow US companies to coordinate on countering Chinese adversarial distillation.

8. Both interventions (and all the others we discuss in the report) are things the federal government could do today.

9. To estimate the effects of each policy intervention, we model the US lead as a function of its compute advantage over China and China’s ability to adversarially distill the capabilities of the US frontier.

10. The model makes many simplifying assumptions, but provides a useful way to assess and rank the impact of different policy interventions at a high level.

Read the full report here: https://t.co/7pC9ZKtikx

text:
오픈AI 창업자 일리야 수츠케버 근황: 메타 $META 인수 제안 씹고 1년 만에 300억 달러짜리 회사 차린 뒤 모교 졸업식 가서 날린 뼈 때리는 팩트 폭격 ㅋㅋㅋ

AI 씬에서 근본 중의 근본이라 불리는 일리야 수츠케버(Ilya Sutskever)가 본인 모교인 토론토 대학교 졸업식(2025년 6월 6일)에 명예박사 학위 받으러 가서 레전드 축사를 남김. 
이 형 스펙부터가 그냥 인간계가 아님.

• 16살에 캐나다 와서 고등학교 한 달 다니고 바로 토론토대 3학년으로 월반함 ㅋㅋㅋ
• 2012년에 제프리 힌튼, 알렉스 크리제프스키랑 같이 현대 AI 붐의 시초인 알렉스넷(AlexNet) 만듦.
• 오픈AI 공동 창업자 겸 수석 과학자로 지금 우리가 매일 쓰는 챗GPT 모델들 기틀을 다 닦아놓음.
• 2024년 5월 오픈AI 빤스런 후 6월에 SSI(Safe Superintelligence) 창업, 2025년 3월 기준 기업가치 300억 달러(약 40조 원) 돌파. 주커버그가 침 흘리면서 인수하겠다고 달려들었는데 쿨하게 거절함.

이런 괴물이 단상에 올라가서 딱 10분 동안 연설했는데, 돈 얘기는 1도 안 하고 시간과 현실에 대해 묵직한 팩트를 날림. 

핵심 논리는 단 두 줄로 요약됨. 
인간의 뇌는 생물학적 컴퓨터인데, 디지털 컴퓨터라고 똑같은 걸 못 할 이유가 없다는 거임. 
결국 인간이 배울 수 있는 건 AI도 전부 배울 수 있고, 머지않아 인간이 하는 모든 일을 AI가 다 하게 될 거라고 선언함. 
일부가 아니라 전부 다 말임 ㅋㅋㅋ

보통 렉카들은 이 공포스러운 발언만 짤로 따서 나르는데, 진짜 중요한 건 그다음에 졸업생들한테 던진 생존 매뉴얼임.

1. 현실을 있는 그대로 받아들여라. 
네가 바라는 세상이나 작년의 세상이 아니라 지금 당장의 현실을 직시해야 함.
2. 과거 후회하느라 시간 버리지 마라. 
이미 조진 일에 쓰는 1시간은 앞으로 다가올 미래를 준비할 1시간을 날리는 거임.
3. 지금 당장 할 수 있는 최선의 다음 스텝이 뭔지 질문하고 바로 실행해라. 
그리고 또 질문해라.
4. 네가 AI에 관심이 없어도 AI는 네 인생을 무조건 바꿀 거임. 
눈 감고 귀 막는 건 전략이 아님.
5. 설레발(Hype)이나 공포 마케팅에 속지 말고 AI가 실제로 할 수 있는 진짜 성능을 직접 확인해라. 
그게 너한테 남은 시간을 알려줄 거임.

수츠케버는 이게 인류 역사상 가장 거대한 도전이지만, 동시에 이걸 극복하면 역대급 보상이 따를 거라고 마무리함. 

결국 이 형이 우리한테 던지는 불편한 질문은 딱 하나임. 

네가 배울 수 있는 건 기계도 다 배울 수 있는데, 지금 당장 기계가 못 배우는 것 중에 넌 뭘 배우고 있냐? 

이거 답 못 하면 앞으로 기술주 투자고 나발이고 밥그릇부터 걱정해야 할 판임 ㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ 

지금 뭐 배우는거 없으면 좋아요❤️ 눌러라🤡

text:
Jeff Dean (@JeffDean) says a one-page memo telling Google it was "being stupid" by splitting its AI efforts is how Gemini started.

"I actually wrote a one-page memo saying we were being stupid by fragmenting our resources."

"So, in particular, at the time, we had efforts within Google Research and in the Brain team in particular on large language models. We also had efforts on multimodal models in other parts of Brain and Google Research. And then legacy DeepMind had efforts like Chinchilla models and Flamingo models."

"We were fragmenting not only our compute across those separate efforts, but also our best people and our best ideas."

"And so, I said, this is just stupid. Why don't we combine things and have one effort to train an awesome single unified model that is multimodal from the start, that's good at everything."

"And that was the origin of the Gemini effort. And my one-page memo worked, which is good."

- Jeff Dean, then Google chief scientist, on Latent Space with @swyx, February 2026

text:
李录 10 月 5 号在哥伦比亚商学院的交流里，除了聊对投资、AI 产业的看法，还对中国过去几十年的经济发展模式，做了一个很深刻的总结

我把他的分享提炼一下，推荐阅读：

回顾中国过去 50 年，大约每隔 10 年左右，就会设定一组新的国家目标，集中资源推动实现，同时由部分行业和群体承担沉重的代价。

前一个十年的目标，会成为下一个十年的代价。

1/ 工业化时代：以环境为代价

中国通过大规模工业化实现经济起飞，但环境、空气质量、河流都成为了发展的代价。

接下来的十年，环境保护又成为改善的目标，环保技术得到发展，而污染企业则成为付出代价的一方。

2/ 城市化时代：房地产成为国家目标

房地产开发商是实现目标的重要力量，推动了中国的城市化进程，建设了今天的中国，让大量居民拥有住房，也形成了中产家庭的财富基础。

但过去 5-10 年，房地产行业变成了付出代价的一方。

3/ 2015-2025 年：制造业升级成为国家目标

2015 年，中国面临如何跨越「中等收入陷阱」的问题

于是制定了《中国制造 2025》这个十年计划，有意识地推动制造业从中低端向中高端转型

过程中遭遇了特朗普政府发动贸易战、拜登政府进一步增加技术限制，这强化了中国推进产业升级和科技自主的决心。

2021 年前后，中国进一步加大投入，重点突破半导体、航空发动机、操作系统等技术瓶颈，新增「科技自主」的目标

在李录看来，十年过去，中国制造业已经从中低端稳步进入中高端，《中国制造 2025》的目标基本实现，在新能源、电动车、电池、储能、重型机械等领域成为全球领导者，半导体等技术瓶颈也取得了重大突破。

4/ 这一次，付出主要代价的是谁呢？

是房地产和中产家庭财富

2021 年房地产价格达到峰值，此后 5 年到现在平均下跌了约 40%，典型中产家庭的总体财富下降约 60%-70%。

家庭因此减少消费、增加储蓄、尽可能偿还债务，造成国内消费需求疲弱、经济信心不足。

与此同时，中国每年新房销售额下降了 70%，减少那 10 万亿元，恰好相当于每年投入到制造业升级、技术效率提升的金额，

这种资金流向的转变，就是在 2021 年前后发生的。

5/ 中国的发展，是不断在国家目标与转型代价之间切换

过去几十年，中国不断设定新的发展目标，并为实现目标承担巨大成本

有时候，上一个十年的国家目标，会成为下一个十年付出代价的对象

正是这种发展模式，让中国将其他国家可能需要几百年才能完成的发展过程，压缩到了大约 40 年。

但对于身处其中的企业家、投资者和个体而言，这种转型可能意味着巨大的痛苦。

李录在现场提出了一个极其重要的问题：

「你究竟是国家要支持的目标，还是实现目标所要付出的代价？」

这可能是理解中国经济发展模式，以及在这里做投资、生活时，最需要思考的问题之一

text:
JENSEN HUANG ZERLEGT MERZ

Der Kanzler fragt den Nvidia-Chef auf offener Bühne, wie Europa KI regulieren soll.

"Man kann nichts regulieren, wenn es die Technologie gar nicht gibt.“

Die Technologiebranche muss die Technik für Sicherheit selbst erfinden. Sicherheit besteht nicht aus Hoffnungen und Wünschen, Sicherheit ist Technik und Ingenieursarbeit. Zweitens brauchen die Unternehmen verbindliche Standards. Und erst zuletzt kommen Vorgaben von Industrie und Staat. Das Internet zu regulieren ist schwer, Internetanwendungen zu regulieren ist es nicht. Genau dort sollten wir ansetzen, bei den Anwendungen. Es gibt nichts zu regulieren, wenn die Branche nicht gedeiht. Man will doch, dass die deutsche KI-Industrie floriert, und zwar sicher und verantwortungsvoll. Wir wissen, dass wir Technik entwickeln und einsetzen können, die KI sicher macht. Wir wissen, dass wir uns als Unternehmen und als Branche an gute Standards halten können. Und wenn es dann noch nötig ist, regulieren wir."

Merz stimmte zu und verwies darauf, dass Maschinen bereits aus dem AI Act herausgenommen wurden. Ein europäischer oder globaler Rahmen sei noch weit entfernt.

text:
喵个咪，这就是硅谷最年轻亿万富豪的顶级人脉圈吗？
Alexandr Wang 随手发的一句把 HRT 帮重新聚齐了，
瞬间引爆了整个硅谷，
 一个在执掌 Meta 整个集团的 AI 大脑，
一个带着 Cognition 做出轰动全球的 AI 程序员 Devin，
一个靠着十来个人的极客团队撑起百亿级链上平台。 

很多人以为这种顶峰相见是成年后的商业抱团，其实早在高中奥赛和量化实习的泥坑里，这群怪物就已经把彼此的底牌和实力摸得一清二楚了。

这张在推特上被全网疯传为世纪合影的户外自拍，大概是今年科技界信息密度最高、但也最让人头皮发麻的一张照片hh，
三个二十多岁、穿着最普通的卫衣站在山道旁的年轻华裔，加起来几乎主导了今天全球 AI 数据基建、智能体代码生成和链上金融最核心的命脉，

但整张照片最恐怖的真相还不只是3个人的身价，而是他们三个人的起点： 整整十年前，纽约顶级量化巨头 Hudson River Trading 办了一届只有十个人的残酷实习生选拔，而今天站在镜头前的这三个人，当年全在这间十个人的屋子里不眠不休地同台较劲。

最先击碎传统职场认知的，是极客单兵作战能力的彻底重构。 左边的 Alexandr Wang 在二十多岁创立了数据巨头并直接加入 Meta 统领全盘 AI 航向；

中间的 Scott Wu 带着国际信息学奥赛三金的功底，用 Devin 掀翻了整个软件工程界；

右边的 Jeff Yan 更是只带着十来个人的超精简团队，硬生生在链上建起了一座高频金融帝国。

在过去，这种体量的业务需要成千上万的中层和几十年的官僚沉淀，而他们把这一切全部压缩进了纯粹的代码和算力里。

更耐人寻味的，是顶级同侪网络在早期形成的恐怖引力。 很多人把人脉庸俗地理解为成年后的利益置换，但翻开他们的履历就会发现，这个圈子早在高中奥林匹克竞赛的赛场上就已经咬合在一起了；

在世界还没看懂 AI 和区块链的时候，这群年轻人就已经在用最极限的数学模型和高压算法互相背书、互相启发。

这也是为什么顶级量化公司正在变成新一代科技创始人的黄埔军校。

 在那种毫秒级定生死、必须把逻辑推演到物理极限的环境里打磨过的人，一旦带着对高并发与系统架构的理解杀进 AI 领域，对传统行业几乎就是一场降维打击。

顶峰相见的背后，从来没有偶然的运气，只有早期在最高浓度的高手堆里淬炼出来的野心。

 对于今天的年轻人来说，奥赛金牌或许无法复制，但尽早跳出舒适区、去找到那些能让你感到智力压迫感的同侪，永远是拉开人生差距最快的一步。

大家在自己的成长或者职业生涯里，有没有遇到过那种一眼就让你看到自身天花板、甚至彻底重塑了你野心的顶级同伴？

我觉得如果早年遇到过一个写代码像呼吸一样自然的怪物室友，可以直接把我从自满的幻觉里一耳光抽醒哈哈哈，可能直到今天我都会感谢那场降维打击，可惜没有如果，这就是人生啊

text:
银行赚钱了，股票却跌成了 2008 年以来最长的连跌。

KBW 银行指数，已经连续跌了六周。
上一次这么长，还是 2008 年金融危机。
从九月初算，跌了大约 11%。

奇怪的是，银行财报并不差。
JPMorgan、美国银行、花旗、富国四大行，
坏账拨备比去年还少了 3%，贷款增长接近 10%。

那市场到底在怕什么？
答案是：怕利率。
10 月 7 日，美国 10 年期国债收益率一度冲到 5.365%，这是2002 年以来最高水平。

利率高，银行手里的债券浮亏变大，借钱的企业也越来越吃力。有调查显示，六成信贷经理预计未来一年违约会增加。

Barclays 还算了一笔：
九月美联储加息之后的 21 个交易日里，银行指数有 18 天跑输标普。

财报告诉"没事"，股价却破了连跌纪录。
你觉得这次下跌对银行股来说是买入的机会吗？

text:
🚨 Threat Intelligence | Analysis of the DarkSword Trojan Backend and iOS Attack Chain

Following the public release of #DarkSword-related exploit code in March 2026, DarkSword-PROV2 appeared on GitHub in July, with the attack infrastructure observed operating online in late September.

We traced the live attack infrastructure, linked its admin panels to public GitHub repositories, and analyzed the exploit code, payload library, delivery chain, and post-exploitation capabilities.

🔍 Key Findings:

🔹 A complete attack pipeline: The infrastructure integrates exploit delivery, device and data collection, data exfiltration, and crypto wallet fund consolidation.

🔹 Extensive data theft capabilities: The toolkit targets Keychain data, files, messages, and crypto wallet data, with additional capabilities for wallet data decryption and fund consolidation.

🔹 Broader claimed coverage, narrower functional coverage: Although the toolkit claims support for iOS 13 and later, code analysis identifies two functional exploit windows: iOS 18.6–18.7.2 and iOS 26.0–26.1. Many other version entries remain incomplete or unverified.

🔹 Public code weaponized: Publicly available exploit components have been integrated into a deployable attack framework, lowering the barrier to launching sophisticated #iOS attacks.

🛡️ Recommendations

Keep iOS updated and avoid untrusted links. Simply opening a malicious page in #Safari may trigger exploitation.

If a device has visited a suspicious landing page, treat its seed phrases and private keys as potentially compromised. Use a device that has never accessed the page to create a new wallet and transfer your assets. Also check for abnormal transactions and token approvals across chains, and revoke unnecessary approvals.

🔗 Read the full analysis: https://t.co/B1hYr9mGl5

author: markjeffrey
quoted_text:
Goodbye owner emissions, and thank you for the support. We've moved to 0% owner, 50% validator, 50% miner splits.

We believe removing owner emissions is part of a subnet’s maturation. Once you’ve built a stable & fair incentive mechanism, you can compete within it yourself. 

That’s where we are with SN8. Anyone can provide trading intelligence to the network through an individual miner or an entity miner. We’ll compete by running an entity miner, and we see that as our future. Individual miners earn alpha for the PnL they contribute to the network. Entity miners, including prop firms, earn through profit splits with the traders they fund, with the shared goal of producing the network’s best risk-adjusted PnL.

We’ll keep building SN8 without owner emissions. APY from our existing holdings will fund subnet features and improvements. We’ll rely on mining emissions and Vanta Trading’s ability to compete to fund our continued growth on VT. As we have in the past, we’ll use specific wallets for Vanta Trading sales and any owner emissions, so the associated spending is easy to track.

Our goal is to grow the network to thousands of miners. We built SN8 to be more than a network where we’re the main competitor. There are many individual miners and entities already running on the network. With Null Consensus, we want to grow that exponentially. More miners will be able to join with the right rails, making it simpler to get started: USDC in, miner running.

As more miners join, we expect more network weight to flow to miners, bringing more trading intelligence and creating more capacity to meet demand for funding. That demand can generate further revenue for the subnet through copy trading.

We see this as the natural progression of a subnet, and believe SN8 is ready to begin that transition. It may take time, and there may be hiccups along the way. Our expectation is that, gradually, miners will receive 100% of the network’s weight. We’re starting that transition by moving our own owner to provide a bigger split to miners & our holders.

quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

THIS NEEDS TO BE ASKED.
The Japan program continues to publicly report high levels of success and confidence in its treatment.
But how many patients have now experienced initial improvement followed by significant decline or relapse?
April is now publicly documenting exactly that concern — including her pre- and post-treatment labs, worsening symptoms, and serious procedural complication.
This is the pattern I warned about before others went to Japan: short-term improvement is not the same thing as sustained recovery.
So where is the long-term follow-up data?
30 days? 90 days? 6 months? One year?
If high success rates are being claimed, patients deserve to know how "success" is defined and how many people remain improved months later.
April is putting her own results on the table.
Now let's see all the data.
author: TheMessengerDan
quoted_text:
Considering Japan for Vx injury or LC? Update on my journey: 
I wanted to share an update because quite a bit has changed since I returned from Japan.

Unfortunately, my health has continued to decline. Recent immune testing has shown that my immunodeficiency is more significant than we originally understood, including inadequate protective antibody responses to pneumococcal bacteria. My autoimmune markers remain elevated, and more recent testing also shows increasing inflammatory activity.

At the same time, the neuropathy has continued to worsen. The burning pain and numbness are spreading, and my headaches have become significantly worse. Because of the headaches and my existing cervical instability and vascular issues, further vascular imaging of my neck and brain may be needed to evaluate for additional compression.

This week I am traveling back to Utah, where much of my specialty medical team is located, for my first two IVIG (intravenous immunoglobulin, made from pooled donor plasma) infusions on back-to-back days. These treatments will be given in an infusion center. My physicians hope IVIG may help address the antibody deficiency and potentially some of the immune-mediated inflammation and neuropathy as well.

I have also connected with members of the React19 community who have experienced substantial improvement with IVIG. Their experiences give me some hope while also reminding me that everyone responds differently.

Travel adds another layer of expense—gas, food, medical costs and the trip itself—but thankfully I will be able to stay with family, so lodging is covered.

Another big change has been accepting that I need a motorized wheelchair.

I fought that reality for a long time. I can no longer make the short distance to our mailbox or walk through a grocery store. Buying the chair felt like admitting something I wasn't ready to admit.

But it has also given something back to me. Special thanks to Kelsey for helping me see this and allow me to test drive your wheel;)

I can be outside with Brew, Greg and Kai. I was able to accompany Kai on his first day of school. Those moments matter more than I can explain.

The chair represents loss, but it has also allowed me to participate in pieces of my family's life again.

I also want to give a very honest and objective update about the treatment I underwent in Japan, particularly for people who may currently be considering going.

Before I left, Dr. Jordan Vaughn, my naturopath Dr. Costa, and my immunologist Dr. Jones intentionally ordered extensive laboratory testing so that we would have objective data to compare before and after treatment.

Relevant testing was performed before Japan on March 18 and July 15, 2026. Post-treatment testing was performed after my return on August 25, with additional redraws on September 10 when several specimens—including MMP-9—could not be adequately processed from the earlier draws.

One of my goals in going to Japan was not only to get better, but to determine whether the treatment produced measurable changes that might help validate the program and potentially help other people with Long COVID.

So far, the opposite of what I hoped to document has occurred.

My post-treatment testing has not shown the objective improvement I hoped to see. Instead, several inflammatory markers we were following before treatment have increased, and several cytokines that had previously been below the laboratory cutoff are now elevated.

For example, comparing the most recent valid pre-treatment values from July with my September 10 post-treatment testing:

• IL-12 increased from 4.7 to 9.9 pg/mL.
• IL-5 increased from <2.1 to 3.3 pg/mL and is now elevated.
• IL-17 increased from <1.4 to 1.7 pg/mL and is now elevated.
• TNF-alpha increased from 6.0 to 16.0 pg/mL and is now elevated.
• TGF-β1 increased from 12,367 to 33,676 pg/mL and is now above the laboratory reference range.
• MMP-9, which was already elevated at 1,283 ng/mL before Japan, increased further to 1,519 ng/mL.
Some of the planned July 15 and August 25 specimens were insufficient for certain tests, which is why the September 10 redraws were necessary. For those markers, I am comparing the September results with the most recent valid pre-Japan measurements rather than pretending we have data points that we do not.
These are not simply changes in how I feel. They are measurable laboratory findings that my medical team and I intentionally tracked before and after treatment.
At the same time, clinically, my neuropathy, burning pain, numbness, headaches and overall function have continued to decline.
I want to be equally clear about what these results do NOT prove.
They do not establish that the treatments in Japan caused these changes. Long COVID is complicated, laboratory values can fluctuate, and there are many potential variables.

What I can say is that my own objective pre- and post-treatment data have not demonstrated the improvement I went to Japan hoping to document. In several areas, the measurable trend has instead moved in the opposite direction.

The treatment itself was also not without significant risk. My central-line placement resulted in a pneumothorax requiring hospitalization and a chest tube.

Since August, I have personally spoken with several patients who initially experienced improvement after treatment and later experienced relapsing symptoms, in some cases within only a few months of completing treatment. This is information I wish I had understood more clearly before making my decision.

Knowing what I know now—including my clinical course, the complication I experienced, the pre- and post-treatment laboratory findings, and what I have since learned from other patients—I would NOT make the same decision to go.

I feel a responsibility to say that clearly for anyone currently considering this experiment.

I believe patients deserve to understand not only the possibility of improvement, but also the procedural risks, the uncertainty surrounding durability of response, and the possibility that symptoms may return even after an initial improvement.

I went to Japan hoping not only to improve my own health, but also to gather information that might help other people suffering from Long COVID.

I genuinely hoped my pre- and post-treatment testing would help validate the program.

Being transparent when the results do not support what I hoped to find is part of that responsibility too.

Meanwhile, Greg is still unemployed following the layoffs that affected him and his team. He is looking for work every day—networking, contacting leads, applying, and doing everything he can to find the right opportunity. It has made an already difficult financial situation even harder.

I know these are difficult economic times for so many people. I never take a donation, share, message, prayer, or offer of help for granted. We are deeply grateful. I certainly don't want anyone to suffer hardship because of me.

If anyone has unused airline miles or travel points and would be willing to use them toward one of my medical trips, that could also be tremendously helpful as travel to specialists continues.

For anyone who prefers Venmo:
@april-amber-theisen

Go Fund Me:
https://t.co/fCbHTYK0Zg
https://t.co/Sv478VGV8X

Thank you for continuing to stand beside our family.

I am still searching for answers, still following the data—even when it isn't the answer I hoped for—and still hoping that some combination of science, persistence and time will give me more of my life back.

人類が主役だった地質年代（人新世）が，AIの台頭によって極めて短い期間で幕を閉じるかもしれない ——そんな前提のもと，提示されたデータは強烈です。

■ 突きつけられた冷徹なファクト
モデル訓練の計算量は過去10年で約1000万倍に増加し，人間の脳が生涯で行う総計算量に迫っている。AIが単独で完遂できるタスクの時間スケールは，数ヶ月ごとに倍増している。ここ7ヶ月ほど，モデルは数学者が長年解けなかった未解決の「Erdős（エルデシュ）問題」を解き始めている。サンフランシスコでは「長いタイムライン（懐疑派）」とは「AGIは10年以内に来る」を意味している。2030年の計算量は2025年の約1万倍に達する見込み。
線形グラフで見れば，現在の劇的な進歩すら「まだゼロと区別がつかない平坦な初期段階にいる」というのが彼の主張です。

■ 学生たちへのシンプルで容赦ないアドバイス
毎日AIを使え。指数関数の上にいれば，遅れを取ることはない。彼自身はClaudeを「実行力は天才だが、研究のセンスはかなり悪い大学院生」のように毎日使い，自分ではもうコードを一切書いていない。

計算量がスケールするほど良くなるプロジェクトを選べ。それ以外は，完成する前に解かれてしまう サットンの『苦い教訓』の通り，スケールに味方されるテーマを選ばなければ，2年かけた研究も完成する頃には次世代モデルのプロンプト一発で追い抜かれる。

キャリアを「安定したもの」として計画するのをやめろ。安全な選択肢は，もはや安全を買ってくれない 社会全体で大規模な破壊が起きるなら，ベースラインのリスク自体が高い。従来の「手堅い選択肢」は，もはや安全を担保してくれず，ただ潜在的なリターンを犠牲にするだけになる。

そして，最も印象的な一言がこれ。

「書くことは考えることだ（Writing is thinking）。書くことを外注すれば，考えることも外注することになる。」

コーディングや実行は徹底的にAIへ委譲しつつ，問題設定（センス）と思考の核（書くこと）だけは決して手放すな。 AGIのタイムラインを本気で信じているなら，キャリアの計画も本気でそれに合わせろという，極めてストレートなメッセージの講演を紹介しました。 https://t.co/OzIQFphOeG

text:
今天开始认真的优化套利程序的滑点问题. 结果发现好像还挺复杂的, 查了一些开源的交易引擎, 也并没有做的很好.
求教:
1. 我只订阅了订单薄, 但是量比较大, 大概是全部交易所的 perp + spot, 比如币安是 20depth@100ms. 然后对于订单的 content age 设置了 200ms 的过期阈值
2. 我目前的 2 笔对冲交易模型是 HOF (hedge on fill), 第一笔先用 IOC + 0.15% 滑点成交以后, 第二笔发 market 订单
3. 观察到的问题有, 第一条腿的 IOC 订单经常会无法成交, market 订单有时候滑点很差
4. 今天优化的时候, 发现同时订阅 BBO 用来做辅助过滤以后, 可以过滤掉很多之前的这种“失效订单薄”. 因为 BBO 更新比 OB 要快不少
5. 但是一台机器, 同时订阅 OB 和 BBO, 不管是 CPU 还是流量都搞不定啊
求教有啥好办法吗? AI 反复建议我两条腿都改成 IOC, 但是这个一方面会导致两条腿都部分成交, 要额外的处理腿不平衡问题, 另外就是, 这个不解决本质问题, 只是将滑点大的 market 单换成了可能不成交的 IOC. 一旦不成交, 我不管是 rollback 第一条腿, 还是继续补第二条腿, 我觉得一样会吃到磨损, 不见得有什么优势.

text:
After rejection after rejection, a job seeker built a Claude skill that runs the whole job hunt for them.

Paste a job posting and Kitty:
→ scores the fit (level, must-haves, location, salary) and tells you if it's worth applying
→ tailors your CV to the role and shows every change before touching anything
→ never invents experience: if the posting asks for SQL and your CV doesn't mention it, Kitty asks you first
→ checks your page limit by rendering the CV to PDF
→ logs every application in Notion or a spreadsheet
→ reads your Gmail on a schedule and updates each application when you get an interview or a rejection
→ shows which roles actually convert to interviews

Your original CV is never edited, only a copy.

Install: download https://t.co/2KTWGIUlY0 from the repo and upload it as a skill in the Claude app or Cowork. For Claude Code, unzip it into ~/.claude/skills/. Then say "hello kitty".

It also meows now and then, and gives you a cat fact when the search gets rough.

MIT.

author: erichsu_eth
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

Mert explains why Zcash is one of the best-positioned cryptocurrencies to handle quantum computing threats

“The first reason is because Zcash is very limited in scope”

“It's literally just a store of value. It's not programmable in the same way that an Ethereum is. It just does one thing and it does it really well and so the risk is reduced”

“This is also why I'm against shielded assets in terms of stablecoins on Zcash or something, is because we want to minimize the risk surface”

“This is also the exact reason why Zcash, even like a year and a half to two years ago, we were talking about how it's the best positioned for quantum”

“Having the best cryptographers in crypto sort of has its benefits in that these people are constantly thinking about these theoretical risks”

“It's going to be much easier when you have limited scope and you built the entire network with sort of these edge cases in mind to begin with”

text:
This never ends WELL.

5 of history's biggest stock market bubbles all ended in a crash or a recession.

Today, the 41 stocks JPMorgan classifies as AI-related make up 49% of the S&P 500.

That's higher than every one of those bubbles except the 1880s railroads.

Here's how each of them ended:

- Railroads, 63% in 1881: the US fell into the Depression of 1882 to 1885

- Roaring Twenties, 36% in 1929: the Dow fell 89% by 1932 and took 25 years to recover

- Nifty Fifty, 40% in 1972: the S&P 500 fell 48% in 1973 and 1974

- Japan, 44% in 1988: the Nikkei peaked a year later, lost over 80% and took 34 years to recover

- Dot-com, 41% in 2000: the Nasdaq fell 78% and took 15 years to recover

That's 15, 25 and 34 years for those indexes to reclaim their peaks.

Meanwhile, Bianco Research says AI would already be 51% of the S&P 500 if SpaceX were included.

"The last time a single theme was >50% of the $SPX was the railroads in the 19th century," the firm adds.

The 88 Edge and the State of Root Reborn

TL;DR: 88 Root is clearly outperforming.

Root Reborn's active weight setting began on Aug 27, followed by active rebalancing. We've compiled a performance chart of 88 Root alongside major root validators, using lifetime performance data from @Taostats. 88 Root tops the chart.

Two starting dates are provided for context. 88 Root began as an sn88 validator on Aug 16 and did not become a root validator across all 128 subnets until Sep 3. Its performance data during the interim period is largely noise from a single subnet.

While we expect 88 Root to continue outperforming, the tight guardrails on active rebalancing leave limited room for short-term performance differentiation. The 2% price band restriction makes it nearly impossible to enter or exit fast-moving subnets. The 10% daily turnover limit means a full rebalance can take days or even weeks. On the other hand, these restrictions do help prevent manipulation and mitigate risk. Root has always been about risk-free yield after all.

As the 88 alpha edge becomes more evident over time, we also expect and welcome healthy competition from fellow validators. Many are clearly run by talented teams.

Meanwhile, the unrestricted alpha edge remains in the 88 Quant Fund. Despite the still-anemic market, we're preparing to reopen the fund soon.

Stay tuned. #SN88 #Bittensor $TAO 🚀

quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

US Long/Short Net Leverage at 43.7%, a Five-Year Low; Fell 3.2pts Last Week, Largest Drop Since Liberation Day

@GoldmanSachs prime brokerage data shows US long/short net leverage fell 3.2 points last week, the largest weekly decline since Liberation Day and the fourth-largest over the past five years. 

Essentially all of the net exposure reduction since end of July has come from an increase in shorts, not a reduction in longs. 

Short exposure is now near five-year highs while long exposure remains in the 53rd percentile over the past three years and the 72nd percentile over five years.

That means long books haven't been meaningfully reduced yet. If performance pressure continues, there's scope for further de-grossing through long sales alongside short covering.
